text.original: فَصْلٌ: إِذَا تَنَازَعَ الْفِعْلَانِ فِي اسْمٍ ظَاهِرٍ بَعْدَهُمَا، أَيْ أَرَادَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنَ الْفِعْلَيْنِ أَنْ يَعْمَلَ فِي ذَلِكَ الِاسْمِ، فَهَذَا إِنَّمَا يَكُونُ عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْسَامٍ: الْأَوَّلُ أَنْ يَتَنَازَعَا فِي الْفَاعِلِيَّةِ فَقَطْ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمَنِي زَيْدٌ، الثَّانِي أَنْ يَتَنَازَعَا فِي الْمَفْعُولِيَّةِ فَقَطْ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُ زَيْدًا، الثَّالِثُ أَنْ يَتَنَازَعَا فِي الْفَاعِلِيَّةِ وَالْمَفْعُولِيَّةِ وَيَقْتَضِيَ الْأَوَّلُ الْفَاعِلَ وَالثَّانِي الْمَفْعُولَ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمْتُ زَيْدًا، الرَّابِعُ عَكْسُهُ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمَنِي زَيْدٌ.
text.en: Section. When two verbs contend (tanāzuʿ) for an explicit noun after them, that is, each of the two verbs wants to govern that noun, this happens in four kinds only. The first: that they contend only for being the fāʿil, as ḍarabanī wa-akramanī Zaydun “Zayd hit me and honoured me”. The second: that they contend only for being the mafʿūl, as ḍarabtu wa-akramtu Zaydan “I hit and honoured Zayd”. The third: that they contend for being the fāʿil and the mafʿūl, the first requiring the fāʿil and the second the mafʿūl, as ḍarabanī wa-akramtu Zaydan “he hit me, and I honoured Zayd”. The fourth is the reverse, as ḍarabtu wa-akramanī Zaydun “I hit [him], and Zayd honoured me”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ فِي جَمِيعِ هَذِهِ الْأَقْسَامِ يَجُوزُ إِعْمَالُ الْفِعْلِ الْأَوَّلِ وَإِعْمَالُ الْفِعْلِ الثَّانِي، خِلَافًا لِلْفَرَّاءِ فِي الصُّورَةِ الْأُولَى وَالثَّالِثَةِ إِنْ أُعْمِلَ الثَّانِي، وَدَلِيلُهُ لُزُومُ أَحَدِ الْأَمْرَيْنِ: إِمَّا حَذْفُ الْفَاعِلِ، أَوِ الْإِضْمَارُ قَبْلَ الذِّكْرِ، وَكِلَاهُمَا مَحْذُورَانِ، وَهَذَا فِي الْجَوَازِ. وَأَمَّا الِاخْتِيَارُ فَفِيهِ خِلَافُ الْبَصْرِيِّينَ، فَإِنَّهُمْ يَخْتَارُونَ إِعْمَالَ الْفِعْلِ الثَّانِي اعْتِبَارًا لِلْقُرْبِ وَالْجِوَارِ، وَالْكُوفِيُّونَ يَخْتَارُونَ إِعْمَالَ الْفِعْلِ الْأَوَّلِ مُرَاعَاةً لِلتَّقْدِيمِ وَالِاسْتِحْقَاقِ.
text.en: Know that in all these kinds it is allowed to let the first verb govern and to let the second verb govern — against al-Farrāʾ in the first and the third case, if the second is made to govern; his proof is that one of two things then follows, either the dropping of the fāʿil or a pronoun before [its noun is] mentioned, and both are to be avoided. This is as to what is allowed. As to what is preferred, the Baṣrans differ [from the Kūfans]: they prefer to let the second verb govern, in regard to nearness and neighbourhood, while the Kūfans prefer to let the first verb govern, in respect for its coming first and its right.

text.original: فَإِنْ أَعْمَلْتَ الثَّانِيَ فَانْظُرْ: إِنْ كَانَ الْفِعْلُ الْأَوَّلُ يَقْتَضِي الْفَاعِلَ أَضْمَرْتَ الْفَاعِلَ فِي الْأَوَّلِ، كَمَا تَقُولُ فِي الْمُتَوَافِقَيْنِ: ضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمَنِي زَيْدٌ، وَضَرَبَانِي وَأَكْرَمَنِي الزَّيْدَانِ، وَضَرَبُونِي وَأَكْرَمَنِي الزَّيْدُونَ، وَفِي الْمُتَخَالِفَيْنِ: ضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمْتُ زَيْدًا، وَضَرَبَانِي وَأَكْرَمْتُ الزَّيْدَيْنِ، وَضَرَبُونِي وَأَكْرَمْتُ الزَّيْدِينَ.
text.en: If you let the second govern, look: if the first verb requires the fāʿil, you put the fāʿil in the first as a pronoun, as you say with verbs that agree ḍarabanī wa-akramanī Zaydun “he hit me, and Zayd honoured me”, ḍarabānī wa-akramanī al-Zaydāni “they two hit me, and the two Zayds honoured me” and ḍarabūnī wa-akramanī al-Zaydūna “they hit me, and the Zayds honoured me”; and with verbs that differ ḍarabanī wa-akramtu Zaydan “he hit me, and I honoured Zayd”, ḍarabānī wa-akramtu al-Zaydayni “they two hit me, and I honoured the two Zayds” and ḍarabūnī wa-akramtu al-Zaydīna “they hit me, and I honoured the Zayds”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ الْفِعْلُ الْأَوَّلُ يَقْتَضِي الْمَفْعُولَ وَلَمْ يَكُنِ الْفِعْلَانِ مِنْ أَفْعَالِ الْقُلُوبِ حَذَفْتَ الْمَفْعُولَ مِنَ الْفِعْلِ الْأَوَّلِ، كَمَا تَقُولُ فِي الْمُتَوَافِقَيْنِ: ضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُ زَيْدًا، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُ الزَّيْدَيْنِ، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُ الزَّيْدِينَ، وَفِي الْمُتَخَالِفَيْنِ: ضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمَنِي زَيْدٌ، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمَنِي الزَّيْدَانِ، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمَنِي الزَّيْدُونَ.
text.en: If the first verb requires the mafʿūl, and the two verbs are not verbs of the heart, you drop the mafʿūl of the first verb, as you say with verbs that agree ḍarabtu wa-akramtu Zaydan “I hit and honoured Zayd”, ḍarabtu wa-akramtu al-Zaydayni “I hit and honoured the two Zayds” and ḍarabtu wa-akramtu al-Zaydīna “I hit and honoured the Zayds”; and with verbs that differ ḍarabtu wa-akramanī Zaydun “I hit, and Zayd honoured me”, ḍarabtu wa-akramanī al-Zaydāni “I hit, and the two Zayds honoured me” and ḍarabtu wa-akramanī al-Zaydūna “I hit, and the Zayds honoured me”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ الْفِعْلَانِ مِنْ أَفْعَالِ الْقُلُوبِ يَجِبُ إِظْهَارُ الْمَفْعُولِ لِلْفِعْلِ الْأَوَّلِ، كَمَا تَقُولُ: حَسِبَنِي مُنْطَلِقًا وَحَسِبْتُ زَيْدًا مُنْطَلِقًا؛ إِذْ لَا يَجُوزُ حَذْفُ الْمَفْعُولِ مِنْ أَفْعَالِ الْقُلُوبِ، وَلَا إِضْمَارُ الْمَفْعُولِ قَبْلَ الذِّكْرِ. هَذَا هُوَ مَذْهَبُ الْبَصْرِيِّينَ.
text.en: If the two verbs are verbs of the heart, the mafʿūl of the first verb must be expressed, as you say ḥasibanī munṭaliqan wa-ḥasibtu Zaydan munṭaliqan “he thought me departing, and I thought Zayd departing”; for the mafʿūl may not be dropped from the verbs of the heart, nor may the mafʿūl be a pronoun before [its noun is] mentioned. This is the school of the Baṣrans.

lessons.title: Contention: the Kūfan way; the verbs of the heart
body: The Kūfan way: the first verb governs the noun. If the second verb wants a fāʿil, a pronoun is put in it: ḍarabanī wa-akramanī Zaydun; ḍarabanī wa-akramānī al-Zaydāni; ḍarabanī wa-akramūnī al-Zaydūna. With verbs that differ, the noun takes the iʿrāb the first verb gives: ḍarabtu wa-akramanī Zaydan, “I hit Zayd, and he honoured me”, with Zaydan as the object of ḍarabtu. The noun belongs to the first verb, which comes first, so the pronoun in the second refers to a noun already in its place.

If the second verb wants an object, and they are not verbs of the heart, two ways are allowed: to drop the object, or to put it as a pronoun, “and the second is preferred, so that what is spoken agrees with what is meant”. Dropped: ḍarabtu wa-akramtu Zaydan; with verbs that differ, ḍarabanī wa-akramtu Zaydun, “Zayd hit me, and I honoured him”. As a pronoun: ḍarabtu wa-akramtuhu Zaydan; ḍarabanī wa-akramtuhu Zaydun.

With verbs of the heart the object must be expressed: ḥasibanī wa-ḥasibtuhumā munṭaliqayni al-Zaydāni munṭaliqan, “the two Zayds thought me departing, and I thought them departing”. The two verbs contended for munṭaliqan, their second object. The first, ḥasibanī, governs: al-Zaydāni is its fāʿil and munṭaliqan its second object. The second verb, ḥasibtuhumā, has its first object in humā, and its second object, munṭaliqayni, is spoken out.

Why must it be spoken out? The book closes every other door. Drop munṭaliqayni, and ḥasibtuhumā is left with one object, which a verb of the heart may not have. Put a singular pronoun, iyyāhu, and the second object does not agree with the first, humā. Put a dual pronoun, iyyāhumā, and a dual pronoun would refer to a singular word, munṭaliqan. “And when dropping and the pronoun are not allowed, expressing it is necessary.”
This is how the madrasa argues: list every possible way, show why each but one fails, and the one left is the rule. A student who can follow this paragraph can follow the Kāfiya's commentaries.

expressing the object in full, as a noun

tasks.prompt: Parse ḍarabtu wa-akramanī Zaydan the Kūfan way.
tasks.answer: The first verb, ḍarabtu, governs Zaydan as its object (in naṣb). The second, akramanī, wants a fāʿil, so a pronoun is put in it, hidden, referring to Zayd; the yāʾ is its object.

tasks.prompt: Give both ways the book allows for the second verb's object, and say which is preferred and why.
tasks.answer: Dropping it, ḍarabtu wa-akramtu Zaydan, or putting it as a pronoun, ḍarabtu wa-akramtuhu Zaydan. The pronoun is preferred, so that what is spoken agrees with what is meant.

tasks.prompt: In ḥasibanī wa-ḥasibtuhumā munṭaliqayni al-Zaydāni munṭaliqan, give the fāʿil and the two objects of each verb.
tasks.answer: Ḥasibanī: fāʿil al-Zaydāni, first object the yāʾ, second object munṭaliqan. Ḥasibtuhumā: fāʿil the tāʾ, first object humā, second object munṭaliqayni.

tasks.prompt: Why may munṭaliqayni be neither dropped nor replaced by iyyāhu or iyyāhumā?
tasks.answer: Dropped, it would leave a verb of the heart with one object, which is not allowed. Iyyāhu, singular, would not agree with the first object humā. Iyyāhumā, dual, would refer to the singular word munṭaliqan. So it must be expressed.

quiz.prompt: In the Kūfan way, which verb governs the noun?
quiz.explanation: For its coming first and its right.

text.original: وَأَمَّا إِنْ أَعْمَلْتَ الْفِعْلَ الْأَوَّلَ عَلَى مَذْهَبِ الْكُوفِيِّينَ فَانْظُرْ: إِنْ كَانَ الْفِعْلُ الثَّانِي يَقْتَضِي الْفَاعِلَ أَضْمَرْتَ الْفَاعِلَ فِي الْفِعْلِ الثَّانِي، كَمَا تَقُولُ فِي الْمُتَوَافِقَيْنِ: ضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمَنِي زَيْدٌ، وَضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمَانِي الزَّيْدَانِ، وَضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمُونِي الزَّيْدُونَ، وَفِي الْمُتَخَالِفَيْنِ: ضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمَنِي زَيْدًا، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمَانِي الزَّيْدَيْنِ، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمُونِي الزَّيْدِينَ.
text.en: But if you let the first verb govern, by the school of the Kūfans, look: if the second verb requires the fāʿil, you put the fāʿil in the second verb as a pronoun, as you say with verbs that agree ḍarabanī wa-akramanī Zaydun “Zayd hit me, and he honoured me”, ḍarabanī wa-akramānī al-Zaydāni “the two Zayds hit me, and they honoured me” and ḍarabanī wa-akramūnī al-Zaydūna “the Zayds hit me, and they honoured me”; and with verbs that differ ḍarabtu wa-akramanī Zaydan “I hit Zayd, and he honoured me”, ḍarabtu wa-akramānī al-Zaydayni “I hit the two Zayds, and they honoured me” and ḍarabtu wa-akramūnī al-Zaydīna “I hit the Zayds, and they honoured me”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ الْفِعْلُ الثَّانِي يَقْتَضِي الْمَفْعُولَ وَلَمْ يَكُنِ الْفِعْلَانِ مِنْ أَفْعَالِ الْقُلُوبِ جَازَ فِيهِ الْوَجْهَانِ: حَذْفُ الْمَفْعُولِ، وَالْإِضْمَارُ، وَالثَّانِي هُوَ الْمُخْتَارُ؛ لِيَكُونَ الْمَلْفُوظُ مُطَابِقًا لِلْمُرَادِ. أَمَّا الْحَذْفُ فَكَمَا تَقُولُ فِي الْمُتَوَافِقَيْنِ: ضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُ زَيْدًا، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُ الزَّيْدَيْنِ، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُ الزَّيْدِينَ، وَفِي الْمُتَخَالِفَيْنِ: ضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمْتُ زَيْدٌ، وَضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمْتُ الزَّيْدَانِ، وَضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمْتُ الزَّيْدُونَ.
text.en: If the second verb requires the mafʿūl, and the two verbs are not verbs of the heart, two ways are allowed in it, dropping the mafʿūl and [putting it as] a pronoun; the second is preferred, so that what is spoken agrees with what is meant. Dropping is as you say with verbs that agree ḍarabtu wa-akramtu Zaydan “I hit Zayd, and I honoured [him]”, ḍarabtu wa-akramtu al-Zaydayni and ḍarabtu wa-akramtu al-Zaydīna; and with verbs that differ ḍarabanī wa-akramtu Zaydun “Zayd hit me, and I honoured [him]”, ḍarabanī wa-akramtu al-Zaydāni and ḍarabanī wa-akramtu al-Zaydūna.

text.original: وَأَمَّا الْإِضْمَارُ فَكَمَا تَقُولُ فِي الْمُتَوَافِقَيْنِ: ضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُهُ زَيْدًا، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُهُمَا الزَّيْدَيْنِ، وَضَرَبْتُ وَأَكْرَمْتُهُمُ الزَّيْدِينَ، وَفِي الْمُتَخَالِفَيْنِ: ضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمْتُهُ زَيْدٌ، وَضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمْتُهُمَا الزَّيْدَانِ، وَضَرَبَنِي وَأَكْرَمْتُهُمُ الزَّيْدُونَ.
text.en: [Putting it as] a pronoun is as you say with verbs that agree ḍarabtu wa-akramtuhu Zaydan “I hit Zayd, and I honoured him”, ḍarabtu wa-akramtuhumā al-Zaydayni and ḍarabtu wa-akramtuhumu al-Zaydīna; and with verbs that differ ḍarabanī wa-akramtuhu Zaydun “Zayd hit me, and I honoured him”, ḍarabanī wa-akramtuhumā al-Zaydāni and ḍarabanī wa-akramtuhumu al-Zaydūna.

text.original: وَأَمَّا إِذَا كَانَ الْفِعْلَانِ مِنْ أَفْعَالِ الْقُلُوبِ فَلَا بُدَّ مِنْ إِظْهَارِ الْمَفْعُولِ، كَمَا تَقُولُ: حَسِبَنِي وَحَسِبْتُهُمَا مُنْطَلِقَيْنِ الزَّيْدَانِ مُنْطَلِقًا؛ وَذَلِكَ لِأَنَّ حَسِبَنِي وَحَسِبْتُهُمَا تَنَازَعَا فِي مُنْطَلِقًا، وَأَعْمَلْتَ الْأَوَّلَ، وَهُوَ حَسِبَنِي، وَأَظْهَرْتَ الْمَفْعُولَ فِي الثَّانِي.
text.en: But when the two verbs are verbs of the heart, the mafʿūl must be expressed, as you say ḥasibanī wa-ḥasibtuhumā munṭaliqayni al-Zaydāni munṭaliqan “the two Zayds thought me departing, and I thought them departing”; for ḥasibanī and ḥasibtuhumā contended for munṭaliqan, and you let the first, ḥasibanī, govern, and expressed the mafʿūl in the second.

text.original: فَإِنْ حَذَفْتَ مُنْطَلِقَيْنِ وَقُلْتَ: حَسِبَنِي وَحَسِبْتُهُمَا الزَّيْدَانِ مُنْطَلِقًا، يَلْزَمُ الِاقْتِصَارُ عَلَى أَحَدِ الْمَفْعُولَيْنِ فِي أَفْعَالِ الْقُلُوبِ، وَهُوَ غَيْرُ جَائِزٍ. وَإِنْ أَضْمَرْتَ فَلَا يَخْلُو مِنْ أَنْ تُضْمِرَ مُفْرَدًا وَتَقُولَ: حَسِبَنِي وَحَسِبْتُهُمَا إِيَّاهُ الزَّيْدَانِ مُنْطَلِقًا، وَحِينَئِذٍ لَا يَكُونُ الْمَفْعُولُ الثَّانِي مُطَابِقًا لِلْمَفْعُولِ الْأَوَّلِ الَّذِي هُوَ هُمَا فِي قَوْلِكَ: حَسِبْتُهُمَا، وَلَا يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ.
text.en: If you drop munṭaliqayni and say ḥasibanī wa-ḥasibtuhumā al-Zaydāni munṭaliqan, it follows that one of the two mafʿūls of a verb of the heart is left alone, and that is not allowed. If you put a pronoun, then either you put a singular pronoun and say ḥasibanī wa-ḥasibtuhumā iyyāhu al-Zaydāni munṭaliqan, and then the second mafʿūl does not agree with the first mafʿūl, which is humā in your saying ḥasibtuhumā, and that is not allowed;

text.original: أَوْ أَنْ تُضْمِرَ مُثَنًّى وَتَقُولَ: حَسِبَنِي وَحَسِبْتُهُمَا إِيَّاهُمَا الزَّيْدَانِ مُنْطَلِقًا، وَحِينَئِذٍ يَلْزَمُ عَوْدُ الضَّمِيرِ الْمُثَنَّى إِلَى اللَّفْظِ الْمُفْرَدِ، وَهُوَ مُنْطَلِقًا الَّذِي وَقَعَ فِيهِ التَّنَازُعُ، وَهَذَا أَيْضًا لَا يَجُوزُ. وَإِذَا لَمْ يَجُزِ الْحَذْفُ وَالْإِضْمَارُ كَمَا عَرَفْتَ وَجَبَ الْإِظْهَارُ.
text.en: or you put a dual pronoun and say ḥasibanī wa-ḥasibtuhumā iyyāhumā al-Zaydāni munṭaliqan, and then it follows that a dual pronoun refers to a singular word, namely munṭaliqan, over which the contention arose; and this too is not allowed. And when dropping and the pronoun are not allowed, as you have learned, expressing [the mafʿūl] is necessary.

lessons.title: The object whose doer is not named; the mubtadaʾ and the khabar
lessons.arabic: مَفْعُولُ مَا لَمْ يُسَمَّ فَاعِلُهُ وَالْمُبْتَدَأُ وَالْخَبَرُ
lessons.transliteration: mafʿūl mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu wa-l-mubtadaʾ wa-l-khabar
body: The second marfūʿ is “every mafʿūl whose fāʿil has been dropped and which has been put in its place”: ḍuriba Zaydun. Everything learned about the verb with its fāʿil holds for it: the verb is singular with an explicit noun, it agrees with a pronoun, and it is feminine on the same conditions. So ḍuribat Hindun, as qāmat Hindun.

The mubtadaʾ and the khabar are “two nouns free of the spoken governors”: one is that of which something is said (musnad ilayhi), the mubtadaʾ, and the other that which is said (musnad bihi), the khabar: Zaydun qāʾimun. “The governor in them is abstract: it is the ibtidāʾ”, the noun's being placed at the beginning, free of any governor. The book takes the view that this one abstract governor raises both.

The base of the mubtadaʾ is to be definite, and of the khabar to be indefinite: one speaks of what the hearer knows and tells him what he does not. But an indefinite may be the mubtadaʾ when it is qualified, wa-la-ʿabdun muʾminun khayrun min mushrikin (Q 2:221), or made particular in another way. The book's examples give the ways: a question with am, a-rajulun fī al-dāri ami imraʾatun, where the speaker knows that one of the two is there; a negation, mā aḥadun khayrun minka, which takes in every one; sharrun aharra dhā nābin, which the commentators read as “only an evil made the fanged one snarl”; the khabar an adverb put first, fī al-dāri rajulun; and a prayer, salāmun ʿalayka.

If one noun is definite and the other indefinite, the definite is the mubtadaʾ and the indefinite the khabar, “always”. If both are definite, either may be the mubtadaʾ: Allāhu ilāhunā, Muḥammadun nabiyyunā, Ādamu abūnā.

terms.en: the noun of which something is said, free of spoken governors
what is said of the mubtadaʾ
being placed at the beginning: the abstract governor of both
an indefinite made particular, which may be a mubtadaʾ

examples.en: the object put in the place of the dropped fāʿil
an indefinite mubtadaʾ qualified (Q 2:221)
an indefinite mubtadaʾ in a prayer

examples.arabic: اللَّهُ إِلَهُنَا، وَمُحَمَّدٌ نَبِيُّنَا، وَآدَمُ أَبُونَا
examples.en: both definite: either may be the mubtadaʾ

tasks.prompt: Make the verb agree as the book's rules require: ḍuriba Hindun; ḍuriba al-Zaydāni; al-Zaydāni ḍuriba.
tasks.answer: Ḍuribat Hindun (a true feminine joined to its verb). Ḍuriba al-Zaydāni is right (with an explicit noun the verb is singular). Al-Zaydāni ḍuribā (with a pronoun the verb agrees).

tasks.prompt: What is the governor of Zaydun and of qāʾimun in Zaydun qāʾimun, according to the book?
tasks.answer: The abstract governor, the ibtidāʾ: both nouns are free of spoken governors, and the ibtidāʾ raises the mubtadaʾ Zaydun and the khabar qāʾimun.

tasks.prompt: Why may the indefinite rajulun be a mubtadaʾ in a-rajulun fī al-dāri ami imraʾatun, and fī al-dāri rajulun?
tasks.arabic: أَرَجُلٌ فِي الدَّارِ أَمِ امْرَأَةٌ — فِي الدَّارِ رَجُلٌ
tasks.answer: In the first it is made particular by the question with am: the speaker knows that one of the two is in the house. In the second the khabar, an adverb, is put first. Either way the indefinite has become particular enough to be spoken of.

tasks.prompt: Both nouns are definite in Allāhu ilāhunā. Which is the mubtadaʾ?
tasks.answer: Either may be made the mubtadaʾ and the other the khabar, the book says, when both are definite.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: مَفْعُولُ مَا لَمْ يُسَمَّ فَاعِلُهُ، وَهُوَ كُلُّ مَفْعُولٍ حُذِفَ فَاعِلُهُ وَأُقِيمَ هُوَ مَقَامَهُ، نَحْوُ: ضُرِبَ زَيْدٌ، وَحُكْمُهُ فِي تَوْحِيدِ فِعْلِهِ وَتَثْنِيَتِهِ وَجَمْعِهِ وَتَذْكِيرِهِ وَتَأْنِيثِهِ عَلَى قِيَاسِ مَا عَرَفْتَ فِي الْفَاعِلِ.
text.en: Section. The object of a verb whose doer is not named: it is every mafʿūl whose fāʿil has been dropped and which has been put in its place, as ḍuriba Zaydun “Zayd was hit”. Its rule as to making its verb singular, dual or plural, and masculine or feminine, follows the analogy of what you have learned in the fāʿil.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمُبْتَدَأُ وَالْخَبَرُ هُمَا اسْمَانِ مُجَرَّدَانِ عَنِ الْعَوَامِلِ اللَّفْظِيَّةِ، أَحَدُهُمَا مُسْنَدٌ إِلَيْهِ، وَيُسَمَّى الْمُبْتَدَأَ، وَالثَّانِي مُسْنَدٌ بِهِ، وَيُسَمَّى الْخَبَرَ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ. وَالْعَامِلُ فِيهِمَا مَعْنَوِيٌّ، وَهُوَ الِابْتِدَاءُ. وَأَصْلُ الْمُبْتَدَإِ أَنْ يَكُونَ مَعْرِفَةً، وَأَصْلُ الْخَبَرِ أَنْ يَكُونَ نَكِرَةً.
text.en: Section. The mubtadaʾ and the khabar are two nouns free of the spoken governors: one of them is that of which something is said (musnad ilayhi), and it is called the mubtadaʾ; the second is that which is said (musnad bihi), and it is called the khabar, as Zaydun qāʾimun “Zayd is standing”. The governor in them is abstract (maʿnawī): it is the ibtidāʾ (being put at the beginning). The base of the mubtadaʾ is to be definite, and the base of the khabar is to be indefinite.

text.original: وَالنَّكِرَةُ إِذَا وُصِفَتْ جَازَ أَنْ تَقَعَ مُبْتَدَأً، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَلَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ، وَكَذَا إِذَا تَخَصَّصَتْ بِوَجْهٍ آخَرَ، نَحْوُ: أَرَجُلٌ فِي الدَّارِ أَمِ امْرَأَةٌ، وَمَا أَحَدٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْكَ، وَشَرٌّ أَهَرَّ ذَا نَابٍ، وَفِي الدَّارِ رَجُلٌ، وَسَلَامٌ عَلَيْكَ.
text.en: An indefinite noun, when it is qualified, may stand as mubtadaʾ, as in His saying, exalted is He: wa-la-ʿabdun muʾminun khayrun min mushrikin “and a believing slave is better than an idolater”; likewise when it is made particular in another way, as a-rajulun fī al-dāri ami imraʾatun “is a man in the house, or a woman?”, mā aḥadun khayrun minka “no one is better than you”, sharrun aharra dhā nābin “an evil has made the fanged one snarl”, fī al-dāri rajulun “in the house is a man” and salāmun ʿalayka “peace be upon you”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ أَحَدُ الِاسْمَيْنِ مَعْرِفَةً وَالْآخَرُ نَكِرَةً فَاجْعَلِ الْمَعْرِفَةَ مُبْتَدَأً وَالنَّكِرَةَ خَبَرًا الْبَتَّةَ، كَمَا مَرَّ، وَإِنْ كَانَا مَعْرِفَتَيْنِ فَاجْعَلْ أَيَّهُمَا شِئْتَ مُبْتَدَأً وَالْآخَرَ خَبَرًا، نَحْوُ: اللَّهُ إِلَهُنَا، وَمُحَمَّدٌ نَبِيُّنَا، وَآدَمُ أَبُونَا.
text.en: If one of the two nouns is definite and the other indefinite, make the definite one the mubtadaʾ and the indefinite one the khabar, always, as has passed; if both are definite, make whichever you wish the mubtadaʾ and the other the khabar, as Allāhu ilāhunā “God is our god”, Muḥammadun nabiyyunā “Muḥammad is our prophet” and Ādamu abūnā “Ādam is our father”.

lessons.title: The khabar as a sentence; its order; the mubtadaʾ with no khabar
body: The khabar may be a whole sentence: nominal, Zaydun abūhu qāʾimun; verbal, Zaydun qāma abūhu; conditional, Zaydun in jāʾanī fa-akramtuhu; or adverbial, Zaydun khalfaka, ʿAmrun fī al-dāri. Most grammarians say the adverb is attached to a sentence, “istaqarra, for example”: Zaydun fī al-dāri is Zaydun istaqarra fī al-dāri. On this view an adverbial khabar is really a verbal sentence with its verb unsaid.

A khabar that is a sentence “must have a pronoun that refers back to the mubtadaʾ, like the hāʾ” of abūhu. Without it the sentence would not be about the mubtadaʾ at all. It may be dropped when the context shows it: al-samnu manawāni bi-dirhamin, “butter: two manns for a dirham”, and al-burru al-kurru bi-sittīna dirhaman, “wheat: the kurr for sixty dirhams”, where minhu, “of it”, is understood.
The khabar may come before the mubtadaʾ: fī al-dāri Zaydun. And one mubtadaʾ may have many khabars: Zaydun ʿālimun fāḍilun ʿāqilun, “Zayd is learned, excellent, wise”.

“They have another kind of mubtadaʾ, which is not that of which something is said”: an adjective after a particle of negation or of question, mā qāʾimun Zaydun, a-qāʾimun Zaydun, on condition that it raises an explicit noun. With the dual the condition is plain: in mā qāʾimun al-Zaydāni and a-qāʾimun al-Zaydāni, qāʾimun is the mubtadaʾ and al-Zaydāni its fāʿil, which fills the place of the khabar. But mā qāʾimāni al-Zaydāni is different: qāʾimāni agrees with al-Zaydāni, so it is a khabar put first, and al-Zaydāni is the mubtadaʾ.

terms.en: a khabar that is a whole sentence
the pronoun that refers back to the mubtadaʾ
what the adverb is attached to: istaqarra
an adjective raising an explicit noun: a mubtadaʾ with no khabar

examples.en: a conditional sentence as khabar
an adverb as khabar: istaqarra understood
the pronoun dropped: minhu
one mubtadaʾ, three khabars
an adjective as mubtadaʾ, its fāʿil for the khabar

tasks.prompt: Name the kind of khabar and its link back: Zaydun qāma abūhu; Zaydun khalfaka.
tasks.answer: Zaydun qāma abūhu: a verbal sentence; the link is the hāʾ of abūhu. Zaydun khalfaka: an adverbial khabar, attached to an understood istaqarra, whose hidden pronoun goes back to Zayd.

tasks.prompt: What is dropped in al-burru al-kurru bi-sittīna dirhaman, and why may it be dropped?
tasks.answer: The pronoun that refers back to al-burru: al-kurru minhu bi-sittīna dirhaman. It may be dropped because the context shows it: the kurr can only be of the wheat.

tasks.prompt: Parse mā qāʾimun al-Zaydāni and mā qāʾimāni al-Zaydāni.
tasks.arabic: مَا قَائِمٌ الزَّيْدَانِ — مَا قَائِمَانِ الزَّيْدَانِ
tasks.answer: In the first, qāʾimun is a mubtadaʾ after the negation, and al-Zaydāni its fāʿil, which stands in the place of the khabar. In the second, qāʾimāni agrees with al-Zaydāni, so it is a khabar put first, and al-Zaydāni is the mubtadaʾ.

tasks.prompt: Show the adverbial khabar of Zaydun fī al-dāri in its full form, as most grammarians give it.
tasks.answer: Zaydun istaqarra fī al-dāri: the adverb is attached to the understood verb istaqarra, and the sentence istaqarra fī al-dāri is the khabar.

quiz.prompt: Zaydun in jāʾanī fa-akramtuhu has a khabar that is…
Most grammarians attach the adverb in Zaydun fī al-dāri to…
A khabar sentence must have…
options: a pronoun referring to the mubtadaʾ

quiz.prompt: In al-samnu manawāni bi-dirhamin, what is dropped?
quiz.explanation: Two manns of it for a dirham.

quiz.prompt: May a mubtadaʾ have more than one khabar?
In a-qāʾimun al-Zaydāni, qāʾimun is…
quiz.explanation: Its fāʿil al-Zaydāni stands in the place of the khabar.

quiz.prompt: In mā qāʾimāni al-Zaydāni, qāʾimāni is…
quiz.explanation: It agrees with al-Zaydāni, the mubtadaʾ.

text.original: وَقَدْ يَكُونُ الْخَبَرُ جُمْلَةً اسْمِيَّةً، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ أَبُوهُ قَائِمٌ، أَوْ فِعْلِيَّةً، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ قَامَ أَبُوهُ، أَوْ شَرْطِيَّةً، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ إِنْ جَاءَنِي فَأَكْرَمْتُهُ، أَوْ ظَرْفِيَّةً، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ خَلْفَكَ، وَعَمْرٌو فِي الدَّارِ. وَالظَّرْفُ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِجُمْلَةٍ عِنْدَ الْأَكْثَرِ، وَهِيَ اسْتَقَرَّ مَثَلًا، تَقُولُ: زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ، تَقْدِيرُهُ: زَيْدٌ اسْتَقَرَّ فِي الدَّارِ.
text.en: The khabar may be a nominal sentence, as Zaydun abūhu qāʾimun “Zayd, his father is standing”; or a verbal one, as Zaydun qāma abūhu “Zayd, his father stood”; or a conditional one, as Zaydun in jāʾanī fa-akramtuhu “Zayd, if he comes to me, I honour him”; or an adverbial one, as Zaydun khalfaka “Zayd is behind you” and ʿAmrun fī al-dāri “ʿAmr is in the house”. The adverb is attached to a sentence according to most [grammarians], namely istaqarra “is settled”, for example: you say Zaydun fī al-dāri, which is in its underlying form Zaydun istaqarra fī al-dāri “Zayd is settled in the house”.

text.original: وَلَا بُدَّ فِي الْجُمْلَةِ مِنْ ضَمِيرٍ يَعُودُ إِلَى الْمُبْتَدَإِ، كَالْهَاءِ فِيمَا مَرَّ، وَيَجُوزُ حَذْفُهُ عِنْدَ وُجُودِ قَرِينَةٍ، نَحْوُ: السَّمْنُ مَنَوَانِ بِدِرْهَمٍ، وَالْبُرُّ الْكُرُّ بِسِتِّينَ دِرْهَمًا. وَقَدْ يَتَقَدَّمُ الْخَبَرُ عَلَى الْمُبْتَدَإِ، نَحْوُ: فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدٌ. وَيَجُوزُ لِلْمُبْتَدَإِ الْوَاحِدِ أَخْبَارٌ كَثِيرَةٌ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ عَالِمٌ فَاضِلٌ عَاقِلٌ.
text.en: In the sentence there must be a pronoun that refers back to the mubtadaʾ, like the hāʾ in what has passed; it may be dropped when there is an indication, as al-samnu manawāni bi-dirhamin “butter: two manns for a dirham” and al-burru al-kurru bi-sittīna dirhaman “wheat: the kurr for sixty dirhams”. The khabar may come before the mubtadaʾ, as fī al-dāri Zaydun “in the house is Zayd”. One mubtadaʾ may have many khabars, as Zaydun ʿālimun fāḍilun ʿāqilun “Zayd is learned, excellent, wise”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ قِسْمًا آخَرَ مِنَ الْمُبْتَدَإِ لَيْسَ مُسْنَدًا إِلَيْهِ، وَهُوَ صِفَةٌ وَقَعَتْ بَعْدَ حَرْفِ النَّفْيِ، نَحْوُ: مَا قَائِمٌ زَيْدٌ، أَوْ بَعْدَ حَرْفِ الِاسْتِفْهَامِ، نَحْوُ: أَقَائِمٌ زَيْدٌ، بِشَرْطِ أَنْ تَرْفَعَ تِلْكَ الصِّفَةُ اسْمًا ظَاهِرًا، نَحْوُ: مَا قَائِمٌ الزَّيْدَانِ، وَأَقَائِمٌ الزَّيْدَانِ، بِخِلَافِ: مَا قَائِمَانِ الزَّيْدَانِ.
text.en: Know that they have another kind of mubtadaʾ, which is not that of which something is said: an adjective that stands after a particle of negation, as mā qāʾimun Zaydun “Zayd is not standing”, or after a particle of question, as a-qāʾimun Zaydun “is Zayd standing?”, on condition that this adjective puts an explicit noun in rafʿ, as mā qāʾimun al-Zaydāni “the two Zayds are not standing” and a-qāʾimun al-Zaydāni “are the two Zayds standing?”, unlike mā qāʾimāni al-Zaydāni.

lessons.title: Inna, kāna, mā and lā: the khabar and the ism in rafʿ
body: Inna and its sisters, anna, kaʾanna, lākinna, layta and laʿalla, come upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar: they put the mubtadaʾ in naṣb, and it is called the ism of inna, and the khabar in rafʿ, and it is called the khabar of inna: inna Zaydan qāʾimun. This khabar is like the khabar of the mubtadaʾ in every rule, a single word or a sentence, definite or indefinite. But it may not come before the ism “unless it is an adverb”, inna fī al-dāri Zaydan, “because more freedom is allowed with adverbs”.

Kāna and its sisters do the opposite: ṣāra, aṣbaḥa, amsā, aḍḥā, ẓalla, bāta, rāḥa, āḍa, ʿāda, ghadā, mā zāla, mā bariḥa, mā fatiʾa, mā infakka, mā dāma and laysa. They put the mubtadaʾ in rafʿ as the ism of kāna and the khabar in naṣb as the khabar of kāna: kāna Zaydun qāʾiman. The ism of kāna, being in rafʿ, is counted here; its khabar comes among the manṣūb.

Their khabar may come before their ism in all of them: kāna qāʾiman Zaydun. It may even come before the verb itself in the first nine of the list: qāʾiman kāna Zaydun. Not in those that begin with mā: one does not say qāʾiman mā zāla Zaydun; the commentators give the reason, that the mā of negation must head its sentence. About laysa the grammarians disagree. More on these verbs comes in the part on the verb.

The ism of mā and lā that resemble laysa is in rafʿ: mā Zaydun qāʾiman, lā rajulun afḍala minka. Lā is used only with indefinites, mā with both. And the khabar of the lā that denies the kind (lā li-nafy al-jins) is in rafʿ: lā rajula qāʾimun, “there is no man standing”, the ism coming among the manṣūb (lesson 23).

terms.en: inna and its sisters: naṣb of the ism, rafʿ of the khabar
kāna and its sisters: rafʿ of the ism, naṣb of the khabar
mā and lā that work like laysa
the lā that denies the whole kind

examples.en: the khabar of inna before its ism: an adverb
the ism of kāna in rafʿ
the khabar before kāna itself
lā like laysa: its ism indefinite
the khabar of the lā of the kind in rafʿ

tasks.prompt: Put inna and then kāna before Zaydun qāʾimun, and parse each.
tasks.answer: Inna Zaydan qāʾimun: Zaydan is the ism of inna, in naṣb; qāʾimun its khabar, in rafʿ. Kāna Zaydun qāʾiman: Zaydun is the ism of kāna, in rafʿ; qāʾiman its khabar, in naṣb.

tasks.prompt: Which is allowed? inna qāʾimun Zaydan; inna fī al-dāri Zaydan; qāʾiman kāna Zaydun; qāʾiman mā zāla Zaydun.
tasks.answer: Inna qāʾimun Zaydan: not allowed (the khabar of inna comes first only if it is an adverb). Inna fī al-dāri Zaydan: allowed (an adverb). Qāʾiman kāna Zaydun: allowed (kāna is among the first nine). Qāʾiman mā zāla Zaydun: not allowed (mā zāla begins with mā).

tasks.prompt: Why may one say mā Zaydun qāʾiman but not lā Zaydun qāʾiman?
tasks.answer: Mā like laysa takes definites and indefinites; lā like laysa takes only indefinites, as lā rajulun afḍala minka.

tasks.prompt: In lā rajula qāʾimun, which word is counted among the marfūʿ, and why?
tasks.answer: Qāʾimun, the khabar of the lā that denies the kind, which is in rafʿ. Its ism, rajula, belongs to the manṣūb.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: خَبَرُ إِنَّ وَأَخَوَاتِهَا، وَهِيَ أَنَّ وَكَأَنَّ وَلَكِنَّ وَلَيْتَ وَلَعَلَّ؛ هَذِهِ الْحُرُوفُ تَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ فَتَنْصِبُ الْمُبْتَدَأَ، وَيُسَمَّى اسْمَ إِنَّ، وَتَرْفَعُ الْخَبَرَ، وَيُسَمَّى خَبَرَ إِنَّ. فَخَبَرُ إِنَّ هُوَ الْمُسْنَدُ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهَا، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، وَحُكْمُهُ فِي كَوْنِهِ مُفْرَدًا أَوْ جُمْلَةً أَوْ مَعْرِفَةً أَوْ نَكِرَةً كَحُكْمِ خَبَرِ الْمُبْتَدَإِ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ تَقْدِيمُ أَخْبَارِهَا عَلَى أَسْمَائِهَا إِلَّا إِذَا كَانَ ظَرْفًا، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدًا؛ لِجَوَازِ التَّوَسُّعِ فِي الظُّرُوفِ.
text.en: Section. The khabar of inna and its sisters, which are anna, kaʾanna, lākinna, layta and laʿalla. These particles come upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar: they put the mubtadaʾ in naṣb, and it is called the ism of inna, and they put the khabar in rafʿ, and it is called the khabar of inna. The khabar of inna is that which is said after [inna] has come in, as inna Zaydan qāʾimun “Zayd is indeed standing”. Its rule as to being a single word or a sentence, definite or indefinite, is like the rule of the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. Their khabars may not be put before their isms unless [the khabar] is an adverb, as inna fī al-dāri Zaydan “indeed, in the house is Zayd”, because more freedom is allowed with adverbs.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: اسْمُ كَانَ وَأَخَوَاتِهَا، وَهِيَ صَارَ، وَأَصْبَحَ، وَأَمْسَى، وَأَضْحَى، وَظَلَّ، وَبَاتَ، وَرَاحَ، وَآضَ، وَعَادَ، وَغَدَا، وَمَا زَالَ، وَمَا بَرِحَ، وَمَا فَتِئَ، وَمَا انْفَكَّ، وَمَا دَامَ، وَلَيْسَ؛ هَذِهِ الْأَفْعَالُ تَدْخُلُ أَيْضًا عَلَى الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ، فَتَرْفَعُ الْمُبْتَدَأَ، وَيُسَمَّى اسْمَ كَانَ، وَتَنْصِبُ الْخَبَرَ، وَيُسَمَّى خَبَرَ كَانَ. فَاسْمُ كَانَ هُوَ الْمُسْنَدُ إِلَيْهِ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهَا، نَحْوُ: كَانَ زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا.
text.en: Section. The ism of kāna and its sisters, which are ṣāra, aṣbaḥa, amsā, aḍḥā, ẓalla, bāta, rāḥa, āḍa, ʿāda, ghadā, mā zāla, mā bariḥa, mā fatiʾa, mā infakka, mā dāma and laysa. These verbs too come upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar: they put the mubtadaʾ in rafʿ, and it is called the ism of kāna, and they put the khabar in naṣb, and it is called the khabar of kāna. The ism of kāna is that of which something is said after [kāna] has come in, as kāna Zaydun qāʾiman “Zayd was standing”.

text.original: وَيَجُوزُ فِي الْكُلِّ تَقْدِيمُ أَخْبَارِهَا عَلَى أَسْمَائِهَا، نَحْوُ: كَانَ قَائِمًا زَيْدٌ، وَعَلَى نَفْسِ الْأَفْعَالِ أَيْضًا فِي التِّسْعَةِ الْأُوَلِ، نَحْوُ: قَائِمًا كَانَ زَيْدٌ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ فِيمَا فِي أَوَّلِهِ مَا، فَلَا يُقَالُ: قَائِمًا مَا زَالَ زَيْدٌ، وَفِي لَيْسَ خِلَافٌ. وَبَاقِي الْكَلَامِ فِي هَذِهِ الْأَفْعَالِ يَجِيءُ فِي الْقِسْمِ الثَّانِي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.
text.en: In all of them their khabars may be put before their isms, as kāna qāʾiman Zaydun, and before the verbs themselves too in the first nine, as qāʾiman kāna Zaydun; that is not allowed in those that begin with mā, so one does not say qāʾiman mā zāla Zaydun; and about laysa there is disagreement. The rest of what is said on these verbs comes in the second part, if God Most High wills.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: اسْمُ مَا وَلَا الْمُشَبَّهَتَيْنِ بِلَيْسَ، وَهُوَ الْمُسْنَدُ إِلَيْهِ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهِمَا، نَحْوُ: مَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا، وَلَا رَجُلٌ أَفْضَلَ مِنْكَ، وَيَخْتَصُّ لَا بِالنَّكِرَةِ، وَيَعُمُّ مَا بِالْمَعْرِفَةِ وَالنَّكِرَةِ. فَصْلٌ: خَبَرُ لَا لِنَفْيِ الْجِنْسِ، وَهُوَ الْمُسْنَدُ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهَا، نَحْوُ: لَا رَجُلَ قَائِمٌ.
text.en: Section. The ism of mā and lā that resemble laysa: it is that of which something is said after they have come in, as mā Zaydun qāʾiman “Zayd is not standing” and lā rajulun afḍala minka “no man is better than you”. Lā belongs to the indefinite only, while mā covers the definite and the indefinite. Section. The khabar of the lā that denies the kind: it is that which is said after it has come in, as lā rajula qāʾimun “there is no man standing”.

lessons.title: The twelve manṣūb; the absolute object
body: The second aim is the manṣūb nouns, twelve: the five objects (al-mafʿūl al-muṭlaq, bihi, fīhi, lahu, maʿahu), the ḥāl, the tamyīz, the mustathnā, the ism of inna and its sisters, the khabar of kāna and its sisters, the noun in naṣb by the lā that denies the kind, and the khabar of mā and lā like laysa. As with the marfūʿ, the muḍāriʿ in naṣb waits for the part on the verb.

The absolute object is “a maṣdar in the meaning of a verb mentioned before it”. It is said for one of three things. For emphasis: ḍarabtu ḍarban, “I hit a hitting”. To show the kind: jalastu jilsata al-qāriʾi, “I sat the sitting of the reciter”. To show the number: jalastu jalsatan, “one sitting”, jalsatayni, “two sittings”, jalasātin, “sittings”. The two patterns are a lesson of ṣarf in passing: fiʿla, jilsa, names a manner, and faʿla, jalsa, a single time.

It may be of another wording than the verb, as long as the meaning is the same: qaʿadtu julūsan, “I sat a sitting”, and anbata nabātan, “He made grow a growing”, from wa-Allāhu anbatakum mina al-arḍi nabātan (Q 71:17), where nabāt is the maṣdar of nabata, not of anbata.

Its verb may be dropped when the context shows it. By choice: to one who arrives you say khayra maqdamin, “the best of arrivals”, that is, qadimta qudūman khayra maqdamin. And necessarily, “by hearing”: saqyan, shukran, ḥamdan, raʿyan, that is, saqāka Allāhu saqyan, “may God water you”, shakartuka shukran, ḥamidtuka ḥamdan, raʿāka Allāhu raʿyan. These are fixed phrases of prayer and thanks; the Arabs never say their verbs with them, so one may not either.

terms.en: the twelve manṣūb nouns
a maṣdar in the meaning of the verb before it
showing the kind and the number
dropping that is necessary, as heard from the Arabs

examples.en: for emphasis
to show the kind: fiʿla

tasks.prompt: Say what each absolute object shows: ḍarabtu ḍarban; jalastu jilsata al-qāriʾi; jalastu jalsatayni.
tasks.arabic: ضَرَبْتُ ضَرْبًا — جَلَسْتُ جِلْسَةَ الْقَارِئِ — جَلَسْتُ جَلْسَتَيْنِ
tasks.answer: Ḍarban: emphasis only. Jilsata al-qāriʾi: the kind, “the reciter's way of sitting”, on the pattern fiʿla. Jalsatayni: the number, two sittings, the dual of faʿla.

tasks.prompt: Why is julūsan an absolute object in qaʿadtu julūsan?
tasks.answer: The absolute object is a maṣdar in the meaning of the verb before it. Julūs has the meaning of qaʿada, though its wording is another root, so it is the absolute object.

tasks.prompt: Give the full form of khayra maqdamin and of shukran.
tasks.answer: Khayra maqdamin: qadimta qudūman khayra maqdamin, its verb dropped by choice. Shukran: shakartuka shukran, its verb dropped necessarily, as heard from the Arabs.

tasks.prompt: Name the twelve manṣūb of the book.
tasks.answer: The absolute object; the mafʿūl bihi; the mafʿūl fīhi; the mafʿūl lahu; the mafʿūl maʿahu; the ḥāl; the tamyīz; the mustathnā; the ism of inna and its sisters; the khabar of kāna and its sisters; the noun in naṣb by the lā that denies the kind; the khabar of mā and lā like laysa.

quiz.prompt: How many manṣūb nouns does the book count?
quiz.explanation: The muḍāriʿ waits for the part on the verb.

a maṣdar in the meaning of a verb before it

quiz.prompt: Jalastu jilsata al-qāriʾi shows…
Jalastu jalsatan shows…

quiz.explanation: The maṣdar of nabata, with the meaning of anbata.

Saqyan, shukran, ḥamdan have their verbs dropped…
quiz.explanation: Saqāka Allāhu saqyan, and the rest.

text.original: الْأَسْمَاءُ الْمَنْصُوبَةُ اثْنَا عَشَرَ قِسْمًا: الْمَفْعُولُ الْمُطْلَقُ، وَبِهِ، وَفِيهِ، وَلَهُ، وَمَعَهُ، وَالْحَالُ، وَالتَّمْيِيزُ، وَالْمُسْتَثْنَى، وَاسْمُ إِنَّ وَأَخَوَاتِهَا، وَخَبَرُ كَانَ وَأَخَوَاتِهَا، وَالْمَنْصُوبُ بِلَا الَّتِي لِنَفْيِ الْجِنْسِ، وَخَبَرُ مَا وَلَا الْمُشَبَّهَتَيْنِ بِلَيْسَ.
text.en: The manṣūb nouns are of twelve kinds: the absolute object (al-mafʿūl al-muṭlaq) and the objects bihi, fīhi, lahu and maʿahu; the ḥāl; the tamyīz; the excepted (mustathnā); the ism of inna and its sisters; the khabar of kāna and its sisters; the noun put in naṣb by the lā that denies the kind; and the khabar of mā and lā that resemble laysa.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَفْعُولُ الْمُطْلَقُ، وَهُوَ مَصْدَرٌ بِمَعْنَى فِعْلٍ مَذْكُورٍ قَبْلَهُ، وَيُذْكَرُ لِلتَّأْكِيدِ، كَضَرَبْتُ ضَرْبًا، أَوْ لِبَيَانِ النَّوْعِ، نَحْوُ: جَلَسْتُ جِلْسَةَ الْقَارِئِ، أَوْ لِبَيَانِ الْعَدَدِ، كَجَلَسْتُ جَلْسَةً أَوْ جَلْسَتَيْنِ أَوْ جَلَسَاتٍ. وَقَدْ يَكُونُ مِنْ غَيْرِ لَفْظِ الْفِعْلِ الْمَذْكُورِ، نَحْوُ: قَعَدْتُ جُلُوسًا، وَأَنْبَتَ نَبَاتًا.
text.en: Section. The absolute object (al-mafʿūl al-muṭlaq): it is a maṣdar in the meaning of a verb mentioned before it. It is mentioned for emphasis, as ḍarabtu ḍarban “I hit a hitting”; or to show the kind, as jalastu jilsata al-qāriʾi “I sat the sitting of the reciter”; or to show the number, as jalastu jalsatan “I sat one sitting”, or jalsatayni “two sittings”, or jalasātin “[several] sittings”. It may be from a wording other than that of the verb mentioned, as qaʿadtu julūsan “I sat a sitting” and anbata nabātan “He made [it] grow a growing”.

text.original: وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ فِعْلُهُ لِقِيَامِ قَرِينَةٍ جَوَازًا، كَقَوْلِكَ لِلْقَادِمِ: خَيْرَ مَقْدَمٍ، أَيْ قَدِمْتَ قُدُومًا خَيْرَ مَقْدَمٍ، وَوُجُوبًا سَمَاعًا، نَحْوُ: سَقْيًا، وَشُكْرًا، وَحَمْدًا، وَرَعْيًا، أَيْ سَقَاكَ اللَّهُ سَقْيًا، وَشَكَرْتُكَ شُكْرًا، وَحَمِدْتُكَ حَمْدًا، وَرَعَاكَ اللَّهُ رَعْيًا.
text.en: Its verb may be dropped because there is an indication, by choice, as your saying to one who arrives khayra maqdamin “the best of arrivals”, that is, qadimta qudūman khayra maqdamin “you have arrived an arrival that is the best of arrivals”; and necessarily, by hearing, as saqyan “a watering”, shukran “thanks”, ḥamdan “praise” and raʿyan “a guarding”, that is, saqāka Allāhu saqyan “may God water you a watering”, shakartuka shukran “I thank you a thanking”, ḥamidtuka ḥamdan “I praise you a praising” and raʿāka Allāhu raʿyan “may God guard you a guarding”.

lessons.title: The mafʿūl bihi; when its verb must be dropped
body: The mafʿūl bihi is “the noun of that upon which the act of the fāʿil falls”: ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran. It may come before the fāʿil, ḍaraba ʿAmran Zaydun (lesson 10). Its verb may be dropped by choice when the context shows it, Zaydan in answer to man aḍribu, “whom shall I hit?”; and necessarily in four places.

The first is “by hearing”: phrases the Arabs always say without the verb. Imraʾan wa-nafsahu, “[leave] a man and himself”; intahū khayran lakum, “desist, [doing] what is better for you” (Q 4:171), where the commentators understand a verb such as “and do”; and ahlan wa-sahlan, “welcome”, which they explain as “you have come to family, and trodden on level ground”. The other three places are by rule.

The second is the warning (taḥdhīr). The noun is governed by an understood ittaqi, “guard against”: iyyāka wa-l-asada, “beware of the lion!”, “whose underlying form is ittaqika wa-l-asada”, guard yourself and the lion, that is, keep the two apart. Or the thing warned against is repeated: al-ṭarīqa al-ṭarīqa, “the road, the road!”, said to one about to step into it.

The third is the noun whose governor is hidden “on condition of explanation” (ʿalā sharīṭat al-tafsīr), which later books call ishtighāl. It is a noun followed by a verb that is “kept busy” away from it by its pronoun, or by something connected with it, “such that if it, or what fits it, were set over that noun, it would put it in naṣb”: Zaydan ḍarabtuhu, “Zayd, I hit him”. Ḍarabtuhu already has its object, the hāʾ, so Zaydan is in naṣb by a dropped ḍarabtu, which the spoken verb explains.

“Or what fits it”: in Zaydan marartu bihi the commentators understand jāwaztu Zaydan, “I passed Zayd”, since marra itself takes its object through the bāʾ. “This chapter has many branches”, the book says, and leaves them to the Kāfiya. The fourth place is the munādā, the next lesson.

the warning, governed by an understood ittaqi

tasks.prompt: Give the underlying form of iyyāka wa-l-asada and say what governs each noun.
tasks.answer: Ittaqika wa-l-asada, “guard yourself and the lion”. Iyyāka is the object of the understood ittaqi, and al-asada is joined to it, also in naṣb. The verb must be dropped in a warning.

tasks.prompt: Why is Zaydan in naṣb in Zaydan ḍarabtuhu, and what governs it?
tasks.answer: Ḍarabtuhu is kept busy with Zayd's pronoun, the hāʾ, so it cannot govern Zaydan. Zaydan is the object of a dropped verb, ḍarabtu, which the spoken ḍarabtuhu explains: ḍarabtu Zaydan ḍarabtuhu.

tasks.prompt: In Zaydan marartu bihi, which verb do the commentators understand, and why not marartu?
tasks.answer: Jāwaztu, “I passed”. Marra does not put its object in naṣb by itself but reaches it through the bāʾ, so the book's words “or what fits it” call for a verb of the same meaning that does give naṣb.

tasks.prompt: Name the four places where the verb of the mafʿūl bihi must be dropped.
tasks.answer: What is heard from the Arabs (as ahlan wa-sahlan); the warning (iyyāka wa-l-asada); the noun whose governor is hidden on condition of explanation (Zaydan ḍarabtuhu); and the munādā (yā ʿAbda Allāhi).

quiz.explanation: The heard, the warning, the explained, the munādā.

quiz.explanation: Its underlying form is ittaqika wa-l-asada.

quiz.explanation: The thing warned against, said twice.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَفْعُولُ بِهِ، وَهُوَ اسْمُ مَا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ فِعْلُ الْفَاعِلِ، كَضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا، وَقَدْ يَتَقَدَّمُ عَلَى الْفَاعِلِ، كَضَرَبَ عَمْرًا زَيْدٌ. وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ فِعْلُهُ لِقِيَامِ قَرِينَةٍ جَوَازًا، نَحْوُ: زَيْدًا، فِي جَوَابِ مَنْ قَالَ: مَنْ أَضْرِبُ؟ وَوُجُوبًا فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ: الْأَوَّلُ سَمَاعِيٌّ، نَحْوُ: امْرَأً وَنَفْسَهُ، وَانْتَهُوا خَيْرًا لَكُمْ، وَأَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا. وَالْبَوَاقِي قِيَاسِيَّةٌ.
text.en: Section. The mafʿūl bihi (direct object): it is the noun of that upon which the act of the fāʿil falls, as ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran “Zayd hit ʿAmr”; it may come before the fāʿil, as ḍaraba ʿAmran Zaydun. Its verb may be dropped because there is an indication, by choice, as Zaydan “Zayd” in answer to one who says man aḍribu “whom shall I hit?”; and necessarily in four places. The first is by hearing, as imraʾan wa-nafsahu “[leave] a man and himself”, intahū khayran lakum “desist, [doing] what is better for you” and ahlan wa-sahlan “welcome”. The others are by rule.

text.original: الثَّانِي التَّحْذِيرُ، وَهُوَ مَعْمُولٌ بِتَقْدِيرِ اتَّقِ، تَحْذِيرًا مِمَّا بَعْدَهُ، نَحْوُ: إِيَّاكَ وَالْأَسَدَ، أَصْلُهُ: اتَّقِكَ وَالْأَسَدَ، أَوْ ذُكِرَ الْمُحَذَّرُ مِنْهُ مُكَرَّرًا، نَحْوُ: الطَّرِيقَ الطَّرِيقَ.
text.en: The second is the warning (taḥdhīr): it is governed by an implied ittaqi “guard against”, as a warning against what comes after it, as iyyāka wa-al-asada “beware of the lion!”, whose underlying form is ittaqika wa-al-asada; or [it is] when that which is warned against is mentioned twice, as al-ṭarīqa al-ṭarīqa “the road, the road!”.

text.original: الثَّالِثُ مَا أُضْمِرَ عَامِلُهُ عَلَى شَرِيطَةِ التَّفْسِيرِ، وَهُوَ كُلُّ اسْمٍ بَعْدَهُ فِعْلٌ أَوْ شِبْهُهُ يَشْتَغِلُ ذَلِكَ الْفِعْلُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ الِاسْمِ بِضَمِيرِهِ أَوْ مُتَعَلِّقِهِ، بِحَيْثُ لَوْ سُلِّطَ عَلَيْهِ هُوَ أَوْ مُنَاسِبُهُ لَنَصَبَهُ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدًا ضَرَبْتُهُ؛ فَإِنَّ زَيْدًا مَنْصُوبٌ بِفِعْلٍ مَحْذُوفٍ، وَهُوَ ضَرَبْتُ، يُفَسِّرُهُ الْفِعْلُ الْمَذْكُورُ بَعْدَهُ، وَهُوَ ضَرَبْتُهُ. وَلِهَذَا الْبَابِ فُرُوعٌ كَثِيرَةٌ.
text.en: The third is that whose governor is concealed on condition of explanation (ʿalā sharīṭat al-tafsīr): it is every noun after which there is a verb, or what resembles a verb, that is kept busy away from that noun by its pronoun or by something connected with it, such that if it, or what fits it, were set over that noun, it would put it in naṣb, as Zaydan ḍarabtuhu “Zayd, I hit him”: Zaydan is in naṣb by a dropped verb, ḍarabtu, which the verb mentioned after it, ḍarabtuhu, explains. This chapter has many branches.

lessons.title: The munādā; shortening; the one lamented
body: The munādā is “a noun called by a particle of the vocative in the wording”: yā ʿAbda Allāhi, “that is, adʿū ʿAbda Allāhi”, “I call ʿAbd Allāh”; so it is the object of a verb the particle stands for (lesson 3). The particles are five: yā, ayā, hayā, ay and the hamza with fatḥa. The particle may be dropped from the wording: Yūsufu aʿriḍ ʿan hādhā, “Yūsuf, turn away from this” (Q 12:29).

A single definite munādā is built on its sign of rafʿ: on the ḍamma, yā Zaydu, and yā rajulu, a man made definite by being called; on the alif, yā Zaydāni; on the wāw, yā Zaydūna. With the lām of calling for help it is in khafḍ, yā la-Zaydin; with the alif of that call added, it takes fatḥa, yā Zaydāh.

It is in naṣb when it is muḍāf, yā ʿAbda Allāhi; “like the muḍāf”, yā ṭāliʿan jabalan, “O you who climb a mountain!”, where ṭāliʿan governs jabalan as a muḍāf governs its muḍāf ilayhi; or an indefinite not specified, “as the blind man says: yā rajulan khudh bi-yadī”, “O [some] man, take my hand!”, for he calls no man in particular. If the munādā has the lām of definiteness, ayyuhā or ayyatuhā is put between: yā ayyuhā al-rajulu, yā ayyatuhā al-marʾatu.

The munādā may be shortened (tarkhīm), “a dropping at its end for lightness”: Mālik, yā Māli; Manṣūr, yā Manṣu; ʿUthmān, yā ʿUthma. The last letter left may take the ḍamma, as though it were the whole name, or keep its own vowel: for Ḥārith, yā Ḥāru or yā Ḥāri.

Yā is also used for the one lamented (mandūb), the one grieved over: yā Zaydāh, wā Zaydāh, “alas, Zayd!”. Wā is only for lament; yā serves both. The mandūb follows the munādā's rules of iʿrāb and binā.

terms.en: the one called, the object of an understood adʿū
like the muḍāf: a munādā that governs what follows it
shortening the end of a munādā for lightness
the one lamented, with wā or yā

examples.en: the particle of the vocative dropped (Q 12:29)
single and definite: built on the ḍamma
like the muḍāf: in naṣb
an unspecified indefinite: in naṣb

tasks.prompt: Give the state of each munādā and why: yā Zaydu; yā ʿAbda Allāhi; yā ṭāliʿan jabalan; yā rajulan.
tasks.arabic: يَا زَيْدُ — يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ — يَا طَالِعًا جَبَلًا — يَا رَجُلًا
tasks.answer: Yā Zaydu: single and definite, built on the ḍamma. Yā ʿAbda Allāhi: muḍāf, in naṣb. Yā ṭāliʿan jabalan: like the muḍāf (it governs jabalan), in naṣb. Yā rajulan: an unspecified indefinite, in naṣb, as the blind man calls any man.

tasks.prompt: How do yā rajulu and yā rajulan differ?
tasks.answer: In yā rajulu a particular man is called, and the calling makes the word definite: single and definite, it is built on the ḍamma. In yā rajulan no particular man is meant: it stays indefinite and is in naṣb.

tasks.prompt: Shorten Mālik, Manṣūr and Ḥārith in the vocative, and give the two ways for Ḥārith.
tasks.answer: Yā Māli, yā Manṣu, yā Ḥāru or yā Ḥāri: the last letter left takes the ḍamma, as if it were the whole name, or keeps its own vowel.

tasks.prompt: Why is the munādā counted among the manṣūb, though yā Zaydu ends in a ḍamma?
tasks.answer: The munādā is the object of an understood verb, adʿū, for which the particle stands; so its place is naṣb. When it is single and definite it is built on its sign of rafʿ, but its place stays naṣb, and when it is muḍāf the naṣb shows.

quiz.prompt: The particle of the vocative stands in place of…
quiz.explanation: So the munādā is an object.

quiz.prompt: How many particles of the vocative does the book give?
quiz.explanation: Yā, ayā, hayā, ay, the hamza.

quiz.prompt: Yā Zaydāni is built on…
quiz.explanation: The sign of rafʿ of the dual.

quiz.prompt: Yā la-Zaydin is in khafḍ because of…
options: the lām of calling for help

text.original: الرَّابِعُ الْمُنَادَى، وَهُوَ اسْمٌ مَدْعُوٌّ بِحَرْفِ النِّدَاءِ لَفْظًا، نَحْوُ: يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، أَيْ أَدْعُو عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، وَحَرْفُ النِّدَاءِ قَائِمٌ مَقَامَ أَدْعُو، وَحُرُوفُ النِّدَاءِ خَمْسَةٌ: يَا، وَأَيَا، وَهَيَا، وَأَيْ، وَالْهَمْزَةُ الْمَفْتُوحَةُ. وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ حَرْفُ النِّدَاءِ لَفْظًا، نَحْوُ: يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذَا.
text.en: The fourth is the munādā (the one called): it is a noun called by a particle of the vocative in the wording, as yā ʿAbda Allāhi “O ʿAbd Allāh!”, that is, adʿū ʿAbda Allāhi “I call ʿAbd Allāh”; the particle of the vocative stands in the place of adʿū. The particles of the vocative are five: yā, ayā, hayā, ay and the hamza with fatḥa. The particle of the vocative may be dropped from the wording, as Yūsufu aʿriḍ ʿan hādhā “Yūsuf, turn away from this”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْمُنَادَى عَلَى أَقْسَامٍ: فَإِنْ كَانَ مُفْرَدًا مَعْرِفَةً يُبْنَى عَلَى عَلَامَةِ الرَّفْعِ، كَالضَّمَّةِ نَحْوُ: يَا زَيْدُ، وَيَا رَجُلُ، وَالْأَلِفِ نَحْوُ: يَا زَيْدَانِ، وَالْوَاوِ نَحْوُ: يَا زَيْدُونَ، وَيُخْفَضُ بِلَامِ الِاسْتِغَاثَةِ، نَحْوُ: يَا لَزَيْدٍ، وَيُفْتَحُ بِإِلْحَاقِ أَلِفِهَا، نَحْوُ: يَا زَيْدَاهْ، وَيُنْصَبُ إِنْ كَانَ مُضَافًا، نَحْوُ: يَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ، أَوْ مُشَابِهًا لِلْمُضَافِ، نَحْوُ: يَا طَالِعًا جَبَلًا، أَوْ نَكِرَةً غَيْرَ مُعَيَّنَةٍ، كَقَوْلِ الْأَعْمَى: يَا رَجُلًا خُذْ بِيَدِي.
text.en: Know that the munādā is of [several] kinds. If it is a single definite [noun], it is fixed (mabnī) on the sign of rafʿ: the ḍamma, as yā Zaydu “O Zayd!” and yā rajulu “O man!”; the alif, as yā Zaydāni “O two Zayds!”; and the wāw, as yā Zaydūna “O Zayds!”. It is put in khafḍ by the lām of calling for help (istighātha), as yā la-Zaydin “O help, Zayd!”, and given a fatḥa when its alif is joined to it, as yā Zaydāh “O Zayd!”. It is put in naṣb if it is muḍāf, as yā ʿAbda Allāhi “O ʿAbd Allāh!”, or like the muḍāf, as yā ṭāliʿan jabalan “O you who climb a mountain!”, or an indefinite that is not specified, as the blind man says: yā rajulan khudh bi-yadī “O [some] man, take my hand!”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ مُعَرَّفًا بِاللَّامِ قِيلَ: يَا أَيُّهَا الرَّجُلُ، وَيَا أَيَّتُهَا الْمَرْأَةُ. وَيَجُوزُ تَرْخِيمُ الْمُنَادَى، وَهُوَ حَذْفٌ فِي آخِرِهِ لِلتَّخْفِيفِ، كَمَا تَقُولُ فِي مَالِكٍ: يَا مَالِ، وَفِي مَنْصُورٍ: يَا مَنْصُ، وَفِي عُثْمَانَ: يَا عُثْمَ. وَيَجُوزُ فِي آخِرِ الْمُنَادَى الْمُرَخَّمِ الضَّمُّ، وَالْحَرَكَةُ الْأَصْلِيَّةُ، كَمَا تَقُولُ فِي يَا حَارِثُ: يَا حَارُ، وَيَا حَارِ.
text.en: If it is defined by the lām, one says yā ayyuhā al-rajulu “O man!” and yā ayyatuhā al-marʾatu “O woman!”. The munādā may be shortened (tarkhīm), which is a dropping at its end for lightness, as you say for Mālikin yā Māli, for Manṣūrin yā Manṣu and for ʿUthmāna yā ʿUthma. At the end of the shortened munādā the ḍamma and the original vowel are both allowed, as you say for yā Ḥārithu yā Ḥāru and yā Ḥāri.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ يَا مِنْ حُرُوفِ النِّدَاءِ، وَقَدْ يُسْتَعْمَلُ فِي الْمَنْدُوبِ أَيْضًا، وَهُوَ الْمُتَفَجَّعُ عَلَيْهِ بِيَا أَوْ وَا، كَمَا يُقَالُ: يَا زَيْدَاهْ، وَوَا زَيْدَاهْ. وَا مُخْتَصَّةٌ بِالْمَنْدُوبِ، وَيَا مُشْتَرَكَةٌ بَيْنَ النِّدَاءِ وَالْمَنْدُوبِ، وَحُكْمُهُ فِي الْإِعْرَابِ وَالْبِنَاءِ مِثْلُ حُكْمِ الْمُنَادَى.
text.en: Know that yā, among the particles of the vocative, is sometimes also used for the one lamented (mandūb), who is the one grieved over with yā or wā, as one says yā Zaydāh and wā Zaydāh “alas, Zayd!”. Wā belongs to the mandūb only, while yā is shared between the vocative and the mandūb; and its rule as to iʿrāb and bināʾ is like the rule of the munādā.

lessons.title: The mafʿūl fīhi, the mafʿūl lahu and the mafʿūl maʿahu
body: The mafʿūl fīhi is the time or place in which the act happens, and it is called an adverb (ẓarf). Adverbs of time are vague, with no fixed limit, as dahr, “an age”, ḥīn, “a while”, or limited, as yawm, layla, shahr, sana; “all of them are in naṣb by an implied fī”: ṣumtu dahran, sāfartu shahran.

Adverbs of place are of the same two kinds, but they behave differently. A vague place is in naṣb by an implied fī: jalastu khalfaka wa-amāmaka. A limited place, one with a name and bounds, takes no naṣb: “fī must be mentioned in it”: jalastu fī al-dāri, fī al-sūqi, fī al-masjidi. One does not say jalastu al-dāra.

The mafʿūl lahu is that “for the sake of which the act mentioned before it happens”, in naṣb by an implied lām: ḍarabtuhu taʾdīban, “I hit him for correction”, that is, li-l-taʾdībi; qaʿadtu ʿani al-ḥarbi jubnan, “I stayed from war out of cowardice”. Al-Zajjāj holds that it is a maṣdar, an absolute object of an understood verb: addabtuhu taʾdīban, jabuntu jubnan.

The mafʿūl maʿahu is what comes after a wāw in the sense of maʿa, “with”, to show company: jāʾa al-bardu wa-l-jubbāti, “the cold came, with the cloaks”, where the cloaks do not come, so the wāw cannot join them to the cold; and jiʾtu anā wa-Zaydan. When the verb is in the wording and joining (ʿaṭf) is allowed, both are allowed: jiʾtu anā wa-Zaydan, or wa-Zaydun, joined to anā. When joining is not allowed, naṣb is the only way: jiʾtu wa-Zaydan, since a noun is not joined to the tāʾ without the separate pronoun.

When the verb is only in the meaning, the rule is turned round. If joining is allowed, it is required: mā li-Zaydin wa-ʿAmrin, “what is with Zayd and ʿAmr?”, ʿAmrin joined to Zaydin. If not, naṣb: mā laka wa-Zaydan, mā shaʾnuka wa-ʿAmran, “for the meaning is mā taṣnaʿu”, “what are you doing [with him]?”; Zaydan cannot be joined to the kāf without repeating the lām.

terms.en: the adverb: the time or place of the act, the mafʿūl fīhi
vague and limited, of time and of place
that for whose sake the act happens, with the lām understood
the noun after the wāw of company

examples.en: time, vague and limited: fī understood
a vague place: fī understood
a limited place: fī must be said
the mafʿūl lahu
the mafʿūl maʿahu: no joining possible

tasks.prompt: Correct if needed: jalastu al-dāra; jalastu khalfaka; ṣumtu dahran.
tasks.answer: Jalastu al-dāra is wrong: a limited place needs fī, jalastu fī al-dāri. Jalastu khalfaka is right: a vague place, in naṣb by an implied fī. Ṣumtu dahran is right: every adverb of time is in naṣb by an implied fī.

tasks.prompt: Give the two readings of jubnan in qaʿadtu ʿani al-ḥarbi jubnan.
tasks.answer: As the book takes it, a mafʿūl lahu in naṣb by an implied lām: li-l-jubni, “out of cowardice”. According to al-Zajjāj, a maṣdar, the absolute object of an understood verb: jabuntu jubnan.

tasks.prompt: Why are both naṣb and rafʿ allowed in jiʾtu anā wa-Zayd…, but only naṣb in jiʾtu wa-Zaydan?
tasks.answer: With anā, the noun may be joined to the separate pronoun (rafʿ) or be a mafʿūl maʿahu (naṣb). Without anā it cannot be joined to the tāʾ, a marfūʿ joined pronoun, so naṣb as mafʿūl maʿahu is the only way.

tasks.prompt: Why is mā li-Zaydin wa-ʿAmrin joined, but mā laka wa-Zaydan in naṣb?
tasks.arabic: مَا لِزَيْدٍ وَعَمْرٍو — مَا لَكَ وَزَيْدًا
tasks.answer: The verb is only in the meaning. In the first, ʿAmr can be joined to Zayd (a noun after the lām), so joining is required. In the second, Zayd cannot be joined to the kāf, a majrūr pronoun, without repeating the lām, so it is in naṣb, with the meaning mā taṣnaʿu.

quiz.prompt: The mafʿūl fīhi is also called…
quiz.explanation: The time or place of the act.

options: a maṣdar of an understood verb

options: the cloaks do not come: no joining

quiz.prompt: In mā laka wa-Zaydan, the meaning is…
quiz.explanation: The verb is only in the meaning.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَفْعُولُ فِيهِ، هُوَ اسْمُ مَا وَقَعَ فِعْلُ الْفَاعِلِ فِيهِ مِنَ الزَّمَانِ وَالْمَكَانِ، وَيُسَمَّى ظَرْفًا. وَظُرُوفُ الزَّمَانِ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: مُبْهَمٌ، وَهُوَ مَا لَا يَكُونُ لَهُ حَدٌّ مُعَيَّنٌ، كَدَهْرٍ وَحِينٍ، وَمَحْدُودٌ، وَهُوَ مَا يَكُونُ لَهُ حَدٌّ مُعَيَّنٌ، كَيَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ وَشَهْرٍ وَسَنَةٍ، وَكُلُّهَا مَنْصُوبٌ بِتَقْدِيرِ فِي، تَقُولُ: صُمْتُ دَهْرًا، وَسَافَرْتُ شَهْرًا، أَيْ فِي دَهْرٍ وَفِي شَهْرٍ.
text.en: Section. The mafʿūl fīhi: it is the noun of the time and the place in which the act of the fāʿil happens, and it is called an adverb (ẓarf). The adverbs of time are of two kinds: vague (mubham), which is one that has no fixed limit, as dahrin “an age” and ḥīnin “a while”; and limited (maḥdūd), which is one that has a fixed limit, as yawmin “a day”, laylatin “a night”, shahrin “a month” and sanatin “a year”. All of them are in naṣb by an implied fī “in”; you say ṣumtu dahran “I fasted an age” and sāfartu shahran “I travelled a month”, that is, fī dahrin and wa-fī shahrin.

text.original: وَظُرُوفُ الْمَكَانِ كَذَلِكَ: مُبْهَمٌ، وَهُوَ مَنْصُوبٌ أَيْضًا بِتَقْدِيرِ فِي، نَحْوُ: جَلَسْتُ خَلْفَكَ وَأَمَامَكَ، وَمَحْدُودٌ، وَهُوَ مَا لَا يَكُونُ مَنْصُوبًا بِتَقْدِيرِ فِي، بَلْ لَا بُدَّ مِنْ ذِكْرِ فِي فِيهِ، نَحْوُ: جَلَسْتُ فِي الدَّارِ، وَفِي السُّوقِ، وَفِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
text.en: The adverbs of place are likewise: vague, and it too is in naṣb by an implied fī, as jalastu khalfaka wa-amāmaka “I sat behind you and in front of you”; and limited, which is not in naṣb by an implied fī, but fī must be mentioned in it, as jalastu fī al-dāri “I sat in the house”, wa-fī al-sūqi “and in the market” and wa-fī al-masjidi “and in the mosque”.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَفْعُولُ لَهُ، هُوَ اسْمُ مَا لِأَجْلِهِ يَقَعُ الْفِعْلُ الْمَذْكُورُ قَبْلَهُ، وَيُنْصَبُ بِتَقْدِيرِ اللَّامِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُهُ تَأْدِيبًا، أَيْ لِلتَّأْدِيبِ، وَقَعَدْتُ عَنِ الْحَرْبِ جُبْنًا، أَيْ لِلْجُبْنِ. وَعِنْدَ الزَّجَّاجِ هُوَ مَصْدَرٌ، تَقْدِيرُهُ: أَدَّبْتُهُ تَأْدِيبًا، وَجَبُنْتُ جُبْنًا.
text.en: Section. The mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose): it is the noun of that for the sake of which the act mentioned before it happens; it is in naṣb by an implied lām, as ḍarabtuhu taʾdīban “I hit him for correction”, that is, li-al-taʾdībi, and qaʿadtu ʿani al-ḥarbi jubnan “I stayed away from war out of cowardice”, that is, li-al-jubni. According to al-Zajjāj it is a maṣdar; its underlying form is addabtuhu taʾdīban “I corrected him a correcting” and wa-jabuntu jubnan “and I was cowardly a cowardice”.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَفْعُولُ مَعَهُ، هُوَ مَا يُذْكَرُ بَعْدَ الْوَاوِ بِمَعْنَى مَعَ لِمُصَاحَبَةِ مَعْمُولِ الْفِعْلِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَ الْبَرْدُ وَالْجُبَّاتِ، وَجِئْتُ أَنَا وَزَيْدًا، أَيْ مَعَ الْجُبَّاتِ وَمَعَ زَيْدٍ. فَإِنْ كَانَ الْفِعْلُ لَفْظًا وَجَازَ الْعَطْفُ يَجُوزُ فِيهِ الْوَجْهَانِ: النَّصْبُ وَالرَّفْعُ، نَحْوُ: جِئْتُ أَنَا وَزَيْدًا، وَزَيْدٌ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَجُزِ الْعَطْفُ تَعَيَّنَ النَّصْبُ، نَحْوُ: جِئْتُ وَزَيْدًا.
text.en: Section. The mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment): it is what is mentioned after the wāw in the meaning of maʿa “with”, for the accompanying of the governed word of the verb, as jāʾa al-bardu wa-al-jubbāti “the cold came, with the cloaks” and jiʾtu anā wa-Zaydan “I came, with Zayd”, that is, maʿa al-jubbāti and wa-maʿa Zaydin. If the verb is in the wording and conjunction (ʿaṭf) is allowed, both ways are allowed in it, naṣb and rafʿ, as jiʾtu anā wa-Zaydan and wa-Zaydun; if conjunction is not allowed, naṣb is fixed, as jiʾtu wa-Zaydan “I came, with Zayd”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ الْفِعْلُ مَعْنًى وَجَازَ الْعَطْفُ تَعَيَّنَ الْعَطْفُ، نَحْوُ: مَا لِزَيْدٍ وَعَمْرٍو، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَجُزِ الْعَطْفُ تَعَيَّنَ النَّصْبُ، نَحْوُ: مَا لَكَ وَزَيْدًا، وَمَا شَأْنُكَ وَعَمْرًا؛ لِأَنَّ الْمَعْنَى: مَا تَصْنَعُ.
text.en: If the verb is [only] in the meaning and conjunction is allowed, conjunction is fixed, as mā li-Zaydin wa-ʿAmrin “what is with Zayd and ʿAmr?”; if conjunction is not allowed, naṣb is fixed, as mā laka wa-Zaydan “what is with you, with Zayd?” and mā shaʾnuka wa-ʿAmran “what is your affair, with ʿAmr?”; for the meaning is mā taṣnaʿu “what are you doing?”.

lessons.title: The ḥāl
body: The ḥāl is “an utterance that shows the state of the fāʿil or of the mafʿūl bihi or of both”: jāʾanī Zaydun rākiban, the state of the fāʿil; ḍarabtu Zaydan mashdūdan, “I hit Zayd bound”, the state of the object; laqītu ʿAmran rākibayni, “I met ʿAmr, both of us riding”, the state of both, shown by the dual.

The owner may be a fāʿil or an object only in meaning. In Zaydun fī al-dāri qāʾiman the ḥāl belongs to the hidden fāʿil of the understood istaqarra (lesson 14): Zaydun istaqarra fī al-dāri qāʾiman. In hādhā Zaydun qāʾiman it belongs to Zayd as the object of the meaning of hādhā, “I point to him standing”, or, as the book also says, “I call attention and point”.

Its governor is “a verb or the meaning of a verb”. The ḥāl is “always indefinite”, and its owner (dhū al-ḥāl) is mostly definite. If the owner is indefinite, the ḥāl must come before it: jāʾanī rākiban rajulun, “lest it be confused with the adjective in the state of naṣb”. The reason is worth seeing: in rafʿ, rajulun rākibun and rajulun rākiban look different, but in naṣb, raʾaytu rajulan rākiban could be “a riding man” or “a man, riding”. Put first, it can only be a ḥāl.

The ḥāl may be a declarative sentence: jāʾanī Zaydun wa-ghulāmuhu rākibun, “Zayd came, his servant riding”, or rakiba ghulāmuhu. And its governor may be dropped when the context shows it: to a traveller you say sāliman ghāniman, “safe, with gain”, that is, tarjiʿu sāliman ghāniman, “may you return safe, with gain”.

terms.en: what shows the state of the fāʿil, the object, or both
the owner of the ḥāl, mostly definite
a governor that is the meaning of a verb, as in hādhā
confusion with the adjective, in naṣb

examples.en: the ḥāl of the object
the ḥāl of both
the owner a fāʿil in meaning
an indefinite owner: the ḥāl first
the governor dropped: tarjiʿu

tasks.prompt: Find the ḥāl and its owner: jāʾanī Zaydun rākiban; ḍarabtu Zaydan mashdūdan; laqītu ʿAmran rākibayni.
tasks.arabic: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ رَاكِبًا — ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا مَشْدُودًا — لَقِيتُ عَمْرًا رَاكِبَيْنِ
tasks.answer: Rākiban: the ḥāl of Zayd, the fāʿil. Mashdūdan: the ḥāl of Zayd, the object. Rākibayni: the ḥāl of both the speaker (the tāʾ, the fāʿil) and ʿAmr (the object), as the dual shows.

tasks.prompt: Why must the ḥāl come first in jāʾanī rākiban rajulun?
tasks.answer: Its owner rajulun is indefinite. After an indefinite, a ḥāl in naṣb would be confused with an adjective in naṣb (raʾaytu rajulan rākiban). Put first, it can only be a ḥāl.

tasks.prompt: What governs qāʾiman in hādhā Zaydun qāʾiman?
tasks.answer: The meaning of a verb in hādhā: “I point to him” or “I call attention”. Zayd is its object in meaning, and qāʾiman shows his state.

tasks.prompt: Supply the dropped governor in sāliman ghāniman, said to a traveller.
tasks.answer: Tarjiʿu sāliman ghāniman, “may you return safe, with gain”: the two words are ḥāls of the hidden fāʿil of tarjiʿu, dropped because the context shows it.

quiz.prompt: The ḥāl shows the state of…
options: the fāʿil, the object, or both

quiz.prompt: In laqītu ʿAmran rākibayni, the dual shows that the ḥāl belongs to…
The governor of the ḥāl is…
options: a verb or the meaning of a verb

quiz.prompt: The ḥāl is always…
Confusion with the adjective arises in…
In jāʾanī Zaydun wa-ghulāmuhu rākibun, the ḥāl is…
Sāliman ghāniman is governed by…

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْحَالُ لَفْظٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى بَيَانِ هَيْئَةِ الْفَاعِلِ أَوِ الْمَفْعُولِ بِهِ أَوْ كِلَيْهِمَا، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ رَاكِبًا، وَضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا مَشْدُودًا، وَلَقِيتُ عَمْرًا رَاكِبَيْنِ. وَقَدْ يَكُونُ الْفَاعِلُ مَعْنَوِيًّا، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ قَائِمًا؛ لِأَنَّ مَعْنَاهُ: زَيْدٌ اسْتَقَرَّ فِي الدَّارِ قَائِمًا، وَكَذَا الْمَفْعُولُ، نَحْوُ: هَذَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا؛ فَإِنَّ مَعْنَاهُ: أُشِيرُ إِلَيْهِ قَائِمًا، وَهُوَ زَيْدٌ.
text.en: Section. The ḥāl (state) is an utterance that shows the state of the fāʿil or of the mafʿūl bihi or of both, as jāʾanī Zaydun rākiban “Zayd came to me riding”, ḍarabtu Zaydan mashdūdan “I hit Zayd bound” and laqītu ʿAmran rākibayni “I met ʿAmr, both of us riding”. The fāʿil may be in the meaning [only], as Zaydun fī al-dāri qāʾiman “Zayd is in the house, standing”, for its meaning is Zaydun istaqarra fī al-dāri qāʾiman “Zayd is settled in the house, standing”; likewise the mafʿūl, as hādhā Zaydun qāʾiman “this is Zayd, standing”, for its meaning is ushīru ilayhi qāʾiman “I point to him standing”, and he is Zayd.

text.original: وَالْعَامِلُ فِي الْحَالِ فِعْلٌ أَوْ مَعْنَى فِعْلٍ. وَالْحَالُ نَكِرَةٌ أَبَدًا، وَذُو الْحَالِ مَعْرِفَةٌ غَالِبًا، كَمَا رَأَيْتَ فِي الْأَمْثِلَةِ الْمَذْكُورَةِ. فَإِنْ كَانَ ذُو الْحَالِ نَكِرَةً يَجِبُ تَقْدِيمُ الْحَالِ عَلَيْهِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي رَاكِبًا رَجُلٌ؛ لِئَلَّا تَلْتَبِسَ بِالصِّفَةِ فِي حَالَةِ النَّصْبِ فِي مِثْلِ قَوْلِكَ: رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا رَاكِبًا.
text.en: The governor of the ḥāl is a verb or the meaning of a verb. The ḥāl is always indefinite, and the one the ḥāl belongs to (dhū al-ḥāl) is mostly definite, as you have seen in the examples mentioned. If the dhū al-ḥāl is indefinite, the ḥāl must be put before it, as jāʾanī rākiban rajulun “a man came to me riding”, lest it be confused with the adjective in the state of naṣb, in such a saying of yours as raʾaytu rajulan rākiban “I saw a riding man”.

text.original: وَقَدْ تَكُونُ الْحَالُ جُمْلَةً خَبَرِيَّةً، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ وَغُلَامُهُ رَاكِبٌ، أَوْ رَكِبَ غُلَامُهُ. وَسَيَأْتِي مِثَالُ مَا كَانَ عَامِلُهَا مَعْنَى الْفِعْلِ، نَحْوُ: هَذَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا؛ مَعْنَاهُ: أُنَبِّهُ وَأُشِيرُ. وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ الْعَامِلُ لِقِيَامِ قَرِينَةٍ، كَمَا تَقُولُ لِلْمُسَافِرِ: سَالِمًا غَانِمًا، أَيْ تَرْجِعُ سَالِمًا غَانِمًا.
text.en: The ḥāl may be a declarative sentence, as jāʾanī Zaydun wa-ghulāmuhu rākibun “Zayd came to me, his servant riding”, or rakiba ghulāmuhu “his servant having ridden”. The example of one whose governor is the meaning of a verb will come, as hādhā Zaydun qāʾiman, whose meaning is unabbihu wa-ushīru “I call attention and point”. The governor may be dropped because there is an indication, as you say to the traveller sāliman ghāniman “safe, with gain”, that is, tarjiʿu sāliman ghāniman “may you return safe, with gain”.

lessons.title: The tamyīz; the mustathnā and when it is in naṣb
body: The tamyīz is “an indefinite noun mentioned after a measure”, of number, capacity, weight, area or something else, “in which there is vagueness, and it removes that vagueness”. ʿIndī ʿishrūna dirhaman: twenty of what? Dirhams. Qafīzāni burran, two qafīz of wheat (capacity); manawāni samnan, two mann of butter (weight); jarībāni quṭnan, two jarīb of cotton (area); and ʿalā al-tamrati mithluhā zubdan, “on the date its like in butter”, where mithl is vague until zubdan explains it.

It may explain what is not a measure: hādhā khātamun ḥadīdan, “a ring of iron”, siwārun dhahaban, “a bracelet of gold”; but here khafḍ is more common, khātamu ḥadīdin. And it may come after a whole sentence, to remove the vagueness of its attribution: ṭāba Zaydun nafsan, ʿilman, aban, “Zayd is good in soul, in knowledge, as a father”: the sentence says Zayd is good, and the tamyīz says in what.

The mustathnā is “an utterance mentioned after illā and its sisters, so that it be known that what is attributed to what comes before it is not attributed to it”. It is connected (muttaṣil) when it is taken out of a plurality: jāʾanī al-qawmu illā Zaydan, Zayd being one of the people. It is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) when it was never included in what the exception is made from (al-mustathnā minhu): jāʾanī al-qawmu illā ḥimāran, “the people came, except a donkey”.

Its iʿrāb is of four kinds, and the first is naṣb. The mustathnā is in naṣb when it is connected and comes after illā in affirmative speech; when it is disconnected; when it comes before what it is excepted from, mā jāʾanī illā Zaydan aḥadun; after khalā and ʿadā, “according to most”; and after mā khalā, mā ʿadā, laysa and lā yakūnu: jāʾanī al-qawmu khalā Zaydan. The other three kinds come in the next lesson.

terms.en: an indefinite that removes the vagueness of a measure or a sentence
a measure: of number, capacity, weight or area
the connected and the disconnected exception
affirmative speech, with no negation, prohibition or question

examples.en: a tamyīz of number
a tamyīz of another vague word
a tamyīz of what is not a measure

examples.arabic: طَابَ زَيْدٌ نَفْسًا، أَوْ عِلْمًا، أَوْ أَبًا
examples.en: a tamyīz of a sentence's attribution
the mustathnā before what it is excepted from: naṣb

tasks.prompt: Find the tamyīz and say what vagueness it removes: ʿindī ʿishrūna dirhaman; manawāni samnan; ṭāba Zaydun ʿilman.
tasks.arabic: عِنْدِي عِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا — مَنَوَانِ سَمْنًا — طَابَ زَيْدٌ عِلْمًا
tasks.answer: Dirhaman removes the vagueness of the number twenty. Samnan removes the vagueness of the weight “two mann”. ʿIlman removes the vagueness of the attribution in ṭāba Zaydun: Zayd is good in knowledge.

tasks.prompt: Give the two ways of saying “a ring of iron”, and which the book says is more common.
tasks.answer: Khātamun ḥadīdan, with the tamyīz in naṣb, or khātamu ḥadīdin, in khafḍ by iḍāfa. With what is not a measure, khafḍ is more common.

tasks.prompt: Connected or disconnected? jāʾanī al-qawmu illā Zaydan; jāʾanī al-qawmu illā ḥimāran.
tasks.answer: Illā Zaydan is connected: Zayd is one of the people and is taken out of them. Illā ḥimāran is disconnected: the donkey was never among the people. Both are in naṣb.

tasks.prompt: Give the cases in which the mustathnā is in naṣb, as the book lists them.
tasks.answer: Connected, after illā, in affirmative speech; disconnected; put before what it is excepted from; after khalā and ʿadā (according to most); after mā khalā, mā ʿadā, laysa and lā yakūnu.

quiz.prompt: The tamyīz is always…
In qafīzāni burran the vagueness is in…
quiz.explanation: Two qafīz of what? Of wheat.

quiz.prompt: In ṭāba Zaydun nafsan the tamyīz removes vagueness from…
With what is not a measure, as khātam, the more common way is…
In jāʾanī al-qawmu illā ḥimāran, the exception is…
Mā jāʾanī illā Zaydan aḥadun: Zaydan is in naṣb because…
options: it comes before what it is excepted from

quiz.prompt: After laysa and lā yakūnu the mustathnā is…

text.original: فَصْلٌ: التَّمْيِيزُ نَكِرَةٌ تُذْكَرُ بَعْدَ مِقْدَارٍ مِنْ عَدَدٍ أَوْ كَيْلٍ أَوْ وَزْنٍ أَوْ مِسَاحَةٍ أَوْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا فِيهِ إِبْهَامٌ، تَرْفَعُ ذَلِكَ الْإِبْهَامَ، نَحْوُ: عِنْدِي عِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا، وَقَفِيزَانِ بُرًّا، وَمَنَوَانِ سَمْنًا، وَجَرِيبَانِ قُطْنًا، وَعَلَى التَّمْرَةِ مِثْلُهَا زُبْدًا.
text.en: Section. The tamyīz (specification) is an indefinite noun mentioned after a measure — of number, capacity, weight, area or something else — in which there is vagueness, and it removes that vagueness, as ʿindī ʿishrūna dirhaman “I have twenty dirhams”, wa-qafīzāni burran “and two qafīzs of wheat”, wa-manawāni samnan “and two manns of butter”, wa-jarībāni quṭnan “and two jarībs of cotton” and wa-ʿalā al-tamrati mithluhā zubdan “and on the date its like in fresh butter”.

text.original: وَقَدْ يَكُونُ عَنْ غَيْرِ مِقْدَارٍ، نَحْوُ: هَذَا خَاتَمٌ حَدِيدًا، وَسِوَارٌ ذَهَبًا، وَفِيهِ الْخَفْضُ أَكْثَرُ. وَقَدْ يَقَعُ بَعْدَ الْجُمْلَةِ لِرَفْعِ الْإِبْهَامِ عَنْ نِسْبَتِهَا، نَحْوُ: طَابَ زَيْدٌ نَفْسًا، أَوْ عِلْمًا، أَوْ أَبًا.
text.en: It may be of something that is not a measure, as hādhā khātamun ḥadīdan “this is a ring of iron” and wa-siwārun dhahaban “and a bracelet of gold”, and in this khafḍ is more common. It may come after the sentence to remove the vagueness from its attribution, as ṭāba Zaydun nafsan “Zayd is pleasant in soul”, or ʿilman “in knowledge”, or aban “as to a father”.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمُسْتَثْنَى لَفْظٌ يُذْكَرُ بَعْدَ إِلَّا وَأَخَوَاتِهَا لِيُعْلَمَ أَنَّهُ لَا يُنْسَبُ إِلَيْهِ مَا نُسِبَ إِلَى مَا قَبْلَهَا، وَهُوَ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: مُتَّصِلٌ، وَهُوَ مَا أُخْرِجَ عَنْ مُتَعَدِّدٍ بِإِلَّا وَأَخَوَاتِهَا، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ إِلَّا زَيْدًا، وَمُنْقَطِعٌ، وَهُوَ الْمَذْكُورُ بَعْدَ إِلَّا وَأَخَوَاتِهَا غَيْرَ مُخْرَجٍ عَنْ مُتَعَدِّدٍ؛ لِعَدَمِ دُخُولِهِ فِي الْمُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ إِلَّا حِمَارًا.
text.en: Section. The excepted (mustathnā) is an utterance mentioned after illā and its sisters, so that it be known that what is attributed to what comes before it is not attributed to it. It is of two kinds. Connected (muttaṣil), which is what is taken out of a plurality by illā and its sisters, as jāʾanī al-qawmu illā Zaydan “the people came to me except Zayd”; and disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), which is what is mentioned after illā and its sisters without being taken out of a plurality, because it was not included in that from which the exception is made (mustathnā minhu), as jāʾanī al-qawmu illā ḥimāran “the people came to me, except a donkey”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ إِعْرَابَ الْمُسْتَثْنَى عَلَى أَرْبَعَةِ أَقْسَامٍ: فَإِنْ كَانَ مُتَّصِلًا وَقَعَ بَعْدَ إِلَّا فِي كَلَامٍ مُوجَبٍ، أَوْ مُنْقَطِعًا، كَمَا مَرَّ، أَوْ مُقَدَّمًا عَلَى الْمُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ، نَحْوُ: مَا جَاءَنِي إِلَّا زَيْدًا أَحَدٌ، أَوْ كَانَ بَعْدَ خَلَا وَعَدَا عِنْدَ الْأَكْثَرِ، أَوْ بَعْدَ مَا خَلَا وَمَا عَدَا وَلَيْسَ وَلَا يَكُونُ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ خَلَا زَيْدًا، إِلَى آخِرِهِ، كَانَ مَنْصُوبًا.
text.en: Know that the iʿrāb of the mustathnā is of four kinds. If it is connected and stands after illā in affirmative speech (kalām mūjab), or is disconnected, as has passed, or is put before the mustathnā minhu, as mā jāʾanī illā Zaydan aḥadun “no one came to me except Zayd”, or is after khalā and ʿadā according to most, or after mā khalā, mā ʿadā, laysa and lā yakūnu, as jāʾanī al-qawmu khalā Zaydan “the people came to me, save Zayd”, to the end, it is manṣūb.

lessons.title: The mustathnā in other states; ghayr and illā
body: The second kind: after illā in speech that is not affirmative, “all speech in which there is a negation, a prohibition or a question”, with what it is excepted from named, two ways are allowed: naṣb as an exception, or a badal of the word before: mā jāʾanī aḥadun illā Zaydan, or illā Zaydun, Zaydun replacing aḥadun in its rafʿ.

The third kind is the emptied exception (mufarragh): after illā in speech that is not affirmative, with nothing named to except from. Then “its iʿrāb is according to the governors”: mā jāʾanī illā Zaydun, where Zaydun is the fāʿil; mā raʾaytu illā Zaydan, the object; mā marartu illā bi-Zaydin. The governor has been “emptied” for the word after illā, which only limits the negation: “none came but Zayd” is “Zayd alone came”.

The fourth kind: in jarr, after ghayr, siwā and sawāʾ, and after ḥāshā “according to most”: jāʾanī al-qawmu ghayra Zaydin, siwā Zaydin, sawāʾa Zaydin, ḥāshā Zaydin. Here the excepted noun is a muḍāf ilayhi. Ghayr itself then takes the iʿrāb the excepted noun would have taken after illā: ghayra in affirmative speech, ghayra ḥimārin when disconnected, mā jāʾanī ghayra Zaydin al-qawmu when put first, ghayru or ghayra after aḥadun, and in the emptied exception whatever the governor needs: mā jāʾanī ghayru Zaydin, mā raʾaytu ghayra Zaydin, mā marartu bi-ghayri Zaydin.

“The word ghayr is laid down for the adjective and is sometimes used for exception, just as illā is laid down for exception and is sometimes used for the adjective”: law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā Allāhu la-fasadatā (Q 21:22), “that is, ghayru Allāhi”. The book adds lā ilāha illā Allāhu to this. Many grammarians parse that phrase otherwise, with illā as the particle of exception and Allāhu as a badal of the place of lā with its ism; the student should know both.

terms.en: speech with a negation, a prohibition or a question
the mustathnā taking the place and iʿrāb of the word before it
the emptied exception: nothing named to except from
words of exception after which the noun is in jarr

examples.arabic: مَا جَاءَنِي أَحَدٌ إِلَّا زَيْدًا، وَإِلَّا زَيْدٌ

tasks.prompt: Give the iʿrāb of Zayd and the kind of exception: mā jāʾanī aḥadun illā Zaydun; mā raʾaytu illā Zaydan; jāʾanī al-qawmu ḥāshā Zaydin.
tasks.arabic: مَا جَاءَنِي أَحَدٌ إِلَّا زَيْدٌ — مَا رَأَيْتُ إِلَّا زَيْدًا — جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ حَاشَا زَيْدٍ
tasks.answer: Illā Zaydun: speech not affirmative, the whole named; Zaydun is a badal of aḥadun, in rafʿ (naṣb would also be allowed). Illā Zaydan: the emptied exception; Zaydan is the object of raʾaytu. Ḥāshā Zaydin: in jarr after ḥāshā, according to most.

tasks.prompt: Put ghayr in place of illā and give its iʿrāb: jāʾanī al-qawmu illā Zaydan; mā jāʾanī illā Zaydun.
tasks.answer: Jāʾanī al-qawmu ghayra Zaydin: ghayra in naṣb, as Zaydan was. Mā jāʾanī ghayru Zaydin: ghayru in rafʿ, the fāʿil, as Zaydun was. In both, Zayd after ghayr is in jarr as a muḍāf ilayhi.

tasks.prompt: Why is the exception in mā marartu illā bi-Zaydin called “emptied”?
tasks.answer: Nothing is named to except from, so the governor (marartu with its bāʾ) is emptied for the word after illā and works on it directly: bi-Zaydin takes the iʿrāb the governor needs. Illā only limits the negation.

tasks.prompt: How does the book read illā in Q 21:22, and what other reading of lā ilāha illā Allāhu do many grammarians give?
tasks.answer: In Q 21:22 illā is used as an adjective, “other than God” (ghayru Allāhi), and the book reads lā ilāha illā Allāhu the same way. Many grammarians take illā there as the particle of exception, with Allāhu a badal of the place of lā and its ism.
