text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ إِلَّا فِي كَلَامٍ غَيْرِ مُوجَبٍ، وَهُوَ كُلُّ كَلَامٍ يَكُونُ فِيهِ نَفْيٌ أَوْ نَهْيٌ أَوِ اسْتِفْهَامٌ، وَالْمُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ مَذْكُورٌ، يَجُوزُ فِيهِ الْوَجْهَانِ: النَّصْبُ، وَالْبَدَلُ عَمَّا قَبْلَهُ، نَحْوُ: مَا جَاءَنِي أَحَدٌ إِلَّا زَيْدًا، وَإِلَّا زَيْدٌ.
text.en: If it is after illā in speech that is not affirmative — that is, all speech in which there is a negation, a prohibition or a question — and the mustathnā minhu is mentioned, both ways are allowed in it: naṣb, and [making it] a badal of what is before it, as mā jāʾanī aḥadun illā Zaydan “no one came to me except Zayd” and wa-illā Zaydun.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ مُفَرَّغًا، بِأَنْ يَكُونَ بَعْدَ إِلَّا فِي كَلَامٍ غَيْرِ مُوجَبٍ وَالْمُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ غَيْرُ مَذْكُورٍ، كَانَ إِعْرَابُهُ بِحَسَبِ الْعَوَامِلِ، تَقُولُ: مَا جَاءَنِي إِلَّا زَيْدٌ، وَمَا رَأَيْتُ إِلَّا زَيْدًا، وَمَا مَرَرْتُ إِلَّا بِزَيْدٍ. وَإِنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ غَيْرٍ وَسِوًى وَسَوَاءٍ، وَحَاشَا عِنْدَ الْأَكْثَرِ، كَانَ مَجْرُورًا، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ غَيْرَ زَيْدٍ، وَسِوَى زَيْدٍ، وَسَوَاءَ زَيْدٍ، وَحَاشَا زَيْدٍ.
text.en: If it is emptied (mufarragh), in that it is after illā in speech that is not affirmative and the mustathnā minhu is not mentioned, its iʿrāb is according to the governors; you say mā jāʾanī illā Zaydun “none came to me but Zayd”, wa-mā raʾaytu illā Zaydan “and I saw none but Zayd” and wa-mā marartu illā bi-Zaydin “and I passed by none but Zayd”. If it is after ghayrin, siwan and sawāʾin, and after ḥāshā according to most, it is majrūr, as jāʾanī al-qawmu ghayra Zaydin “the people came to me, other than Zayd”, wa-siwā Zaydin, wa-sawāʾa Zaydin and wa-ḥāshā Zaydin.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ إِعْرَابَ غَيْرٍ كَإِعْرَابِ الْمُسْتَثْنَى بِإِلَّا، تَقُولُ: جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ غَيْرَ زَيْدٍ، وَغَيْرَ حِمَارٍ، وَمَا جَاءَنِي غَيْرَ زَيْدٍ الْقَوْمُ، وَمَا جَاءَنِي أَحَدٌ غَيْرُ زَيْدٍ، وَغَيْرَ زَيْدٍ، وَمَا جَاءَنِي غَيْرُ زَيْدٍ، وَمَا رَأَيْتُ غَيْرَ زَيْدٍ، وَمَا مَرَرْتُ بِغَيْرِ زَيْدٍ.
text.en: Know that the iʿrāb of ghayr is like the iʿrāb of what is excepted by illā; you say jāʾanī al-qawmu ghayra Zaydin “the people came to me, other than Zayd”, wa-ghayra ḥimārin “and other than a donkey”, wa-mā jāʾanī ghayra Zaydin al-qawmu “and none of the people came to me, other than Zayd”, wa-mā jāʾanī aḥadun ghayru Zaydin “and no one other than Zayd came to me” and wa-ghayra Zaydin, wa-mā jāʾanī ghayru Zaydin “and none but Zayd came to me”, wa-mā raʾaytu ghayra Zaydin “and I saw none but Zayd” and wa-mā marartu bi-ghayri Zaydin “and I passed by none but Zayd”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ لَفْظَةَ غَيْرٍ مَوْضُوعَةٌ لِلصِّفَةِ، وَقَدْ تُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلِاسْتِثْنَاءِ، كَمَا أَنَّ لَفْظَةَ إِلَّا مَوْضُوعَةٌ لِلِاسْتِثْنَاءِ، وَقَدْ تُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلصِّفَةِ، كَمَا فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا، أَيْ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ، وَكَذَلِكَ قَوْلُكَ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ.
text.en: Know that the word ghayr is laid down for the adjective (ṣifa) and is sometimes used for exception, just as the word illā is laid down for exception and is sometimes used for the adjective, as in His saying, exalted is He: law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā Allāhu la-fasadatā “if there were in them gods other than God, they would both have been ruined”, that is, ghayru Allāhi “other than God”; and so too your saying lā ilāha illā Allāhu “there is no god but God”.

lessons.title: The khabar of kāna, the ism of inna, the ism of lā, the khabar of mā
body: The khabar of kāna and its sisters is “that which is said after they have come in”: kāna Zaydun qāʾiman. It is like the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, with one freedom more: it may come before its ism “even when it is definite”, kāna al-qāʾima Zaydun. A definite khabar of a mubtadaʾ could not do that, since the hearer could not tell which was which; after kāna the iʿrāb tells. The ism of inna and its sisters is that of which something is said after they come in: inna Zaydan qāʾimun.

The noun in naṣb by the lā that denies the kind is an indefinite muḍāf following it, lā ghulāma rajulin fī al-dāri, or one like a muḍāf, lā ʿishrīna dirhaman fī al-kīsi. A single indefinite after lā is built on fatḥa: lā rajula fī al-dāri. If the noun is definite, or separated from lā, it is in rafʿ and lā must be repeated with another noun: lā Zaydun fī al-dāri wa-lā ʿAmrun; lā fīhā rajulun wa-lā imraʾatun.

With a repeated lā, as in lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi, five ways are allowed: fatḥa on both; rafʿ in both; fatḥa on the first and naṣb in the second; fatḥa on the first and rafʿ in the second; rafʿ in the first and fatḥa on the second. The ism of lā may be dropped with a context: lā ʿalayka, “that is, lā baʾsa ʿalayka”.

The khabar of mā and lā like laysa is in naṣb: mā Zaydun qāʾiman, lā rajulun ḥāḍiran. Their work is cancelled in three cases: when the khabar comes after illā, mā Zaydun illā qāʾimun; when it comes before the ism, mā qāʾimun Zaydun; and when in is added after mā, mā in Zaydun qāʾimun. This is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. The Banū Tamīm never let mā and lā govern at all.

The book proves it with a verse said “in the tongue of the Banū Tamīm”: wa-muhafhafin ka-l-ghuṣni qultu lahu intasib, fa-ajāba mā qatlu al-muḥibbi ḥarāmu, “a slender one like a branch, I told him: tell me your lineage! He answered: killing the lover is not forbidden”. The answer is a lover's teasing and a grammatical proof at once: by saying ḥarāmu in rafʿ after mā, he showed that he was of Tamīm.

terms.en: the khabar of kāna, in naṣb; it may come first even when definite
the ism of the lā of the kind: in naṣb, or built when single
repeating lā, required when its noun is definite or separated
the Ḥijāzī dialect, which lets mā govern, and that of Tamīm, which does not

examples.en: a definite khabar of kāna before its ism
the ism of lā, muḍāf: in naṣb
a single indefinite: built on fatḥa
after illā: mā does not govern

tasks.prompt: Give the state of the ism of lā and the reason: lā rajula fī al-dāri; lā ghulāma rajulin fī al-dāri; lā Zaydun fī al-dāri wa-lā ʿAmrun.
tasks.arabic: لَا رَجُلَ فِي الدَّارِ — لَا غُلَامَ رَجُلٍ فِي الدَّارِ — لَا زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ وَلَا عَمْرٌو
tasks.answer: Rajula: a single indefinite, built on fatḥa. Ghulāma: an indefinite muḍāf, in naṣb. Zaydun: definite, so in rafʿ, and lā is repeated with ʿAmrun.

tasks.prompt: Why may one say kāna al-qāʾima Zaydun, putting a definite khabar first?
tasks.answer: After kāna the iʿrāb shows which is which: al-qāʾima is in naṣb, the khabar, and Zaydun in rafʿ, the ism. With a mubtadaʾ and khabar, both in rafʿ, a definite khabar put first could not be told apart.

tasks.prompt: Does mā govern in each? mā Zaydun qāʾiman; mā Zaydun illā qāʾimun; mā qāʾimun Zaydun; mā in Zaydun qāʾimun.
tasks.answer: In the first it governs (the Ḥijāzī way): qāʾiman in naṣb. In the other three it does not: the khabar comes after illā, or before the ism, or in is added after mā; so the khabar is in rafʿ.

tasks.prompt: How does the poet's verse prove the dialect of Tamīm?
tasks.answer: Asked his lineage, the youth answered mā qatlu al-muḥibbi ḥarāmu, with ḥarāmu in rafʿ after mā. In the Ḥijāzī dialect mā would put the khabar in naṣb (ḥarāman); the rafʿ shows the Tamīmī way, so his grammar told his lineage.

quiz.explanation: Fatḥa, rafʿ and naṣb in five pairings.

quiz.explanation: The work of mā is cancelled.

quiz.explanation: The governing is the dialect of the Ḥijāz.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: خَبَرُ كَانَ وَأَخَوَاتِهَا، هُوَ الْمُسْنَدُ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهَا، نَحْوُ: كَانَ زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا، وَحُكْمُهُ كَحُكْمِ خَبَرِ الْمُبْتَدَإِ، إِلَّا أَنَّهُ يَجُوزُ تَقْدِيمُهُ عَلَى اسْمِهَا مَعَ كَوْنِهِ مَعْرِفَةً، بِخِلَافِ الْمُبْتَدَإِ، نَحْوُ: كَانَ الْقَائِمَ زَيْدٌ. فَصْلٌ: اسْمُ إِنَّ وَأَخَوَاتِهَا، هُوَ الْمُسْنَدُ إِلَيْهِ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهَا، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ.
text.en: Section. The khabar of kāna and its sisters: it is that which is said after they have come in, as kāna Zaydun qāʾiman “Zayd was standing”. Its rule is like the rule of the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, except that it may be put before its ism even when it is definite, unlike [the khabar of] the mubtadaʾ, as kāna al-qāʾima Zaydun “the one standing was Zayd”. Section. The ism of inna and its sisters: it is that of which something is said after they have come in, as inna Zaydan qāʾimun “Zayd is indeed standing”.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَنْصُوبُ بِلَا الَّتِي لِنَفْيِ الْجِنْسِ، هُوَ الْمُسْنَدُ إِلَيْهِ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهَا، يَلِيهَا نَكِرَةً مُضَافَةً، نَحْوُ: لَا غُلَامَ رَجُلٍ فِي الدَّارِ، أَوْ مُشَابِهًا لَهَا، نَحْوُ: لَا عِشْرِينَ دِرْهَمًا فِي الْكِيسِ. فَإِنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ لَا نَكِرَةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ تُبْنَى عَلَى الْفَتْحِ، نَحْوُ: لَا رَجُلَ فِي الدَّارِ.
text.en: Section. The noun in naṣb by the lā that denies the kind: it is that of which something is said after it has come in, following it as an indefinite muḍāf, as lā ghulāma rajulin fī al-dāri “there is no man's servant in the house”, or as one like the muḍāf, as lā ʿishrīna dirhaman fī al-kīsi “there are no twenty dirhams in the purse”. If after lā there is a single indefinite, it is fixed on the fatḥa, as lā rajula fī al-dāri “there is no man in the house”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ مَعْرِفَةً، أَوْ نَكِرَةً مَفْصُولًا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ لَا، كَانَ مَرْفُوعًا، وَيَجِبُ تَكْرِيرُ لَا مَعَ اسْمٍ آخَرَ، تَقُولُ: لَا زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ وَلَا عَمْرٌو، وَلَا فِيهَا رَجُلٌ وَلَا امْرَأَةٌ. وَيَجُوزُ فِي مِثْلِ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، خَمْسَةُ أَوْجُهٍ: فَتْحُهُمَا، وَرَفْعُهُمَا، وَفَتْحُ الْأَوَّلِ وَنَصْبُ الثَّانِي، وَفَتْحُ الْأَوَّلِ وَرَفْعُ الثَّانِي، وَرَفْعُ الْأَوَّلِ وَفَتْحُ الثَّانِي. وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ اسْمُ لَا لِقَرِينَةٍ، نَحْوُ: لَا عَلَيْكَ، أَيْ لَا بَأْسَ عَلَيْكَ.
text.en: If it is definite, or an indefinite separated from lā, it is marfūʿ, and lā must be repeated with another noun; you say lā Zaydun fī al-dāri wa-lā ʿAmrun “neither Zayd is in the house nor ʿAmr” and lā fīhā rajulun wa-lā imraʾatun “in it there is neither man nor woman”. In such [a phrase] as lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi “there is no might and no power except through God”, five ways are allowed: a fatḥa on both; rafʿ in both; a fatḥa on the first and naṣb in the second; a fatḥa on the first and rafʿ in the second; and rafʿ in the first and a fatḥa on the second. The ism of lā may be dropped because of an indication, as lā ʿalayka “no [harm] on you”, that is, lā baʾsa ʿalayka “there is no harm on you”.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: خَبَرُ مَا وَلَا الْمُشَبَّهَتَيْنِ بِلَيْسَ، هُوَ الْمُسْنَدُ بَعْدَ دُخُولِهِمَا، نَحْوُ: مَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا، وَلَا رَجُلٌ حَاضِرًا. وَإِنْ وَقَعَ الْخَبَرُ بَعْدَ إِلَّا، نَحْوُ: مَا زَيْدٌ إِلَّا قَائِمٌ، أَوْ تَقَدَّمَ الْخَبَرُ عَلَى الِاسْمِ، نَحْوُ: مَا قَائِمٌ زَيْدٌ، أَوْ زِيدَتْ إِنْ بَعْدَ مَا، نَحْوُ: مَا إِنْ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، بَطَلَ الْعَمَلُ، كَمَا رَأَيْتَ فِي الْأَمْثِلَةِ. وَهَذِهِ لُغَةُ أَهْلِ الْحِجَازِ؛ أَمَّا بَنُو تَمِيمٍ فَلَا يُعْمِلُونَهُمَا أَصْلًا، قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ عَنْ لِسَانِ بَنِي تَمِيمٍ: وَمُهَفْهَفٍ كَالْغُصْنِ قُلْتُ لَهُ انْتَسِبْ * فَأَجَابَ مَا قَتْلُ الْمُحِبِّ حَرَامُ، بِرَفْعِ حَرَامٍ.
text.en: Section. The khabar of mā and lā that resemble laysa: it is that which is said after they have come in, as mā Zaydun qāʾiman “Zayd is not standing” and wa-lā rajulun ḥāḍiran “and no man is present”. If the khabar stands after illā, as mā Zaydun illā qāʾimun “Zayd is nothing but standing”, or the khabar comes before the ism, as mā qāʾimun Zaydun “not standing is Zayd”, or in is added after mā, as mā in Zaydun qāʾimun “Zayd is not standing”, the governing is cancelled, as you have seen in the examples. This is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; as for the Banū Tamīm, they do not let them govern at all. The poet said, in the tongue of the Banū Tamīm: wa-muhafhafin ka-al-ghuṣni qultu lahu intasib / fa-ajāba mā qatlu al-muḥibbi ḥarāmu “And [many] a slender one like the branch, to whom I said: tell your lineage! / He answered: the killing of the lover is not forbidden”, with rafʿ in ḥarāmu.

lessons.title: The majrūr: the muḍāf ilayhi; iḍāfa of meaning and of wording
body: The third aim is short: “the majrūr nouns are only the muḍāf ilayhi”. The book takes the term widely, as the Kāfiya does: it is “every noun to which something is related by means of a particle of jarr”, either expressed, marartu bi-Zaydin, which the terminology calls a jārr and majrūr, or implied, ghulāmu Zaydin, “whose underlying form is ghulāmun li-Zaydin”, which the terminology calls a muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi. So the particles of jarr and the iḍāfa are one subject, seen from two sides.
The muḍāf must be stripped of its tanwīn, “or of what stands in its place, the nūn of the dual and of the plural”: ghulāmu Zaydin, ghulāmā Zaydin, muslimū Miṣra (lesson 6).

Iḍāfa is of two kinds. Iḍāfa of meaning (maʿnawiyya) is any iḍāfa in which the muḍāf is not an adjective made muḍāf to the word it governs. It has the sense of the lām, ghulāmu Zaydin, “a servant belonging to Zayd”; or of min, khātamu fiḍḍatin, “a ring of silver”, when the second is the stuff the first is made of; or of fī, ṣalātu al-layli, “the prayer in the night”. It gives the muḍāf definiteness, if the muḍāf ilayhi is definite, ghulāmu Zaydin, or particularity, if it is indefinite, ghulāmu rajulin, “a man's servant”: not a known servant, but no longer any servant.

Iḍāfa of wording (lafẓiyya) is an adjective made muḍāf to the word it governs: ḍāribu Zaydin, ḥasanu al-wajhi. It is “taken as separated”: in meaning it is still ḍāribun Zaydan, ḥasanun wajhuhu. “Its benefit is lightness in the wording only”: a tanwīn or a nūn is dropped, and nothing else changes. That is why ḍāribu Zaydin stays indefinite; the Qurʾān describes an indefinite with such a phrase: hadyan bāligha al-kaʿbati (Q 5:95).

terms.en: the noun something is related to by a particle of jarr, expressed or implied
the particle of jarr and the noun it governs
iḍāfa of meaning: definiteness or particularity
iḍāfa of wording: an adjective with its governed word, lightness only

examples.en: a jārr and majrūr: the particle expressed
a muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi: ghulāmun li-Zaydin
iḍāfa in the sense of min
iḍāfa in the sense of fī
iḍāfa of wording

tasks.prompt: Give the sense of each iḍāfa of meaning: ghulāmu Zaydin; khātamu fiḍḍatin; ṣalātu al-layli.
tasks.arabic: غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ — خَاتَمُ فِضَّةٍ — صَلَاةُ اللَّيْلِ
tasks.answer: Ghulāmu Zaydin: the lām, ghulāmun li-Zaydin, “a servant belonging to Zayd”. Khātamu fiḍḍatin: min, “a ring of silver”. Ṣalātu al-layli: fī, “the prayer in the night”.

tasks.prompt: Why does ghulāmu Zaydin become definite, but ḍāribu Zaydin does not?
tasks.answer: Ghulāmu Zaydin is an iḍāfa of meaning, which makes the muḍāf definite when the muḍāf ilayhi is definite. Ḍāribu Zaydin is an iḍāfa of wording, an adjective with its governed word; it is taken as separated (ḍāribun Zaydan) and gives only lightness, so it stays indefinite.

tasks.prompt: Put each into iḍāfa: ghulāmāni li-Zaydin; muslimūna min Miṣra.
tasks.answer: Ghulāmā Zaydin and muslimū Miṣra: the nūn of the dual and of the plural, which stands in the place of the tanwīn, is dropped in iḍāfa.

tasks.prompt: How does the book count the majrūr, and what two constructions does it put under one head?
tasks.answer: Only one majrūr, the muḍāf ilayhi. Under it come the noun after an expressed particle of jarr (jārr and majrūr, marartu bi-Zaydin) and the noun after an implied one (muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi, ghulāmu Zaydin).

quiz.prompt: The book counts the majrūr nouns as…
quiz.explanation: With the particle of jarr expressed or implied.

options: tanwīn and the nūn of the dual and plural

Iḍāfa of wording is…
options: an adjective made muḍāf to its governed word
iḍāfa in the sense of fī

quiz.prompt: The benefit of iḍāfa of wording is…

text.original: الْأَسْمَاءُ الْمَجْرُورَةُ هِيَ الْمُضَافُ إِلَيْهِ فَقَطْ، وَهُوَ كُلُّ اسْمٍ نُسِبَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ بِوَاسِطَةِ حَرْفِ الْجَرِّ لَفْظًا، نَحْوُ: مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ، وَيُعَبَّرُ عَنْ هَذَا التَّرْكِيبِ فِي الِاصْطِلَاحِ بِأَنَّهُ جَارٌّ وَمَجْرُورٌ، أَوْ تَقْدِيرًا، نَحْوُ: غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ، تَقْدِيرُهُ: غُلَامٌ لِزَيْدٍ، وَيُعَبَّرُ عَنْهُ فِي الِاصْطِلَاحِ بِأَنَّهُ مُضَافٌ وَمُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ. وَيَجِبُ تَجْرِيدُ الْمُضَافِ عَنِ التَّنْوِينِ، أَوْ مَا يَقُومُ مَقَامَهُ، وَهُوَ نُونُ التَّثْنِيَةِ وَالْجَمْعِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ، وَغُلَامَا زَيْدٍ، وَمُسْلِمُو مِصْرَ.
text.en: The majrūr nouns are only the muḍāf ilayhi: it is every noun to which something is related by means of a particle of jarr, expressed, as marartu bi-Zaydin “I passed by Zayd” — in the terminology this construction is described as a jārr and a majrūr —, or implied, as ghulāmu Zaydin “Zayd's servant”, whose underlying form is ghulāmun li-Zaydin “a servant belonging to Zayd” — in the terminology it is described as a muḍāf and a muḍāf ilayhi. The muḍāf must be stripped of the tanwīn, or of what stands in its place, namely the nūn of the dual and of the plural, as jāʾanī ghulāmu Zaydin “Zayd's servant came to me”, wa-ghulāmā Zaydin “and Zayd's two servants” and wa-muslimū Miṣra “and the Muslims of Egypt”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْإِضَافَةَ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: مَعْنَوِيَّةٌ وَلَفْظِيَّةٌ. أَمَّا الْمَعْنَوِيَّةُ فَهِيَ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْمُضَافُ غَيْرَ صِفَةٍ مُضَافَةٍ إِلَى مَعْمُولِهَا، وَهِيَ إِمَّا بِمَعْنَى اللَّامِ، نَحْوُ: غُلَامُ زَيْدٍ، أَوْ بِمَعْنَى مِنْ، نَحْوُ: خَاتَمُ فِضَّةٍ، أَوْ بِمَعْنَى فِي، نَحْوُ: صَلَاةُ اللَّيْلِ. وَفَائِدَةُ هَذِهِ الْإِضَافَةِ تَعْرِيفُ الْمُضَافِ إِنْ أُضِيفَ إِلَى مَعْرِفَةٍ، كَمَا مَرَّ، أَوْ تَخْصِيصُهُ إِنْ أُضِيفَ إِلَى نَكِرَةٍ، كَغُلَامِ رَجُلٍ.
text.en: Know that iḍāfa is of two kinds: by meaning (maʿnawiyya) and in the wording (lafẓiyya). Iḍāfa by meaning is that the muḍāf is not an adjective made muḍāf to its governed word. It is either in the meaning of the lām, as ghulāmu Zaydin “Zayd's servant”; or in the meaning of min, as khātamu fiḍḍatin “a ring of silver”; or in the meaning of fī, as ṣalātu al-layli “the prayer in the night”. The benefit of this iḍāfa is that the muḍāf becomes definite if it is made muḍāf to a definite noun, as has passed, or particular if it is made muḍāf to an indefinite, as ghulāmi rajulin “a man's servant”.

text.original: وَأَمَّا اللَّفْظِيَّةُ فَهِيَ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْمُضَافُ صِفَةً مُضَافَةً إِلَى مَعْمُولِهَا، وَهِيَ فِي تَقْدِيرِ الِانْفِصَالِ، نَحْوُ: ضَارِبُ زَيْدٍ، وَحَسَنُ الْوَجْهِ، وَفَائِدَتُهَا تَخْفِيفٌ فِي اللَّفْظِ فَقَطْ.
text.en: The iḍāfa in the wording is that the muḍāf is an adjective made muḍāf to its governed word; it is [still] taken as separated, as ḍāribu Zaydin “the hitter of Zayd” and ḥasanu al-wajhi “beautiful of face”; its benefit is lightness in the wording only.

lessons.title: The noun with the yāʾ of the speaker; the six nouns; dhū
body: A sound noun, or one that runs like the sound (lesson 5), made muḍāf to the yāʾ of the speaker takes a kasra on its end, and the yāʾ may have a sukūn or a fatḥa: ghulāmī or ghulāmiya, dalwī, ẓabyī. If the noun ends in an alif, the alif stays and the yāʾ takes a fatḥa: ʿaṣāya, “my stick”, raḥāya, “my mill”. The tribe of Hudhayl say instead ʿaṣayya and raḥayya, turning the alif into a yāʾ and merging it with the pronoun.

If the noun ends in a yāʾ after a kasra, the two yāʾs are merged and the second takes a fatḥa, “lest two unvowelled letters meet”: qāḍin, qāḍiyya, “my judge”. If it ends in a wāw after a ḍamma, the wāw is turned into a yāʾ and the same is done: muslimiyya, as in lesson 6.

The six nouns with the yāʾ of the speaker lose their letters of iʿrāb: akhī, abī, ḥamī, hanī; and fiyya, “my mouth”, “according to most”, or famī “according to some”. Dhū is “never made muḍāf to a pronoun”: it is always followed by a noun of a kind, dhū mālin, dhū ʿilmin. The poet's line innamā yaʿrifu dhā al-faḍli mina al-nāsi dhawūhu, “only those who have it know the man of merit”, with dhawūhu, is “irregular” (shādhdh): it is heard, and kept, but not taken as a model.

Cut off from iḍāfa, the five take tanwīn: akhun, abun, ḥamun, hanun, and famun, where the mīm stands for the lost wāw of fū. Dhū is never cut off from iḍāfa. All this has been iḍāfa with an implied particle of jarr; the particles themselves, expressed, come in the third part.

terms.en: the yāʾ of the speaker, “my”
the dialect of Hudhayl: ʿaṣayya for ʿaṣāya
irregular: heard from the Arabs, kept, but not a model
“possessor of”: never muḍāf to a pronoun, never cut off

examples.en: a sound noun and those like it: the kasra before the yāʾ
the alif stays, the yāʾ takes fatḥa
two yāʾs merged, the second with fatḥa
the six nouns with the yāʾ of the speaker

tasks.prompt: Add the yāʾ of the speaker as the book teaches: ghulām; ʿaṣan; qāḍin; muslimūna.
tasks.answer: Ghulāmī (or ghulāmiya); ʿaṣāya (the alif stays, the yāʾ with fatḥa); qāḍiyya (the yāʾs merged, the second with fatḥa); muslimiyya (the wāw turned into a yāʾ and merged).

tasks.prompt: Why does the second yāʾ of qāḍiyya take a fatḥa?
tasks.answer: The yāʾ of the noun and the yāʾ of the speaker are merged; if the second had a sukūn, two unvowelled letters would meet. So it is given a fatḥa.

tasks.prompt: Why is dhawūhu in the poet's line called irregular?
tasks.arabic: إِنَّمَا يَعْرِفُ ذَا الْفَضْلِ مِنَ النَّاسِ ذَوُوهُ
tasks.answer: Dhū is never made muḍāf to a pronoun, and dhawūhu is the plural of dhū made muḍāf to the hāʾ. The Arabs said it, so it is kept, but it breaks the rule and is not imitated.

tasks.prompt: Give the six nouns cut off from iḍāfa, and say which cannot be.
tasks.answer: Akhun, abun, ḥamun, hanun, famun. Dhū can never be cut off from iḍāfa.

quiz.explanation: It is kept as heard, not used as a model.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّكَ إِذَا أَضَفْتَ الِاسْمَ الصَّحِيحَ وَالْجَارِيَ مَجْرَى الصَّحِيحِ إِلَى يَاءِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ كَسَرْتَ آخِرَهُ، وَأَسْكَنْتَ الْيَاءَ أَوْ فَتَحْتَهَا، كَغُلَامِي وَدَلْوِي وَظَبْيِي، وَإِنْ كَانَ آخِرُ الِاسْمِ أَلِفًا تَثْبُتُ، كَعَصَايَ وَرَحَايَ، خِلَافًا لِلْهُذَيْلِ، كَعَصَيَّ وَرَحَيَّ.
text.en: Know that when you make a sound noun, or one that runs like the sound, muḍāf to the yāʾ of the speaker, you give its end a kasra and give the yāʾ a sukūn or a fatḥa, as ghulāmī “my servant”, wa-dalwī “my bucket” and wa-ẓabyī “my gazelle”. If the end of the noun is an alif, it stays, as ʿaṣāya “my stick” and wa-raḥāya “my mill”, unlike [the dialect of] Hudhayl: ʿaṣayya and wa-raḥayya.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ آخِرُ الِاسْمِ يَاءً مَكْسُورًا مَا قَبْلَهَا أُدْغِمَتِ الْيَاءُ فِي الْيَاءِ وَفُتِحَتِ الْيَاءُ الثَّانِيَةُ؛ لِئَلَّا يَلْتَقِيَ السَّاكِنَانِ، تَقُولُ فِي قَاضٍ: قَاضِيَّ، وَإِنْ كَانَ آخِرُهُ وَاوًا مَضْمُومًا مَا قَبْلَهَا قَلَبْتَهَا يَاءً، وَعَمِلْتَ كَمَا عَمِلْتَ الْآنَ، تَقُولُ: جَاءَنِي مُسْلِمِيَّ.
text.en: If the end of the noun is a yāʾ with a kasra before it, the yāʾ is assimilated into the yāʾ and the second yāʾ is given a fatḥa, lest two unvowelled letters meet; you say for qāḍin “a judge” qāḍiyya “my judge”. If its end is a wāw with a ḍamma before it, you turn it into a yāʾ and do as you have just done; you say jāʾanī muslimiyya “my Muslims came to me”.

text.original: وَالْأَسْمَاءُ السِّتَّةُ مُضَافَةً إِلَى يَاءِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ تَقُولُ: أَخِي، وَأَبِي، وَحَمِي، وَهَنِي، وَفِيَّ عِنْدَ الْأَكْثَرِ، وَفَمِي عِنْدَ قَوْمٍ. وَذُو لَا يُضَافُ إِلَى مُضْمَرٍ أَصْلًا، وَقَوْلُ الْقَائِلِ، شِعْرٌ: إِنَّمَا يَعْرِفُ ذَا الْفَضْلِ مِنَ النَّاسِ ذَوُوهُ، شَاذٌّ. وَإِذَا قُطِعَتْ هَذِهِ الْأَسْمَاءُ عَنِ الْإِضَافَةِ قُلْتَ: أَخٌ، وَأَبٌ، وَحَمٌ، وَهَنٌ، وَفَمٌ، وَذُو لَا يُقْطَعُ عَنِ الْإِضَافَةِ الْبَتَّةَ. هَذَا كُلُّهُ بِتَقْدِيرِ حَرْفِ الْجَرِّ، أَمَّا مَا يُذْكَرُ فِيهِ حَرْفُ الْجَرِّ لَفْظًا فَسَيَأْتِيكَ فِي الْقِسْمِ الثَّالِثِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.
text.en: The six nouns muḍāf to the yāʾ of the speaker: you say akhī “my brother”, abī “my father”, ḥamī “my father-in-law”, hanī “my thing”, and fiyya “my mouth” according to most, famī according to some. Dhū is never made muḍāf to a pronoun; and the saying of the poet, verse: innamā yaʿrifu dhā al-faḍli mina al-nāsi dhawūhu “only those who have it know the man of merit among people”, is irregular. When these nouns are cut off from iḍāfa you say akhun, abun, ḥamun, hanun and famun; and dhū is never cut off from iḍāfa. All this is with an implied particle of jarr; as for that in which the particle of jarr is mentioned in the wording, it will come to you in the third part, if God Most High wills.

lessons.title: The followers; the adjective
body: All the nouns so far had their iʿrāb “in themselves” (bi-l-aṣāla): a governor came into each. A noun may also have its iʿrāb “by following” (bi-l-tabaʿiyya) the word before it: it is then a follower (tābiʿ), “every second word inflected with the iʿrāb of the one before it, from one aspect”. The commentators explain the last words: a khabar has the same rafʿ as its mubtadaʾ, but from another aspect, as what is said of it, so it is not a follower. The followers are five: the adjective (naʿt), ʿaṭf by particles, emphasis, the badal and the explanatory ʿaṭf.

The adjective “indicates a meaning in the word it follows”, jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun, or “in something connected with it”, jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun abūhu; it is also called ṣifa. The first kind follows its noun in ten things: the three states of iʿrāb, definiteness and indefiniteness, the three numbers and the two genders: rajulun ʿālimun, rajulāni ʿālimāni, rijālun ʿālimūna, Zaydun al-ʿālimu, imraʾatun ʿālimatun. Of course any one adjective shows only four of them at once, one from each set.

The second kind follows only in “the first five”, iʿrāb and definiteness: min hādhihi al-qaryati al-ẓālimi ahluhā (Q 4:75), “from this town whose people are wrongdoers”. Al-ẓālimi is in jarr and definite like al-qaryati, but masculine and singular, because what it describes is ahluhā, the people, and it agrees with them as a verb agrees with its explicit fāʿil (lesson 9).

What is the adjective for? To make an indefinite particular, rajulun ʿālimun, or a definite clear, Zaydun al-fāḍilu. Or only for praise, bismi Allāhi al-raḥmāni al-raḥīmi; for blame, aʿūdhu bi-Allāhi mina al-shayṭāni al-rajīmi; or for emphasis, nafkhatun wāḥidatun, “a single blast” (Q 69:13), where wāḥida adds nothing that nafkha did not say.

An indefinite may be described by a declarative sentence: marartu bi-rajulin abūhu ʿālimun, or qāma abūhu. And “the pronoun is not described, nor is anything described by it”: a pronoun is already as definite as a word can be, and it names no quality.

terms.en: the follower: a second word with the iʿrāb of the first, from one aspect
the adjective: a meaning in what it follows, or in something connected with it
the noun described by the adjective
the adjective of a connected thing, following in iʿrāb and definiteness only

examples.en: the adjective following its noun in number
the adjective of a connected thing (Q 4:75)
an adjective for blame

tasks.prompt: Which kind of adjective, and in what does it agree? jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun; jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun abūhu.
tasks.arabic: جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ — جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ أَبُوهُ
tasks.answer: In the first ʿālimun describes the man himself and agrees in iʿrāb, definiteness, number and gender. In the second it describes his father, a connected thing; it agrees with rajulun only in iʿrāb (rafʿ) and indefiniteness, and raises abūhu as its fāʿil.

tasks.prompt: Why is al-ẓālimi masculine singular in min hādhihi al-qaryati al-ẓālimi ahluhā?
tasks.answer: It describes the people (ahluhā), not the town: it is the adjective of a connected thing. It follows al-qaryati in jarr and definiteness, but in number and gender it behaves like a verb before an explicit fāʿil: singular, and masculine with ahl.

tasks.prompt: Say what each adjective is for: rajulun ʿālimun; Zaydun al-fāḍilu; al-raḥmāni al-raḥīmi; nafkhatun wāḥidatun.
tasks.answer: Rajulun ʿālimun: to make an indefinite particular. Zaydun al-fāḍilu: to make a definite clear. Al-raḥmāni al-raḥīmi: praise alone. Nafkhatun wāḥidatun: emphasis.

tasks.prompt: Why is a khabar not a follower, though it has the iʿrāb of its mubtadaʾ?
tasks.answer: A follower takes the iʿrāb of the word before it from one aspect, the same role. The khabar is in rafʿ from another aspect: it is what is said, not a second word for what is spoken of.

quiz.prompt: How many followers does the book count?
quiz.explanation: Naʿt, ʿaṭf by particles, emphasis, badal, explanatory ʿaṭf.

quiz.prompt: A follower takes its iʿrāb…
options: from a governor of its own
from the word before it, from one aspect

quiz.prompt: The adjective of the noun's own meaning follows it in…
The adjective of a connected thing follows only in…

Al-shayṭāni al-rajīmi has an adjective for…
Which is true of the pronoun?
options: it is neither described nor describes
it takes a sentence as adjective
quiz.explanation: It is fully definite and names no quality.

text.original: اعْلَمْ أَنَّ الَّتِي مَرَّتْ مِنَ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْمُعْرَبَةِ كَانَ إِعْرَابُهَا بِالْأَصَالَةِ، بِأَنْ دَخَلَتْهَا الْعَوَامِلُ مِنَ الْمَرْفُوعَاتِ وَالْمَنْصُوبَاتِ وَالْمَجْرُورَاتِ، وَقَدْ يَكُونُ إِعْرَابُ الِاسْمِ بِتَبَعِيَّةِ مَا قَبْلَهُ، وَيُسَمَّى التَّابِعَ؛ لِأَنَّهُ يَتْبَعُ مَا قَبْلَهُ فِي الْإِعْرَابِ. وَهُوَ كُلُّ ثَانٍ مُعْرَبٍ بِإِعْرَابِ سَابِقِهِ مِنْ جِهَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ. وَالتَّوَابِعُ خَمْسَةُ أَقْسَامٍ: النَّعْتُ، وَالْعَطْفُ بِالْحُرُوفِ، وَالتَّأْكِيدُ، وَالْبَدَلُ، وَعَطْفُ الْبَيَانِ.
text.en: Know that the inflected nouns that have passed had their iʿrāb in themselves (bi-l-aṣāla), in that the governors of the marfūʿ, manṣūb and majrūr nouns came into them. The iʿrāb of a noun may also be by following (tabaʿiyya) what is before it; it is then called a follower (tābiʿ), because it follows what is before it in iʿrāb. It is every second [word] inflected with the iʿrāb of the one before it, from one aspect. The followers are of five kinds: the naʿt (adjective), conjunction by particles, emphasis (taʾkīd), the substitute (badal) and the explicative apposition (ʿaṭf al-bayān).

text.original: فَصْلٌ: النَّعْتُ تَابِعٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى مَعْنًى فِي مَتْبُوعِهِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ، أَوْ فِي مُتَعَلِّقِ مَتْبُوعِهِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ أَبُوهُ، وَيُسَمَّى صِفَةً أَيْضًا. وَالْقِسْمُ الْأَوَّلُ يَتْبَعُ مَتْبُوعَهُ فِي عَشَرَةِ أَشْيَاءَ: فِي الْإِعْرَابِ، وَالتَّعْرِيفِ، وَالتَّنْكِيرِ، وَالْإِفْرَادِ، وَالتَّثْنِيَةِ، وَالْجَمْعِ، وَالتَّذْكِيرِ، وَالتَّأْنِيثِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ، وَرَجُلَانِ عَالِمَانِ، وَرِجَالٌ عَالِمُونَ، وَزَيْدٌ الْعَالِمُ، وَامْرَأَةٌ عَالِمَةٌ.
text.en: Section. The naʿt is a follower that indicates a meaning in the word it follows, as jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun “a learned man came to me”, or in something connected with the word it follows, as jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun abūhu “a man whose father is learned came to me”; it is also called ṣifa. The first kind follows the word it follows in ten things: in iʿrāb, definiteness, indefiniteness, the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine, as jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun “a learned man came to me”, wa-rajulāni ʿālimāni “and two learned men”, wa-rijālun ʿālimūna “and learned men”, wa-Zaydun al-ʿālimu “and Zayd the learned” and wa-imraʾatun ʿālimatun “and a learned woman”.

text.original: وَالْقِسْمُ الثَّانِي إِنَّمَا يَتْبَعُ مَتْبُوعَهُ فِي الْخَمْسَةِ الْأُوَلِ فَقَطْ، أَعْنِي الْإِعْرَابَ وَالتَّعْرِيفَ وَالتَّنْكِيرَ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ الظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا. وَفَائِدَةُ النَّعْتِ تَخْصِيصُ الْمَنْعُوتِ إِنْ كَانَا نَكِرَتَيْنِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي رَجُلٌ عَالِمٌ، وَتَوْضِيحُهُ إِنْ كَانَا مَعْرِفَتَيْنِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ الْفَاضِلُ.
text.en: The second kind follows the word it follows in the first five only, I mean iʿrāb, definiteness and indefiniteness, as in His saying, exalted is He: min hādhihi al-qaryati al-ẓālimi ahluhā “from this town whose people are wrongdoers”. The benefit of the naʿt is to make the described word (manʿūt) particular if both are indefinite, as jāʾanī rajulun ʿālimun, and to make it clear if both are definite, as jāʾanī Zaydun al-fāḍilu “Zayd the excellent came to me”.

text.original: وَقَدْ يَكُونُ لِمُجَرَّدِ الثَّنَاءِ وَالْمَدْحِ، نَحْوُ: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ، وَقَدْ يَكُونُ لِلذَّمِّ، نَحْوُ: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ، وَقَدْ يَكُونُ لِلتَّأْكِيدِ، نَحْوُ: نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ. وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ النَّكِرَةَ تُوصَفُ بِالْجُمْلَةِ الْخَبَرِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ أَبُوهُ عَالِمٌ، أَوْ قَامَ أَبُوهُ. وَالْمُضْمَرُ لَا يُوصَفُ وَلَا يُوصَفُ بِهِ.
text.en: It may be for mere praise and commendation, as bismi Allāhi al-raḥmāni al-raḥīmi “in the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate”; it may be for blame, as aʿūdhu bi-Allāhi mina al-shayṭāni al-rajīmi “I take refuge in God from Satan, the accursed”; and it may be for emphasis, as nafkhatun wāḥidatun “a single blast”. Know that the indefinite is described by a declarative sentence, as marartu bi-rajulin abūhu ʿālimun “I passed by a man whose father is learned” or qāma abūhu “whose father stood”. The pronoun is not described, nor is anything described by it.

lessons.title: ʿAṭf by particles
body: ʿAṭf by particles, also called ʿaṭf al-nasaq, is “a follower to which is attributed what is attributed to the word it follows, both of them being intended by that attribution”: qāma Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun, where both stood. The last words set it apart from the badal (lesson 29), where only the second is intended. Its condition is a particle of ʿaṭf between the two; the particles come in the third part.

Two pronouns need care. A noun joined to a marfūʿ joined pronoun needs the separate pronoun first: ḍarabtu anā wa-Zaydun, not ḍarabtu wa-Zaydun, unless something comes between: ḍarabtu al-yawma wa-Zaydun. A noun joined to a majrūr pronoun needs the particle of jarr again: marartu bika wa-bi-Zaydin. The commentators give the reason for both: a joined pronoun is like a part of the word it is joined to, and a noun cannot be joined to part of a word.

“The conjoined word has the rule of the word it is conjoined to”: if the first is an adjective, a khabar, a ṣila or a ḥāl, so is the second, and it must meet the same conditions. The book gives a test: “where the maʿṭūf may be put in the place of the maʿṭūf ʿalayhi, conjunction is allowed, and where not, not.” So after Zaydun qāma abūhu one cannot join wa-qaʿada ʿAmrun as a second khabar: qaʿada ʿAmrun could not stand alone as the khabar of Zayd, having no pronoun of him.

Can one particle join two words to the governed words of two different governors? Only, says the book, when the first of them is majrūr and put first, and so is the second: fī al-dāri Zaydun wa-l-ḥujrati ʿAmrun, where al-ḥujrati is joined to what fī governs and ʿAmrun to what the ibtidāʾ governs. Outside this question there are two other schools: al-Farrāʾ allows it everywhere, and Sībawayh nowhere.

terms.en: ʿaṭf by particles: both words intended by the attribution
the joined word and the word it is joined to
repeating the particle of jarr after a majrūr pronoun
joining to the governed words of two governors

examples.en: both intended by the attribution
the separate pronoun before the joined noun
a separation: the separate pronoun not needed
the particle of jarr repeated
two governors, the majrūr put first

tasks.prompt: Correct each and give the rule: ḍarabtu wa-Zaydun; marartu bika wa-Zaydin.
tasks.answer: Ḍarabtu anā wa-Zaydun: a noun joined to a marfūʿ joined pronoun needs the separate pronoun first (or a separation, ḍarabtu al-yawma wa-Zaydun). Marartu bika wa-bi-Zaydin: with a majrūr pronoun the particle of jarr is repeated.

tasks.prompt: How does ʿaṭf by particles differ from the badal?
tasks.answer: In ʿaṭf both words are intended by the attribution: in qāma Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun both stood. In the badal only the second is intended, and the first only leads up to it.

tasks.prompt: Apply the book's test: may wa-qaʿada ʿAmrun be joined as a second khabar after Zaydun qāma abūhu?
tasks.answer: No. The joined word must be able to stand in the place of the first. Qaʿada ʿAmrun has no pronoun referring to Zayd, so it could not be the khabar of Zayd by itself; it cannot be joined as one either.

tasks.prompt: Give the three views on joining to the governed words of two different governors.
tasks.answer: The book: allowed only when the first governed word is majrūr and put first, and the second likewise (fī al-dāri Zaydun wa-l-ḥujrati ʿAmrun). Al-Farrāʾ: allowed everywhere. Sībawayh: allowed nowhere.

quiz.prompt: In ʿaṭf by particles…
options: both words are intended by the attribution

quiz.prompt: ʿAṭf by particles is also called…
To join Zaydun to the tāʾ of ḍarabtu one says…
In marartu bika wa-bi-Zaydin, the bāʾ is repeated because…
options: the first is a majrūr pronoun
quiz.explanation: The particle of jarr must be repeated.

quiz.prompt: The joined word, if the first is a ṣila, is…
quiz.explanation: It has the rule of what it is joined to.

quiz.prompt: Who allows joining to the governed words of two governors everywhere?
In fī al-dāri Zaydun wa-l-ḥujrati ʿAmrun, al-ḥujrati is joined to…

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْعَطْفُ بِالْحُرُوفِ تَابِعٌ يُنْسَبُ إِلَيْهِ مَا نُسِبَ إِلَى مَتْبُوعِهِ، وَكِلَاهُمَا مَقْصُودَانِ بِتِلْكَ النِّسْبَةِ، وَيُسَمَّى عَطْفَ النَّسَقِ. وَشَرْطُهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ مَتْبُوعِهِ أَحَدُ حُرُوفِ الْعَطْفِ، وَسَيَأْتِي ذِكْرُهَا فِي الْقِسْمِ الثَّالِثِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى، نَحْوُ: قَامَ زَيْدٌ وَعَمْرٌو.
text.en: Section. Conjunction by particles is a follower to which is attributed what is attributed to the word it follows, both of them being intended by that attribution; it is called ʿaṭf al-nasaq. Its condition is that between it and the word it follows there is one of the particles of conjunction, whose mention will come in the third part, if God Most High wills, as qāma Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun “Zayd and ʿAmr stood”.

text.original: وَإِذَا عُطِفَ عَلَى الضَّمِيرِ الْمَرْفُوعِ الْمُتَّصِلِ يَجِبُ تَأْكِيدُهُ بِالضَّمِيرِ الْمُنْفَصِلِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُ أَنَا وَزَيْدٌ، إِلَّا إِذَا فُصِلَ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُ الْيَوْمَ وَزَيْدٌ. وَإِذَا عُطِفَ عَلَى الضَّمِيرِ الْمَجْرُورِ يَجِبُ إِعَادَةُ حَرْفِ الْجَرِّ، نَحْوُ: مَرَرْتُ بِكَ وَبِزَيْدٍ.
text.en: When [a noun] is conjoined to an attached marfūʿ pronoun, [the pronoun] must be emphasised by the separate pronoun, as ḍarabtu anā wa-Zaydun “I hit, I and Zayd”, unless there is a separation, as ḍarabtu al-yawma wa-Zaydun “I hit today, and Zayd”. When [a noun] is conjoined to a majrūr pronoun, the particle of jarr must be repeated, as marartu bi-ka wa-bi-Zaydin “I passed by you and by Zayd”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْمَعْطُوفَ فِي حُكْمِ الْمَعْطُوفِ عَلَيْهِ، أَعْنِي إِذَا كَانَ الْأَوَّلُ صِفَةً لِشَيْءٍ أَوْ خَبَرًا أَوْ صِلَةً أَوْ حَالًا فَالثَّانِي كَذَلِكَ أَيْضًا. وَالضَّابِطَةُ فِيهِ أَنَّهُ حَيْثُ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُقَامَ الْمَعْطُوفُ مَقَامَ الْمَعْطُوفِ عَلَيْهِ جَازَ الْعَطْفُ، وَحَيْثُ لَا فَلَا.
text.en: Know that the conjoined word (maʿṭūf) has the rule of the word it is conjoined to (maʿṭūf ʿalayhi); I mean, if the first is an adjective of something, or a khabar, or a ṣila, or a ḥāl, the second is so too. The rule of thumb in it is that where the maʿṭūf may be put in the place of the maʿṭūf ʿalayhi, conjunction is allowed, and where not, not.

text.original: وَالْعَطْفُ عَلَى مَعْمُولَيْ عَامِلَيْنِ مُخْتَلِفَيْنِ جَائِزٌ إِنْ كَانَ الْمَعْطُوفُ عَلَيْهِ مَجْرُورًا مُقَدَّمًا وَالْمَعْطُوفُ كَذَلِكَ، نَحْوُ: فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدٌ وَالْحُجْرَةِ عَمْرٌو، وَفِي غَيْرِ هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ مَذْهَبَانِ آخَرَانِ: أَحَدُهُمَا أَنْ يَجُوزَ مُطْلَقًا عِنْدَ الْفَرَّاءِ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ مُطْلَقًا عِنْدَ سِيبَوَيْهِ.
text.en: Conjunction on the governed words of two different governors is allowed if the maʿṭūf ʿalayhi is majrūr and put first, and the maʿṭūf likewise, as fī al-dāri Zaydun wa-al-ḥujrati ʿAmrun “in the house is Zayd, and in the room ʿAmr”. Outside this question there are two other schools: one, that it is allowed absolutely, according to al-Farrāʾ; and [the other, that] it is not allowed absolutely, according to Sībawayh.

lessons.title: Emphasis
body: Emphasis is “a follower that indicates the confirming of the word followed in what is attributed to it, or that the judgement covers every individual of it”. Two uses, then: to remove the doubt that someone else was meant (jāʾanī Zaydun nafsuhu, Zayd himself, not his messenger), and to remove the doubt that some were left out (jāʾanī al-qawmu kulluhum).

Verbal emphasis repeats the first word: jāʾanī Zaydun Zaydun; jāʾa jāʾa Zaydun. Emphasis of meaning uses set words. Nafs and ʿayn serve the singular, dual and plural, changing their form and their pronoun: Zaydun nafsuhu; al-Zaydāni anfusuhumā or nafsāhumā; al-Zaydūna anfusuhum; likewise ʿaynuhu, aʿyunuhumā or ʿaynāhumā, aʿyunuhum; and Hindun nafsuhā, al-Hindāni anfusuhumā, al-Hindātu anfusuhunna. Kilā and kiltā are for the dual only: al-rajulāni kilāhumā, al-marʾatāni kiltāhumā.

Kull, ajmaʿ, aktaʿ, abtaʿ and abṣaʿ are for what is not dual, kull changing its pronoun and the rest their form: jāʾanī al-qawmu kulluhum ajmaʿūna aktaʿūna abtaʿūna abṣaʿūna; qāmati al-nisāʾu kulluhunna jumaʿu kutaʿu butaʿu buṣaʿu. Jumaʿ was among the diptotes of lesson 7.

A marfūʿ joined pronoun emphasized by nafs or ʿayn first takes the separate pronoun: ḍarabta anta nafsuka. And kull and ajmaʿ emphasize only what has parts that can be separated, “by the senses, as al-qawm, or by judgement”: ishtaraytu al-ʿabda kullahu, “I bought the slave, all of him”, since a slave can be bought in shares; but not akramtu al-ʿabda kullahu, since honouring a man is not done in parts.
Aktaʿ, abtaʿ and abṣaʿ “are followers of ajmaʿ and have no meaning here without it”: they never come before ajmaʿ, nor without it. They add to the sound of the emphasis, not to its sense.

terms.en: verbal emphasis: the word repeated
emphasis of meaning, with set words
“self”: for one, two or many
“all”: only for what has separable parts

nafs for the dual, in two forms

tasks.prompt: Emphasize each with nafs as the book does: jāʾanī Zaydun; jāʾanī al-Zaydāni; jāʾatnī al-Hindātu.
tasks.answer: Jāʾanī Zaydun nafsuhu; jāʾanī al-Zaydāni anfusuhumā (or nafsāhumā); jāʾatnī al-Hindātu anfusuhunna.

tasks.prompt: Why may one say ishtaraytu al-ʿabda kullahu but not akramtu al-ʿabda kullahu?
tasks.answer: Kull emphasizes only what has parts that can be separated, by the senses or by judgement. A slave can be bought in shares, so the buying has parts; honouring a man is not done in parts, so kull has nothing to cover.

tasks.prompt: Correct the mistake: jāʾanī al-qawmu aktaʿūna ajmaʿūna.
tasks.answer: Jāʾanī al-qawmu ajmaʿūna aktaʿūna. Aktaʿ, abtaʿ and abṣaʿ follow ajmaʿ and have no meaning without it; they never come before it.

tasks.prompt: Emphasize the tāʾ of ḍarabta with nafs.
tasks.answer: Ḍarabta anta nafsuka: a marfūʿ joined pronoun emphasized by nafs or ʿayn must first be emphasized by the separate pronoun.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: التَّأْكِيدُ تَابِعٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَقْرِيرِ الْمَتْبُوعِ فِيمَا نُسِبَ إِلَيْهِ، أَوْ عَلَى شُمُولِ الْحُكْمِ لِكُلِّ فَرْدٍ مِنْ أَفْرَادِ الْمَتْبُوعِ. وَالتَّأْكِيدُ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: لَفْظِيٌّ، وَهُوَ تَكْرِيرُ اللَّفْظِ الْأَوَّلِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ زَيْدٌ، وَجَاءَ جَاءَ زَيْدٌ؛ وَمَعْنَوِيٌّ، وَهُوَ بِأَلْفَاظٍ مَعْدُودَةٍ، وَهِيَ النَّفْسُ وَالْعَيْنُ لِلْوَاحِدِ وَالْمُثَنَّى وَالْمَجْمُوعِ بِاخْتِلَافِ الصِّيغَةِ وَالضَّمِيرِ.
text.en: Section. Emphasis (taʾkīd) is a follower that indicates the confirming of the word followed in what is attributed to it, or that the judgement covers every individual of the word followed. Emphasis is of two kinds. Verbal (lafẓī), which is the repeating of the first word, as jāʾanī Zaydun Zaydun “Zayd came to me, Zayd” and jāʾa jāʾa Zaydun “Zayd came, came”; and by meaning (maʿnawī), which is with a set number of words. They are nafs and ʿayn (self), for the singular, the dual and the plural, with a difference of the form and of the pronoun,

text.original: نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ نَفْسُهُ، وَالزَّيْدَانِ أَنْفُسُهُمَا أَوْ نَفْسَاهُمَا، وَالزَّيْدُونَ أَنْفُسُهُمْ، وَكَذَلِكَ عَيْنُهُ وَأَعْيُنُهُمَا أَوْ عَيْنَاهُمَا وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ، وَجَاءَتْنِي هِنْدٌ نَفْسُهَا، وَجَاءَتْنِي الْهِنْدَانِ أَنْفُسُهُمَا أَوْ نَفْسَاهُمَا، وَجَاءَتْنِي الْهِنْدَاتُ أَنْفُسُهُنَّ. وَكِلَا وَكِلْتَا لِلْمُثَنَّى خَاصَّةً، نَحْوُ: قَامَ الرَّجُلَانِ كِلَاهُمَا، وَقَامَتِ الْمَرْأَتَانِ كِلْتَاهُمَا.
text.en: as jāʾanī Zaydun nafsuhu “Zayd himself came to me”, wa-al-Zaydāni anfusuhumā or nafsāhumā “and the two Zayds themselves”, and wa-al-Zaydūna anfusuhum “and the Zayds themselves”; and likewise ʿaynuhu, aʿyunuhumā or ʿaynāhumā, and aʿyunuhum; and jāʾatnī Hindun nafsuhā “Hind herself came to me”, jāʾatnī al-Hindāni anfusuhumā or nafsāhumā “the two Hinds themselves came to me”, and jāʾatnī al-Hindātu anfusuhunna “the Hinds themselves came to me”. Kilā and kiltā are for the dual only, as qāma al-rajulāni kilāhumā “the two men stood, both of them” and qāmati al-marʾatāni kiltāhumā “the two women stood, both of them”.

text.original: وَكُلٌّ وَأَجْمَعُ وَأَكْتَعُ وَأَبْتَعُ وَأَبْصَعُ لِغَيْرِ الْمُثَنَّى بِاخْتِلَافِ الضَّمِيرِ فِي كُلٍّ، وَالصِّيغَةِ فِي الْبَوَاقِي، تَقُولُ: جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ أَكْتَعُونَ أَبْتَعُونَ أَبْصَعُونَ، وَقَامَتِ النِّسَاءُ كُلُّهُنَّ جُمَعُ كُتَعُ بُتَعُ بُصَعُ.
text.en: Kull, ajmaʿ, aktaʿ, abtaʿ and abṣaʿ are for what is not dual, with a difference of the pronoun in kull and of the form in the others; you say jāʾanī al-qawmu kulluhum ajmaʿūna aktaʿūna abtaʿūna abṣaʿūna “the people came to me, all of them, every one” and qāmati al-nisāʾu kulluhunna jumaʿu kutaʿu butaʿu buṣaʿu “the women stood, all of them, every one”.

text.original: وَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ تَأْكِيدَ الضَّمِيرِ الْمَرْفُوعِ الْمُتَّصِلِ بِالنَّفْسِ وَالْعَيْنِ يَجِبُ تَأْكِيدُهُ بِالضَّمِيرِ الْمُنْفَصِلِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتَ أَنْتَ نَفْسُكَ. وَلَا يُؤَكَّدُ بِكُلٍّ وَأَجْمَعَ إِلَّا مَا لَهُ أَجْزَاءٌ وَأَبْعَاضٌ يَصِحُّ افْتِرَاقُهَا حِسًّا، كَالْقَوْمِ، أَوْ حُكْمًا، كَمَا تَقُولُ: اشْتَرَيْتُ الْعَبْدَ كُلَّهُ، وَلَا تَقُولُ: أَكْرَمْتُ الْعَبْدَ كُلَّهُ.
text.en: When you want to emphasise an attached marfūʿ pronoun with nafs and ʿayn, it must [first] be emphasised with the separate pronoun, as ḍarabta anta nafsuka “you hit, you yourself”. Only that which has parts and portions that can be separated, by the senses, as al-qawmi “the people”, or by judgement, is emphasised with kull and ajmaʿ, as you say ishtaraytu al-ʿabda kullahu “I bought the slave, all of him”; and you do not say akramtu al-ʿabda kullahu “I honoured the slave, all of him”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ أَكْتَعَ وَأَبْتَعَ وَأَبْصَعَ أَتْبَاعٌ لِأَجْمَعَ، وَلَيْسَ لَهَا مَعْنًى هَهُنَا بِدُونِهِ، فَلَا يَجُوزُ تَقْدِيمُهَا عَلَى أَجْمَعَ، وَلَا ذِكْرُهَا بِدُونِهِ.
text.en: Know that aktaʿ, abtaʿ and abṣaʿ are followers of ajmaʿ and have no meaning here without it; so they may not be put before ajmaʿ, nor mentioned without it.

lessons.title: The badal; the explanatory ʿaṭf
body: The badal is “a follower to which is attributed what is attributed to the word it follows, and it is what is intended by the attribution, not the word it follows”. It has four kinds. The badal of the whole for the whole, whose meaning is that of the word followed: jāʾanī Zaydun akhūka. The badal of the part: ḍarabtu Zaydan raʾsahu. The badal of inclusion, whose meaning is something connected with the word followed: suliba Zaydun thawbuhu, “Zayd was robbed, his garment”. And the badal of mistake, said after a slip of the tongue: jāʾanī Zaydun Jaʿfarun; raʾaytu rajulan ḥimāran.

An indefinite badal of a definite must be qualified: bi-l-nāṣiyati nāṣiyatin kādhibatin (Q 96:15–16); a bare nāṣiyatin would only say less than al-nāṣiya. The reverse, a definite badal of an indefinite, needs nothing, as in ilā ṣirāṭin mustaqīmin, ṣirāṭi Allāhi (Q 42:52–53); nor when both are alike.

The explanatory ʿaṭf (ʿaṭf al-bayān) is “a follower, not an adjective, that makes the word it follows clear; it is the better known of two names of a thing”: qāma Abū Ḥafṣin ʿUmaru, the kunya made plain by the name; qāma ʿAbdu Allāhi bnu ʿUmara, the name made plain by the better-known “son of ʿUmar”. Unlike the adjective it shows no quality; unlike the badal, the first word is still what is meant.

In wording it can look exactly like a badal, and the book cites the line: anā ibnu al-tāriki al-Bakriyyi Bishrin, ʿalayhi al-ṭayru tarqubuhu wuqūʿā, “I am the son of the one who left the Bakrī, Bishr, with the birds over him, waiting to alight”. The commentators show why Bishrin must be an explanatory ʿaṭf: a badal stands as if in the place of what it follows, and al-tāriki Bishrin, a participle with the lām made muḍāf to a name without it, is not allowed. So two followers that look the same may be told apart by a rule learned elsewhere.

terms.en: the follower that is what the attribution intends
the badal of inclusion: something connected with the first
the badal of mistake, after a slip
the explanatory ʿaṭf: the better known of two names

tasks.prompt: Name the kind of badal: jāʾanī Zaydun akhūka; ḍarabtu Zaydan raʾsahu; suliba Zaydun thawbuhu; raʾaytu rajulan ḥimāran.
tasks.arabic: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ أَخُوكَ — ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا رَأْسَهُ — سُلِبَ زَيْدٌ ثَوْبُهُ — رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا حِمَارًا
tasks.answer: Akhūka: of the whole (Zayd and your brother are one). Raʾsahu: of the part. Thawbuhu: of inclusion (the garment is connected with Zayd). Ḥimāran: of mistake (the speaker meant to say “a donkey”).

tasks.prompt: Why must nāṣiyatin be qualified in Q 96:15–16, while ṣirāṭi Allāhi in Q 42:53 needs no adjective?
tasks.answer: Nāṣiyatin is an indefinite badal of the definite al-nāṣiya: bare, it would say less than the word it replaces, so it must be qualified (kādhibatin). Ṣirāṭi Allāhi is a definite badal of an indefinite (ṣirāṭin): it already says more, so it needs nothing.

tasks.prompt: How does the explanatory ʿaṭf differ from the adjective and from the badal?
tasks.answer: Unlike the adjective it shows no quality of the first word; it only makes plain who or what is meant, by a better-known name. Unlike the badal, the first word is still what the speaker means; in the badal the second word is the one intended.

tasks.prompt: Why is Bishrin an explanatory ʿaṭf, not a badal, in the poet's line?
tasks.answer: A badal stands as if in the place of the word it follows. Put in the place of al-Bakriyyi, Bishrin would give al-tāriki Bishrin, a participle with the lām made muḍāf to a name without the lām, which is not allowed. So it can only be an explanatory ʿaṭf.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْبَدَلُ تَابِعٌ يُنْسَبُ إِلَيْهِ مَا نُسِبَ إِلَى مَتْبُوعِهِ، وَهُوَ الْمَقْصُودُ بِالنِّسْبَةِ دُونَ مَتْبُوعِهِ. وَأَقْسَامُ الْبَدَلِ أَرْبَعَةٌ: بَدَلُ الْكُلِّ مِنَ الْكُلِّ، وَهُوَ مَا مَدْلُولُهُ مَدْلُولُ الْمَتْبُوعِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ أَخُوكَ، وَبَدَلُ الْبَعْضِ مِنَ الْكُلِّ، وَهُوَ مَا مَدْلُولُهُ جُزْءُ مَدْلُولِ الْمَتْبُوعِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا رَأْسَهُ.
text.en: Section. The substitute (badal) is a follower to which is attributed what is attributed to the word it follows, and it is what is intended by the attribution, not the word it follows. The kinds of badal are four. The substitute of the whole for the whole, which is one whose meaning is the meaning of the word followed, as jāʾanī Zaydun akhūka “Zayd, your brother, came to me”; the substitute of the part for the whole, which is one whose meaning is a part of the meaning of the word followed, as ḍarabtu Zaydan raʾsahu “I hit Zayd, his head”;

text.original: وَبَدَلُ الِاشْتِمَالِ، وَهُوَ مَا مَدْلُولُهُ مُتَعَلِّقُ الْمَتْبُوعِ، كَسُلِبَ زَيْدٌ ثَوْبُهُ، وَبَدَلُ الْغَلَطِ، وَهُوَ مَا يُذْكَرُ بَعْدَ الْغَلَطِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ جَعْفَرٌ، وَرَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا حِمَارًا. وَالْبَدَلُ إِنْ كَانَ نَكِرَةً مِنْ مَعْرِفَةٍ يَجِبُ نَعْتُهُ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: بِالنَّاصِيَةِ نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ، وَلَا يَجِبُ فِي عَكْسِهِ، وَلَا فِي الْمُتَّحِدَيْنِ.
text.en: the substitute of inclusion (ishtimāl), which is one whose meaning is something connected with the word followed, as suliba Zaydun thawbuhu “Zayd was robbed, his garment”; and the substitute of mistake (ghalaṭ), which is what is mentioned after a mistake, as jāʾanī Zaydun Jaʿfarun “Zayd — Jaʿfar came to me” and raʾaytu rajulan ḥimāran “I saw a man — a donkey”. If the badal is an indefinite [substituted] for a definite, it must be qualified, as in His saying, exalted is He: bi-al-nāṣiyati nāṣiyatin kādhibatin “by the forelock, a lying forelock”; this is not necessary in the reverse, nor when the two are alike.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: عَطْفُ الْبَيَانِ تَابِعٌ غَيْرُ صِفَةٍ يُوَضِّحُ مَتْبُوعَهُ، وَهُوَ أَشْهَرُ اسْمَيْ شَيْءٍ، نَحْوُ: قَامَ أَبُو حَفْصٍ عُمَرُ، وَقَامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ. وَقَدْ يَلْتَبِسُ بِالْبَدَلِ لَفْظًا فِي مِثْلِ قَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ، شِعْرٌ: أَنَا ابْنُ التَّارِكِ الْبَكْرِيِّ بِشْرٍ * عَلَيْهِ الطَّيْرُ تَرْقُبُهُ وُقُوعَا.
text.en: Section. The explicative apposition (ʿaṭf al-bayān) is a follower, not an adjective, that makes the word it follows clear; it is the better known of two names of a thing, as qāma Abū Ḥafṣin ʿUmaru “Abū Ḥafṣ ʿUmar stood” and qāma ʿAbdu Allāhi bnu ʿUmara “ʿAbd Allāh son of ʿUmar stood”. It may be confused with the badal in the wording, in such [a line] as the poet's saying, verse: anā ibnu al-tāriki al-Bakriyyi Bishrin / ʿalayhi al-ṭayru tarqubuhu wuqūʿā “I am the son of the one who left the Bakrī, Bishr, / with the birds over him, watching him, alighting”.

lessons.title: The built noun; its eight kinds; the pronouns
body: The second chapter of the noun is the built noun (mabnī). It is either a noun “that stands not put together with another”, as the letters named one by one, alif bā tā thā, or numbers counted, wāḥid ithnān thalāthah, or Zayd said alone; or a noun that resembles what is built in origin (lesson 4). The first kind “is mabnī in fact, on the sukūn, and muʿrab in potential”: put Zayd into a sentence and he takes his iʿrāb. The second “never becomes muʿrab”.

A noun resembles the built words in one of three ways: it needs an indication to point to its meaning, as the demonstrative hāʾulāʾi needs the pointing hand; it has fewer than three letters; or it contains the meaning of a particle, as dhā and man, and the numbers aḥada ʿashara to tisʿata ʿashara, which contain the wāw, “one and ten”.

“Its rule is that its end does not differ with the difference of the governors.” Its vowels have their own names, ḍamm, fatḥ and kasr, and its sukūn is called waqf; the names rafʿ, naṣb, jarr and jazm are kept for iʿrāb. So one says that hāʾulāʾi is built on kasr, never that it is in jarr. The built nouns are of eight kinds: the pronouns, the demonstratives, the relatives, the nouns of verbs, the sounds, the compounds, the allusive nouns (kināyāt) and some adverbs.

The pronoun (muḍmar) is “laid down to indicate a speaker, one addressed, or an absent one previously mentioned in wording, in meaning or by implication”. The commentators illustrate the three: in wording, Zaydun ḍarabtuhu; in meaning, iʿdilū huwa aqrabu li-l-taqwā (Q 5:8), where huwa is the justice understood from iʿdilū; by implication, the pronoun of the matter (next lesson), whose sentence comes after it.

Pronouns are attached (muttaṣil), never used alone, or separate (munfaṣil), used alone. The attached are marfūʿ, ḍarabtu … ḍarabna; manṣūb, ḍarabanī … ḍarabahunna, innanī … innahunna; or majrūr, ghulāmī, lī … ghulāmihinna, lahunna. The separate are marfūʿ, anā … hunna, or manṣūb, iyyāya … iyyāhunna. Five sets of twelve: “that makes sixty pronouns”.

tasks.prompt: Why is Zayd counted out alone called built “in fact” and inflected “in potential”?
tasks.answer: Alone, not put together with another word, it has no governor and so no iʿrāb: it is spoken with a sukūn, built. But it does not resemble the built words, so as soon as it is put into a sentence it takes iʿrāb.

tasks.prompt: Name the three ways a noun may resemble what is built in origin, with the book's examples.
tasks.answer: By needing an indication to show its meaning, as the demonstrative hāʾulāʾi; by having fewer than three letters; or by containing the meaning of a particle, as dhā, man and aḥada ʿashara to tisʿata ʿashara.

tasks.prompt: How would you describe the end of hāʾulāʾi, and why not with the word jarr?
tasks.answer: It is built on kasr. Jarr is the name of a state of iʿrāb, brought by a governor; the kasra of hāʾulāʾi never changes with governors, so it takes the names of binā: ḍamm, fatḥ, kasr, waqf.

tasks.prompt: Give the five sets of pronouns and say how the book reaches sixty.
tasks.answer: Marfūʿ attached (ḍarabtu … ḍarabna), manṣūb attached (ḍarabanī … ḍarabahunna), majrūr attached (ghulāmī … ghulāmihinna), marfūʿ separate (anā … hunna), manṣūb separate (iyyāya … iyyāhunna). Each set has twelve: five times twelve is sixty.

text.original: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ وَقَعَ غَيْرَ مُرَكَّبٍ مَعَ غَيْرِهِ، مِثْلُ: أَلِفْ بَا تَا ثَا، وَمِثْلُ: وَاحِدْ اثْنَانْ ثَلَاثَهْ، وَكَلَفْظَةِ زَيْدٍ وَحْدَهُ؛ فَإِنَّهُ مَبْنِيٌّ بِالْفِعْلِ عَلَى السُّكُونِ، وَمُعْرَبٌ بِالْقُوَّةِ. أَوْ شَابَهَ مَبْنِيَّ الْأَصْلِ، بِأَنْ يَكُونَ فِي الدَّلَالَةِ عَلَى مَعْنَاهُ مُحْتَاجًا إِلَى قَرِينَةٍ، كَالْإِشَارَةِ، نَحْوُ: هَؤُلَاءِ، أَوْ يَكُونَ عَلَى أَقَلَّ مِنْ ثَلَاثَةِ أَحْرُفٍ، أَوْ تَضَمَّنَ مَعْنَى الْحَرْفِ، نَحْوُ: ذَا وَمَنْ، وَأَحَدَ عَشَرَ إِلَى تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ، وَهَذَا الْقِسْمُ لَا يَصِيرُ مُعْرَبًا أَصْلًا.
text.en: It is a noun that stands not put together with another, as alif bā tā thā “alif, bā, tā, thā” and wāḥid ithnān thalāthah “one, two, three”, and as the word Zaydin alone; for it is mabnī in fact, on the sukūn, and muʿrab in potential. Or [it is a noun] that resembles what is mabnī in origin: by needing an indication to point to its meaning, like the demonstrative, as hāʾulāʾi “these”; or by being of fewer than three letters; or by containing the meaning of a particle, as dhā and man, and aḥada ʿashara “eleven” to tisʿata ʿashara “nineteen”. This kind never becomes muʿrab.

text.original: وَحُكْمُهُ أَنْ لَا يَخْتَلِفَ آخِرُهُ بِاخْتِلَافِ الْعَوَامِلِ، وَحَرَكَاتُهُ تُسَمَّى ضَمًّا وَفَتْحًا وَكَسْرًا، وَسُكُونُهُ وَقْفًا. وَهُوَ عَلَى ثَمَانِيَةِ أَنْوَاعٍ: الْمُضْمَرَاتُ، وَأَسْمَاءُ الْإِشَارَاتِ، وَالْمَوْصُولَاتُ، وَأَسْمَاءُ الْأَفْعَالِ، وَالْأَصْوَاتُ، وَالْمُرَكَّبَاتُ، وَالْكِنَايَاتُ، وَبَعْضُ الظُّرُوفِ.
text.en: Its rule is that its end does not differ with the difference of the governors. Its vowels are called ḍamm, fatḥ and kasr, and its sukūn waqf (pause). It is of eight kinds: the pronouns, the demonstratives, the relatives, the nouns of verbs (asmāʾ al-afʿāl), the sounds (aṣwāt), the compounds, the allusive nouns (kināyāt) and some adverbs.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمُضْمَرُ اسْمٌ وُضِعَ لِيَدُلَّ عَلَى مُتَكَلِّمٍ أَوْ مُخَاطَبٍ أَوْ غَائِبٍ تَقَدَّمَ ذِكْرُهُ لَفْظًا أَوْ مَعْنًى أَوْ حُكْمًا. وَهُوَ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: مُتَّصِلٌ، وَهُوَ مَا لَا يُسْتَعْمَلُ وَحْدَهُ، إِمَّا مَرْفُوعٌ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُ إِلَى ضَرَبْنَ، أَوْ مَنْصُوبٌ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبَنِي إِلَى ضَرَبَهُنَّ، وَإِنَّنِي إِلَى إِنَّهُنَّ، أَوْ مَجْرُورٌ، نَحْوُ: غُلَامِي وَلِي إِلَى غُلَامِهِنَّ وَلَهُنَّ؛ وَمُنْفَصِلٌ، وَهُوَ مَا يُسْتَعْمَلُ وَحْدَهُ، وَهُوَ أَيْضًا إِمَّا مَرْفُوعٌ، نَحْوُ: أَنَا إِلَى هُنَّ، أَوْ مَنْصُوبٌ، نَحْوُ: إِيَّايَ إِلَى إِيَّاهُنَّ، فَذَلِكَ سِتُّونَ ضَمِيرًا.
text.en: Section. The pronoun (muḍmar) is a noun laid down to indicate a speaker, one addressed, or an absent one previously mentioned in wording, in meaning or by implication. It is of two kinds. Attached (muttaṣil), which is one that is not used alone: either marfūʿ, as ḍarabtu to ḍarabna; or manṣūb, as ḍarabanī to ḍarabahunna, and innanī to innahunna; or majrūr, as ghulāmī and wa-lī to ghulāmihinna and wa-lahunna. And separate (munfaṣil), which is one that is used alone; it too is either marfūʿ, as anā to hunna, or manṣūb, as iyyāya to iyyāhunna. That makes sixty pronouns.

lessons.title: The hidden pronoun; the separate pronoun; the pronoun of the matter; the faṣl
body: Only the attached marfūʿ pronoun can be hidden. It is hidden in the past for the absent masculine and feminine: ḍaraba, “that is, huwa”, and ḍarabat, “that is, hiya”, the tāʾ being only the sign of the feminine. In the muḍāriʿ it is hidden for the speaker always, aḍribu (anā), naḍribu (naḥnu); for the one man addressed, taḍribu (anta); and for the absent masculine and feminine, yaḍribu (huwa), taḍribu (hiya). And it is hidden in every adjective, the participles and the rest, “in every case”.

“The separate pronoun may be used only when the attached one is impossible.” The book's examples show the four usual reasons: the object put first, iyyāka naʿbudu (Q 1:5); the pronoun after illā, mā ḍarabaka illā anā; a pronoun with no governor to lean on, as the mubtadaʾ in anā Zaydun; and mā anta illā qāʾiman.

The Arabs also have an absent pronoun put before a sentence that explains it: the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) when masculine, the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa) when feminine. Qul huwa Allāhu aḥadun (Q 112:1): huwa means “the matter is”, and the sentence Allāhu aḥadun says what the matter is. Innahā Zaynabu qāʾimatun: “the story is: Zaynab is standing”. It refers forward, not back, and that is why the definition of the pronoun had “by implication”.

Between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar there may come “the form of a separate marfūʿ pronoun agreeing with the mubtadaʾ”, when the khabar is definite or on the pattern afʿal min: Zaydun huwa al-qāʾimu; kāna Zaydun huwa afḍala min ʿAmrin; kunta anta al-raqība ʿalayhim (Q 5:117). It is called faṣl, “separation”, “because it separates the khabar from the adjective”: without it, Zaydun al-qāʾimu could be heard as “Zayd the standing one …”, still waiting for its khabar.

The examples show that the faṣl takes no part in the iʿrāb. In kāna Zaydun huwa afḍala and kunta anta al-raqība the khabar stays in naṣb after it; if huwa were a mubtadaʾ, its khabar would be in rafʿ. That is why the book says only “the form” of a pronoun.

tasks.prompt: Give the hidden pronoun in each: ḍarabat; naḍribu; taḍribu said to a man; yaḍribu.
tasks.answer: Ḍarabat: hiya (the tāʾ is the sign of the feminine). Naḍribu: naḥnu. Taḍribu to a man: anta. Yaḍribu: huwa.

tasks.prompt: Why is the separate pronoun used in iyyāka naʿbudu and in anā Zaydun?
tasks.answer: In iyyāka naʿbudu the object is put before its verb, and an attached pronoun cannot stand before the word it is attached to. In anā Zaydun the pronoun is a mubtadaʾ with no governor to attach to. In both the attached pronoun is impossible.

tasks.prompt: What does huwa refer to in qul huwa Allāhu aḥadun?
tasks.answer: It is the pronoun of the matter: it refers forward to the sentence after it, Allāhu aḥadun, which explains it: “say: the matter is, God is One”.

tasks.prompt: Why is afḍala in naṣb in kāna Zaydun huwa afḍala min ʿAmrin?
tasks.arabic: كَانَ زَيْدٌ هُوَ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ عَمْرٍو
tasks.answer: Huwa is the faṣl, which takes no part in the iʿrāb; afḍala is still the khabar of kāna, in naṣb. If huwa were a mubtadaʾ, afḍalu would be its khabar, in rafʿ.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ الْمَرْفُوعَ الْمُتَّصِلَ خَاصَّةً يَكُونُ مُسْتَتِرًا فِي الْمَاضِي لِلْغَائِبِ وَالْغَائِبَةِ، كَضَرَبَ، أَيْ هُوَ، وَضَرَبَتْ، أَيْ هِيَ، وَفِي الْمُضَارِعِ لِلْمُتَكَلِّمِ مُطْلَقًا، نَحْوُ: أَضْرِبُ، أَيْ أَنَا، وَنَضْرِبُ، أَيْ نَحْنُ، وَلِلْمُخَاطَبِ، كَتَضْرِبُ، أَيْ أَنْتَ، وَلِلْغَائِبِ وَالْغَائِبَةِ، كَيَضْرِبُ، أَيْ هُوَ، وَتَضْرِبُ، أَيْ هِيَ، وَفِي الصِّفَةِ، أَعْنِي اسْمَ الْفَاعِلِ وَالْمَفْعُولِ وَغَيْرَهُمَا، مُطْلَقًا.
text.en: Know that the attached marfūʿ [pronoun] alone is hidden: in the past, for the absent masculine and the absent feminine, as ḍaraba, that is, huwa “he”, and ḍarabat, that is, hiya “she”; in the muḍāriʿ, for the speaker in every case, as aḍribu “I hit”, that is, anā, and naḍribu “we hit”, that is, naḥnu; for the one addressed, as taḍribu “you hit”, that is, anta; and for the absent masculine and feminine, as yaḍribu “he hits”, that is, huwa, and taḍribu “she hits”, that is, hiya; and in the adjective — I mean the active and the passive participle and others — in every case.

text.original: وَلَا يَجُوزُ اسْتِعْمَالُ الْمُنْفَصِلِ إِلَّا عِنْدَ تَعَذُّرِ الْمُتَّصِلِ، كَإِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ، وَمَا ضَرَبَكَ إِلَّا أَنَا، وَأَنَا زَيْدٌ، وَمَا أَنْتَ إِلَّا قَائِمًا. وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ ضَمِيرًا غَائِبًا يَقَعُ قَبْلَ جُمْلَةٍ تُفَسِّرُهُ، وَيُسَمَّى ضَمِيرَ الشَّأْنِ فِي الْمُذَكَّرِ، وَضَمِيرَ الْقِصَّةِ فِي الْمُؤَنَّثِ، نَحْوُ: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ، وَإِنَّهَا زَيْنَبُ قَائِمَةٌ.
text.en: The separate [pronoun] may be used only when the attached one is impossible, as iyyāka naʿbudu “You [alone] we worship”, mā ḍarabaka illā anā “none hit you but I”, anā Zaydun “I am Zayd” and mā anta illā qāʾiman “you are nothing but standing”. Know that they have an absent pronoun that stands before a sentence that explains it; it is called the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) in the masculine and the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa) in the feminine, as qul huwa Allāhu aḥadun “say: He is God, One” and innahā Zaynabu qāʾimatun “indeed, [the story is that] Zaynab is standing”.

text.original: وَيَدْخُلُ بَيْنَ الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ صِيغَةُ مَرْفُوعٍ مُنْفَصِلٍ مُطَابِقٍ لِلْمُبْتَدَإِ إِذَا كَانَ الْخَبَرُ مَعْرِفَةً أَوْ أَفْعَلَ مِنْ كَذَا، وَيُسَمَّى فَصْلًا؛ لِأَنَّهُ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَ الْخَبَرِ وَالصِّفَةِ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ هُوَ الْقَائِمُ، وَكَانَ زَيْدٌ هُوَ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ عَمْرٍو، وَقَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ.
text.en: Between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar there comes the form of a separate marfūʿ [pronoun] agreeing with the mubtadaʾ, when the khabar is definite or [of the form] afʿal min kadhā; it is called faṣl (separator), because it separates the khabar from the adjective, as Zaydun huwa al-qāʾimu “Zayd is the one standing” and kāna Zaydun huwa afḍala min ʿAmrin “Zayd was better than ʿAmr”; and God Most High said: kunta anta al-raqība ʿalayhim “You were the Watcher over them”.

lessons.title: The demonstratives and the relatives
body: The demonstratives are “five words for six meanings”: dhā for the masculine; dhāni, dhayni for its dual; tā, tī, dhī, tih, dhih, tihī, dhihī for the feminine; tāni, tayni for its dual; and ulāʾi, or ulā, for the plural of both. The hā of calling attention may come before them: hādhā, hādhāni, hāʾulāʾi. And “the particle of address” may come after them, again five words for six meanings, ka, kumā, kum, ki, kunna, agreeing with the one spoken to: dhāka … dhākunna, dhānika … dhānikunna, twenty-five forms in all. Dhā is for the near, dhālika for the far, dhāka for what lies between.

The relative (mawṣūl) is “a noun that cannot be a complete part of a sentence without a ṣila after it”. The ṣila is a declarative sentence with a pronoun in it that refers back to the relative (ʿāʾid): jāʾa alladhī abūhu qāʾimun, or qāma abūhu. Alladhī alone means nothing; “the one whose father is standing” is a full part of the sentence, its fāʿil.

The relatives are alladhī; alladhāni, alladhayni; allatī; allatāni, allatayni; alladhīna and al-ulā for men; allātī, allawātī, allāʾi, allāʾī for women; and mā, man, ayyun, ayyatun. In the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ dhū means alladhī: wa-biʾrī dhū ḥafartu wa-dhū ṭawaytu, “and my well is the one I dug and the one I lined”. And the alif and lām on a participle is a relative: jāʾanī al-ḍāribu Zaydan, “that is, alladhī ḍaraba Zaydan”.

The referring pronoun may be dropped when it is an object: qāma alladhī ḍarabtu, “the one I hit stood”, for ḍarabtuhu. Ayyun and ayyatun are inflected, unlike the other relatives, “except when the beginning of their ṣila is dropped”: thumma la-nanziʿanna min kulli shīʿatin ayyuhum ashaddu ʿalā al-raḥmāni ʿitiyyan (Q 19:69), “that is, huwa ashaddu”. Ayyu there is the object of nanziʿanna, yet it ends in ḍamma: it has been built, because its ṣila has lost its mubtadaʾ.

tasks.prompt: Point to two men, speaking to a group of women, with the particle of address. Then point far off to one thing, speaking to one man.
tasks.answer: Dhānikunna: dhāni for the two men pointed at, -kunna for the women spoken to. Dhālika: for what is far, -ka for the one man addressed.

tasks.prompt: Find the relative, its ṣila and the referring pronoun: jāʾa alladhī qāma abūhu; qāma alladhī ḍarabtu.
tasks.arabic: جَاءَ الَّذِي قَامَ أَبُوهُ — قَامَ الَّذِي ضَرَبْتُ
tasks.answer: In the first: alladhī, its ṣila qāma abūhu, the referring pronoun the hāʾ of abūhu. In the second: alladhī, its ṣila ḍarabtu, the referring pronoun dropped, as an object: ḍarabtuhu.

tasks.prompt: Explain al-ḍāribu Zaydan as the book does.
tasks.answer: The alif and lām is a relative in the sense of alladhī, and the participle ḍārib is its ṣila: alladhī ḍaraba Zaydan, “the one who hit Zayd”.

tasks.prompt: Why does ayyu end in ḍamma in Q 19:69, though it is an object?
tasks.answer: Ayyun and ayyatun are inflected, except when the beginning of their ṣila is dropped. Here the ṣila is huwa ashaddu with huwa dropped, so ayyu is built on ḍamma, in naṣb in its place as the object of nanziʿanna.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: أَسْمَاءُ الْإِشَارَةِ مَا وُضِعَ لِيَدُلَّ عَلَى مُشَارٍ إِلَيْهِ، وَهِيَ خَمْسَةُ أَلْفَاظٍ لِسِتَّةِ مَعَانٍ: ذَا لِلْمُذَكَّرِ، وَذَانِ وَذَيْنِ لِمُثَنَّاهُ، وَتَا وَتِي وَذِي وَتِهْ وَذِهْ وَتِهِي وَذِهِي لِلْمُؤَنَّثِ، وَتَانِ وَتَيْنِ لِمُثَنَّاهُ، وَأُولَاءِ بِالْمَدِّ وَالْقَصْرِ لِجَمْعِهِمَا. وَقَدْ يَلْحَقُ بِأَوَائِلِهَا هَاءُ التَّنْبِيهِ، نَحْوُ: هَذَا، وَهَذَانِ، وَهَؤُلَاءِ.
text.en: Section. The demonstratives are what is laid down to indicate that which is pointed at. They are five words for six meanings: dhā for the masculine; dhāni and dhayni for its dual; tā, tī, dhī, tih, dhih, tihī and dhihī for the feminine; tāni and tayni for its dual; and ulāʾi, with the long and the short [alif], for the plural of both. The hāʾ of calling attention may be joined to their beginnings, as hādhā, hādhāni and hāʾulāʾi.

text.original: وَيَتَّصِلُ بِأَوَاخِرِهَا حَرْفُ الْخِطَابِ، وَهُوَ أَيْضًا خَمْسَةُ أَلْفَاظٍ لِسِتَّةِ مَعَانٍ، نَحْوُ: كَ، كُمَا، كُمْ، كِ، كُنَّ، فَذَلِكَ خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ، حَاصِلَةٌ مِنْ ضَرْبِ خَمْسَةٍ فِي خَمْسَةٍ، وَهِيَ: ذَاكَ إِلَى ذَاكُنَّ، وَذَانِكَ إِلَى ذَانِكُنَّ، وَكَذَلِكَ الْبَوَاقِي. وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ ذَا لِلْقَرِيبِ، وَذَلِكَ لِلْبَعِيدِ، وَذَاكَ لِلْمُتَوَسِّطِ.
text.en: The particle of address is attached to their ends; it too is five words for six meanings, as ka, kumā, kum, ki and kunna. That makes twenty-five, coming from multiplying five by five: they are dhāka to dhākunna, dhānika to dhānikunna, and likewise the rest. Know that dhā is for the near, dhālika for the far, and dhāka for the middle.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَوْصُولُ اسْمٌ لَا يَصْلُحُ أَنْ يَكُونَ جُزْءًا تَامًّا مِنْ جُمْلَةٍ إِلَّا بِصِلَةٍ بَعْدَهُ، وَالصِّلَةُ جُمْلَةٌ خَبَرِيَّةٌ، وَلَا بُدَّ مِنْ عَائِدٍ فِيهَا يَعُودُ إِلَى الْمَوْصُولِ، مِثَالُهُ: الَّذِي فِي قَوْلِنَا: جَاءَ الَّذِي أَبُوهُ قَائِمٌ، أَوْ قَامَ أَبُوهُ. وَهُوَ الَّذِي لِلْمُذَكَّرِ، وَاللَّذَانِ وَاللَّذَيْنِ لِمُثَنَّاهُ، وَالَّتِي لِلْمُؤَنَّثِ، وَاللَّتَانِ وَاللَّتَيْنِ لِمُثَنَّاهَا، وَالَّذِينَ وَالْأُلَى لِجَمْعِ الْمُذَكَّرِ، وَاللَّاتِي وَاللَّوَاتِي وَاللَّاءِ وَاللَّائِي لِجَمْعِ الْمُؤَنَّثِ، وَمَا، وَمَنْ، وَأَيٌّ، وَأَيَّةٌ.
text.en: Section. The relative (mawṣūl) is a noun that cannot be a complete part of a sentence without a ṣila after it. The ṣila is a declarative sentence, and there must be in it a returning [pronoun] (ʿāʾid) that refers to the relative; its example is alladhī in our saying jāʾa alladhī abūhu qāʾimun “the one whose father is standing came” or qāma abūhu “whose father stood”. It is alladhī for the masculine; alladhāni and alladhayni for its dual; allatī for the feminine; allatāni and allatayni for its dual; alladhīna and al-ulā for the masculine plural; allātī, allawātī, allāʾi and allāʾī for the feminine plural; and mā, man, ayyun and ayyatun.

text.original: وَذُو بِمَعْنَى الَّذِي فِي لُغَةِ بَنِي طَيِّئٍ، كَقَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ، شِعْرٌ: فَإِنَّ الْمَاءَ مَاءُ أَبِي وَجَدِّي * وَبِئْرِي ذُو حَفَرْتُ وَذُو طَوَيْتُ، أَيِ الَّذِي حَفَرْتُهُ وَالَّذِي طَوَيْتُهُ. وَالْأَلِفُ وَاللَّامُ بِمَعْنَى الَّذِي، صِلَتُهَا اسْمُ الْفَاعِلِ وَاسْمُ الْمَفْعُولِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي الضَّارِبُ زَيْدًا، أَيِ الَّذِي ضَرَبَ زَيْدًا، وَجَاءَ الْمَضْرُوبُ غُلَامُهُ.
text.en: Dhū is in the meaning of alladhī in the dialect of the Banū Ṭayyiʾ, as in the poet's saying, verse: fa-inna al-māʾa māʾu abī wa-jaddī / wa-biʾrī dhū ḥafartu wa-dhū ṭawaytu “For the water is the water of my father and my grandfather, / and my well is the one I dug and the one I lined”, that is, alladhī ḥafartuhu wa-alladhī ṭawaytuhu “which I dug and which I lined”. The alif and lām are in the meaning of alladhī; their ṣila is the active participle and the passive participle, as jāʾanī al-ḍāribu Zaydan “the one who hit Zayd came to me”, that is, alladhī ḍaraba Zaydan, and jāʾa al-maḍrūbu ghulāmuhu “the one whose servant was hit came”.

text.original: وَيَجُوزُ حَذْفُ الْعَائِدِ مِنَ اللَّفْظِ إِنْ كَانَ مَفْعُولًا، نَحْوُ: قَامَ الَّذِي ضَرَبْتُ، أَيِ الَّذِي ضَرَبْتُهُ. وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ أَيًّا وَأَيَّةً مُعْرَبَةٌ إِلَّا إِذَا حُذِفَ صَدْرُ صِلَتِهَا، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمَنِ عِتِيًّا، أَيْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ.
text.en: The returning [pronoun] may be dropped from the wording if it is a mafʿūl, as qāma alladhī ḍarabtu “the one I hit stood”, that is, alladhī ḍarabtuhu. Know that ayy and ayya are inflected, except when the beginning of their ṣila is dropped, as in His saying, exalted is He: thumma la-nanziʿanna min kulli shīʿatin ayyuhum ashaddu ʿalā al-raḥmāni ʿitiyyan “then We shall pluck out from every party whichever of them was most stubborn against the Merciful”, that is, huwa ashaddu “he is most”.

lessons.title: Nouns of verbs; faʿāli; the sounds; the compounds
body: A noun of a verb is “every noun in the meaning of the imperative or of the past”: ruwayda Zaydan, “that is, amhilhu”, give him time; hayhāta Zaydun, “that is, baʿuda”, far is Zayd. The pattern faʿāli in the sense of the imperative is “by rule from the triliteral”: nazāli, “dismount!”, tarāki, “leave!”. It is a pattern a student may form, not only a list of words to learn.

The book joins to them three other uses of faʿāli, built on kasra like them, “mentioned here only because they fit”: a definite maṣdar, fajāri for al-fujūr, “wickedness”; an adjective of a woman in calling, yā fasāqi, yā lakāʿi, “O wicked woman!”, “O base woman!”; and the names of women, Qaṭāmi, Ghalābi, Ḥaḍāri. “These three are not among the nouns of verbs.”

The sounds (aṣwāt) are words that imitate a sound, as ghāqi for the crow's cry, or that are said to beasts, as nakh to make a camel kneel. They are words without a meaning to build a sentence on, so they never take iʿrāb.

The compounds are nouns made of two words “between which there is no relation”, neither iḍāfa nor predication. If the second contains the meaning of a particle, both are built on fatḥa: aḥada ʿashara to tisʿata ʿashara; “except ithnay ʿashara, for it is inflected like the dual”: ithnā ʿashara in rafʿ, ithnay ʿashara in naṣb and jarr. If not, there are several dialects, “the most correct” being to build the first part on fatḥa and give the second the iʿrāb of a diptote: jāʾanī Baʿlabakku, raʾaytu Baʿlabakka, marartu bi-Baʿlabakka (lesson 8).

tasks.prompt: Give the verb each noun of a verb stands for: ruwayda; hayhāta; nazāli; tarāki.
tasks.answer: Ruwayda: amhil, “give time”. Hayhāta: baʿuda, “it is far”. Nazāli: inzil, “dismount”. Tarāki: utruk, “leave”.

tasks.prompt: Are fajāri and Qaṭāmi nouns of verbs? Why does the book mention them here?
tasks.answer: No. Fajāri is a definite maṣdar and Qaṭāmi a woman's name; they share the pattern faʿāli and its binā on kasra, and are mentioned here only because they fit.

tasks.prompt: Parse the number in jāʾanī ithnā ʿashara rajulan and in raʾaytu aḥada ʿashara rajulan.
tasks.arabic: جَاءَنِي اثْنَا عَشَرَ رَجُلًا — رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ رَجُلًا
tasks.answer: Ithnā ʿashara: the first part is inflected like a dual, in rafʿ by the alif, as the fāʿil; ʿashara is built on fatḥa. Aḥada ʿashara: both parts are built on fatḥa, in naṣb in their place as the object. Rajulan is the tamyīz in both.

tasks.prompt: Why is the sound nakh never inflected?
tasks.answer: It is said to a camel to make it kneel; it is not put together with other words as a part of a sentence, so no governor works on it, and it is built.
