tasks.prompt: How does the book reach eighteen questions?
tasks.answer: The adjective has the lām or not (2). The governed word is muḍāf to a pronoun, has the lām, or has neither (×3 = 6). That word is in rafʿ, naṣb or jarr (×3 = 18).

tasks.prompt: Count the pronouns and give the judgement: ḥasanun wajhuhu; ḥasanun wajhahu; ḥasanun al-wajhu; ḥasanun wajhan.
tasks.arabic: حَسَنٌ وَجْهُهُ — حَسَنٌ وَجْهَهُ — حَسَنٌ الْوَجْهُ — حَسَنٌ وَجْهًا
tasks.answer: Ḥasanun wajhuhu: rafʿ, so none in the adjective, one (the hāʾ): best. Ḥasanun wajhahu: naṣb, one hidden in the adjective and the hāʾ: two, good. Ḥasanun al-wajhu: rafʿ and no hāʾ: none, ugly. Ḥasanun wajhan: naṣb, one hidden in the adjective: best.

tasks.prompt: Why are al-ḥasanu wajhihi and al-ḥasanu wajhin impossible?
tasks.answer: In both an adjective with the lām is made muḍāf to a word without the lām, and such an iḍāfa of wording is not allowed: it would give no lightness.

tasks.prompt: Why does the resembling adjective govern without a condition of time, unlike the participle?
tasks.answer: It indicates a lasting quality (thubūt), not an act at a time; a condition of present or future would mean nothing for it. Only the condition of leaning remains.

quiz.prompt: The resembling adjective has the sense of…
quiz.explanation: Thubūt, as against the participle's ḥudūth.

quiz.prompt: Which is disputed?

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الصِّفَةُ الْمُشَبَّهَةُ اسْمٌ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنْ فِعْلٍ لَازِمٍ لِيَدُلَّ عَلَى مَنْ قَامَ بِهِ الْفِعْلُ بِمَعْنَى الثُّبُوتِ، وَصِيغَتُهَا عَلَى خِلَافِ صِيغَةِ اسْمِ الْفَاعِلِ وَالْمَفْعُولِ، إِنَّمَا تُعْرَفُ بِالسَّمَاعِ، كَحَسَنٍ وَصَعْبٍ وَظَرِيفٍ، وَهِيَ تَعْمَلُ عَمَلَ فِعْلِهَا مُطْلَقًا بِشَرْطِ الِاعْتِمَادِ الْمَذْكُورِ.
text.en: Section. The adjective like the participle (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha) is a noun derived from an intransitive verb to indicate the one in whom the act stands, in the sense of lasting (thubūt). Its form differs from the form of the active and passive participles and is known only by hearing, as ḥasanin “beautiful”, ṣaʿbin “hard” and ẓarīfin “witty”. It governs as its verb governs, in every case, on condition of the leaning mentioned.

text.original: وَمَسَائِلُهَا ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ؛ لِأَنَّ الصِّفَةَ إِمَّا بِاللَّامِ أَوْ مُجَرَّدَةٌ عَنْهَا، وَمَعْمُولُ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا إِمَّا مُضَافٌ أَوْ بِاللَّامِ أَوْ مُجَرَّدٌ عَنْهُمَا، فَهَذِهِ سِتَّةٌ، وَمَعْمُولُ كُلٍّ مِنْهَا إِمَّا مَرْفُوعٌ أَوْ مَنْصُوبٌ أَوْ مَجْرُورٌ، فَذَلِكَ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ. وَتَفْصِيلُهَا نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ الْحَسَنُ وَجْهُهُ، ثَلَاثَةُ أَوْجُهٍ، وَكَذَلِكَ: الْحَسَنُ الْوَجْهُ، وَالْحَسَنُ وَجْهٌ، وَحَسَنٌ وَجْهُهُ، وَحَسَنٌ الْوَجْهُ، وَحَسَنٌ وَجْهٌ.
text.en: Its questions are eighteen; for the adjective is either with the lām or free of it, and the governed word of each of them is either muḍāf, or with the lām, or free of both — that makes six —; and the governed word of each of these is either marfūʿ, manṣūb or majrūr; that makes eighteen. They are set out as jāʾanī Zaydun al-ḥasanu wajhuhu “Zayd, the one beautiful of face, came to me”, in three ways; and likewise al-ḥasanu al-wajhu, wa-al-ḥasanu wajhun, wa-ḥasanun wajhuhu, wa-ḥasanun al-wajhu and wa-ḥasanun wajhun.

text.original: وَهِيَ عَلَى خَمْسَةِ أَقْسَامٍ: مِنْهَا مُمْتَنِعٌ: الْحَسَنُ وَجْهِهِ، وَالْحَسَنُ وَجْهٍ، وَمُخْتَلَفٌ فِيهِ: حَسَنُ وَجْهِهِ، وَالْبَوَاقِي: أَحْسَنُ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ ضَمِيرٌ وَاحِدٌ، وَحَسَنٌ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ ضَمِيرَانِ، وَقَبِيحٌ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ ضَمِيرٌ. وَالضَّابِطَةُ أَنَّكَ مَتَى رَفَعْتَ بِهَا مَعْمُولَهَا فَلَا ضَمِيرَ فِي الصِّفَةِ، وَمَتَى نَصَبْتَ أَوْ جَرَرْتَ فَفِيهَا ضَمِيرُ الْمَوْصُوفِ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ حَسَنٌ وَجْهَهُ.
text.en: They are of five kinds. Among them is the impossible: al-ḥasanu wajhihi and wa-al-ḥasanu wajhin; the disputed: ḥasanu wajhihi; and the rest: best (aḥsan), if there is one pronoun in it; good (ḥasan), if there are two pronouns in it; and ugly (qabīḥ), if there is no pronoun in it. The rule of thumb is that whenever you put its governed word in rafʿ by it, there is no pronoun in the adjective, and whenever you put it in naṣb or jarr, there is in it the pronoun of the described noun, as Zaydun ḥasanun wajhahu.

lessons.title: The elative
body: The elative (ism al-tafḍīl) “indicates the described thing with an excess over another”. Its form is afʿal, and it is built “only from the bare triliteral that is not of colour or defect”: Zaydun afḍalu al-nāsi. The commentators give the reason for the last condition: colours and defects already have their adjective on afʿal, aḥmar, aʿraj, so an elative of the same form would be confused with it.

For a verb of more than three letters, or of colour or defect, one builds an afʿal from a bare triliteral meaning intensity, strength or abundance, and puts the maṣdar of the verb after it as a tamyīz: huwa ashaddu istikhrājan, “stronger in bringing out”; aqwā ḥumratan, “stronger in redness”; aqbaḥu ʿarajan, “uglier in lameness”. In its rule the elative is for the doer; a few are for the one acted upon: aʿdhar, “more excused”, ashghal, “more occupied”, ashhar, “better known”.

It is used in three ways. Muḍāf: Zaydun afḍalu al-qawmi, and then it may stay singular or agree: al-Zaydāni afḍalu al-qawmi or afḍalā al-qawmi, al-Zaydūna afḍalu or afḍalū al-qawmi. With the lām: Zaydun al-afḍalu, and then it must agree: al-Zaydāni al-afḍalāni, al-Zaydūna al-afḍalūna. With min: Zaydun afḍalu min ʿAmrin, and then it is always singular and masculine, whoever is described: Zaydun wa-Hindun wa-al-Zaydāni … wa-al-Hindātu afḍalu min ʿAmrin.

In all three its fāʿil is a pronoun hidden in it, and it governs that pronoun; “it never governs an explicit noun”, except in the famous sentence mā raʾaytu rajulan aḥsana fī ʿaynihi al-kuḥlu minhu fī ʿayni Zaydin, “I have not seen a man in whose eye kohl is more beautiful than in the eye of Zayd”, where al-kuḥlu is the fāʿil of aḥsana. “And here there is a matter for discussion”: the book leaves its conditions to the Kāfiya and its commentaries. With this the part on the noun ends.

tasks.prompt: From which verbs may afʿal be built directly, and what is done for the others?
tasks.answer: Only from a bare triliteral that is not of colour or defect, as afḍal. For a longer verb, or one of colour or defect, an afʿal of intensity is built (ashadd, aqwā, aqbaḥ) and the maṣdar of the verb follows as a tamyīz: ashaddu istikhrājan, aqwā ḥumratan, aqbaḥu ʿarajan.

tasks.prompt: Complete with the elative of faḍl and say whether agreement is allowed, required or forbidden: al-Hindātu … min ʿAmrin; al-Zaydūna … al-qawmi; al-Zaydāni al-….
tasks.answer: Al-Hindātu afḍalu min ʿAmrin: with min it must stay singular masculine. Al-Zaydūna afḍalu al-qawmi or afḍalū al-qawmi: muḍāf, both are allowed. Al-Zaydāni al-afḍalāni: with the lām, agreement is required.

tasks.prompt: What is the fāʿil of afḍalu in Zaydun afḍalu min ʿAmrin?
tasks.answer: A pronoun hidden in it, going back to Zayd. The elative governs that pronoun; it does not govern an explicit fāʿil.

tasks.prompt: In the question of the kohl, what is the fāʿil of aḥsana?
tasks.arabic: مَا رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا أَحْسَنَ فِي عَيْنِهِ الْكُحْلُ مِنْهُ فِي عَيْنِ زَيْدٍ
tasks.answer: Al-kuḥlu, an explicit noun: this sentence is the one case the book allows where the elative governs an explicit fāʿil.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: اسْمُ التَّفْضِيلِ اسْمٌ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنْ فِعْلٍ لِيَدُلَّ عَلَى الْمَوْصُوفِ بِزِيَادَةٍ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ، وَصِيغَتُهُ أَفْعَلُ، فَلَا يُبْنَى إِلَّا مِنَ الثُّلَاثِيِّ الْمُجَرَّدِ الَّذِي لَيْسَ بِلَوْنٍ وَلَا عَيْبٍ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ النَّاسِ.
text.en: Section. The elative (ism al-tafḍīl) is a noun derived from a verb to indicate the described thing with an excess over another. Its form is afʿalu; it is built only from the bare triliteral that is not [a verb of] colour or defect, as Zaydun afḍalu al-nāsi “Zayd is the most excellent of people”.

text.original: فَإِنْ كَانَ زَائِدًا عَلَى الثُّلَاثِيِّ، أَوْ كَانَ لَوْنًا أَوْ عَيْبًا، يَجِبُ أَنْ يُبْنَى أَفْعَلُ مِنْ ثُلَاثِيٍّ مُجَرَّدٍ لِيَدُلَّ عَلَى مُبَالَغَةٍ وَشِدَّةٍ وَكَثْرَةٍ، ثُمَّ يُذْكَرُ بَعْدَهُ مَصْدَرُ ذَلِكَ الْفِعْلِ مَنْصُوبًا عَلَى التَّمْيِيزِ، كَمَا تَقُولُ: هُوَ أَشَدُّ اسْتِخْرَاجًا، وَأَقْوَى حُمْرَةً، وَأَقْبَحُ عَرَجًا. وَقِيَاسُهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِلْفَاعِلِ، كَمَا مَرَّ، وَقَدْ جَاءَ لِلْمَفْعُولِ قَلِيلًا، نَحْوُ: أَعْذَرُ، وَأَشْغَلُ، وَأَشْهَرُ.
text.en: If [the verb] is more than triliteral, or is [one of] colour or defect, an afʿal must be built from a bare triliteral to indicate intensity, strength and abundance, and then the maṣdar of that verb is mentioned after it in naṣb as a tamyīz, as you say huwa ashaddu istikhrājan “he is stronger in bringing out”, wa-aqwā ḥumratan “and stronger in redness” and wa-aqbaḥu ʿarajan “and uglier in lameness”. Its rule is that it is for the doer, as has passed; and it has come for the one acted upon, rarely, as aʿdharu “more excused”, wa-ashghalu “more busied” and wa-ashharu “better known”.

text.original: وَاسْتِعْمَالُهُ عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ أَوْجُهٍ: إِمَّا مُضَافٌ، كَمَا مَرَّ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ الْقَوْمِ، أَوْ مُعَرَّفٌ بِاللَّامِ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ الْأَفْضَلُ، أَوْ بِمِنْ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ عَمْرٍو. وَيَجُوزُ فِي الْأَوَّلِ الْإِفْرَادُ وَمُطَابَقَةُ اسْمِ التَّفْضِيلِ لِلْمَوْصُوفِ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ الْقَوْمِ، وَالزَّيْدَانِ أَفْضَلُ الْقَوْمِ وَأَفْضَلَا الْقَوْمِ، وَالزَّيْدُونَ أَفْضَلُ الْقَوْمِ وَأَفْضَلُو الْقَوْمِ.
text.en: Its use is in three ways: either muḍāf, as has passed, as Zaydun afḍalu al-qawmi “Zayd is the most excellent of the people”; or defined by the lām, as Zaydun al-afḍalu “Zayd is the most excellent”; or with min, as Zaydun afḍalu min ʿAmrin “Zayd is more excellent than ʿAmr”. In the first, the singular and the agreement of the elative with the described noun are both allowed, as Zaydun afḍalu al-qawmi, wa-al-Zaydāni afḍalu al-qawmi and wa-afḍalā al-qawmi “and the two Zayds are the most excellent of the people”, and wa-al-Zaydūna afḍalu al-qawmi and wa-afḍalū al-qawmi “and the Zayds are the most excellent of the people”.

text.original: وَفِي الثَّانِي يَجِبُ الْمُطَابَقَةُ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ الْأَفْضَلُ، وَالزَّيْدَانِ الْأَفْضَلَانِ، وَالزَّيْدُونَ الْأَفْضَلُونَ. وَفِي الثَّالِثِ يَجِبُ كَوْنُهُ مُفْرَدًا مُذَكَّرًا أَبَدًا، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ وَهِنْدٌ وَالزَّيْدَانِ وَالْهِنْدَانِ وَالزَّيْدُونَ وَالْهِنْدَاتُ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ عَمْرٍو.
text.en: In the second, agreement is necessary, as Zaydun al-afḍalu, wa-al-Zaydāni al-afḍalāni and wa-al-Zaydūna al-afḍalūna. In the third it must always be singular and masculine, as Zaydun wa-Hindun wa-al-Zaydāni wa-al-Hindāni wa-al-Zaydūna wa-al-Hindātu afḍalu min ʿAmrin “Zayd, Hind, the two Zayds, the two Hinds, the Zayds and the Hinds are more excellent than ʿAmr”.

text.original: وَعَلَى الْأَوْجُهِ الثَّلَاثَةِ يُضْمَرُ فِيهِ الْفَاعِلُ، وَهُوَ يَعْمَلُ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمُضْمَرِ، وَلَا يَعْمَلُ فِي الْمُظْهَرِ أَصْلًا إِلَّا فِي مِثْلِ قَوْلِهِمْ: مَا رَأَيْتُ رَجُلًا أَحْسَنَ فِي عَيْنِهِ الْكُحْلُ مِنْهُ فِي عَيْنِ زَيْدٍ؛ فَإِنَّ الْكُحْلَ فَاعِلٌ لِأَحْسَنَ، وَهَهُنَا بَحْثٌ.
text.en: In the three ways the fāʿil is hidden in it as a pronoun, and it governs that pronoun; it never governs an explicit noun, except in such [a phrase] as their saying mā raʾaytu rajulan aḥsana fī ʿaynihi al-kuḥlu minhu fī ʿayni Zaydin “I have not seen a man in whose eye kohl is more beautiful than in the eye of Zayd”; for al-kuḥlu is the fāʿil of aḥsana; and here there is [a matter for] discussion.

lessons.title: The verb: the past and the muḍāriʿ
body: The second part is on the verb, of three kinds: the past, the muḍāriʿ and the imperative. The past “indicates a time before your time”, and it is built. On fatḥa when no vowelled marfūʿ pronoun and no wāw is joined to it, ḍaraba; on sukūn with a vowelled marfūʿ pronoun, ḍarabtu; on ḍamma with the wāw, ḍarabū.

The muḍāriʿ is “a verb that resembles the noun”, with one of the letters of atayna (a, t, y, n) at its beginning. It resembles the noun in its wording, with the same order of vowels and sukūns, yaḍribu as ḍārib, yastakhriju as mustakhrij, and the same number of letters; in taking the lām of emphasis, inna Zaydan la-yaqūmu as inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun; and in its meaning, shared between the present and the future like the active participle. “For that reason they named it muḍāriʿ”, “resembling”.

The sīn and sawfa make it future, sa-yaḍribu, sawfa yaḍribu; the lām with fatḥa makes it present, la-yaḍribu. Its prefix has a ḍamma in a verb of four letters, yudaḥriju, yukhriju, “for its original form is yuʾakhriju”, and a fatḥa in all others, yaḍribu, yastakhriju.

Why does a verb take iʿrāb at all, when “the base of the verb is binā”? Because the muḍāriʿ resembles the noun, “and the base of the noun is iʿrāb”. So it is inflected as long as neither the nūn of emphasis nor the nūn of the feminine plural is joined to it; with them it is built again. Its iʿrāb is rafʿ, naṣb and jazm: huwa yaḍribu, lan yaḍriba, lam yaḍrib. Jazm takes the place that jarr has in the noun.

terms.en: the past: built on fatḥa, sukūn or ḍamma
the verb that resembles the noun, with a prefix of atayna

tasks.prompt: On what is each past built, and why? ḍaraba; ḍarabtu; ḍarabū.
tasks.answer: Ḍaraba: on fatḥa, with no pronoun joined. Ḍarabtu: on sukūn, with the vowelled marfūʿ pronoun tu. Ḍarabū: on ḍamma, with the wāw.

tasks.prompt: Name three ways in which the muḍāriʿ resembles the noun.
tasks.answer: Its vowels and sukūns follow the noun's (yaḍribu, ḍārib), with the same number of letters; it takes the lām of emphasis as the noun does (la-yaqūmu, la-qāʾimun); and it means the present or the future, like the active participle.

tasks.prompt: Why does yukhriju begin with a ḍamma and yaḍribu with a fatḥa?
tasks.answer: The prefix has a ḍamma in a verb of four letters (akhraja, whose muḍāriʿ is in origin yuʾakhriju) and a fatḥa in all others.

tasks.prompt: When is the muḍāriʿ inflected, and why?
tasks.answer: When neither the nūn of emphasis nor the nūn of the feminine plural is joined to it. The verb's base is binā, but the muḍāriʿ resembles the noun, whose base is iʿrāb, so it takes iʿrāb.

text.original: وَقَدْ سَبَقَ تَعْرِيفُهُ، وَأَقْسَامُهُ ثَلَاثَةٌ: مَاضٍ، وَمُضَارِعٌ، وَأَمْرٌ. الْأَوَّلُ الْمَاضِي، وَهُوَ فِعْلٌ دَلَّ عَلَى زَمَانٍ قَبْلَ زَمَانِكَ، وَهُوَ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى الْفَتْحِ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ مَعَهُ ضَمِيرٌ مَرْفُوعٌ مُتَحَرِّكٌ وَلَا وَاوٌ، كَضَرَبَ، وَمَعَ الضَّمِيرِ الْمَرْفُوعِ الْمُتَحَرِّكِ عَلَى السُّكُونِ، كَضَرَبْتُ، وَعَلَى الضَّمِّ مَعَ الْوَاوِ، كَضَرَبُوا.
text.en: Its definition has passed already. Its kinds are three: past (māḍī), muḍāriʿ and imperative (amr). The first is the past: it is a verb that indicates a time before your time. It is fixed on the fatḥa if there is no vowelled marfūʿ pronoun with it and no wāw, as ḍaraba “he hit”; with the vowelled marfūʿ pronoun it is on the sukūn, as ḍarabtu “I hit”; and on the ḍamma with the wāw, as ḍarabū “they hit”.

text.original: وَالثَّانِي الْمُضَارِعُ، وَهُوَ فِعْلٌ يُشْبِهُ الِاسْمَ بِأَحَدِ حُرُوفِ أَتَيْنَ فِي أَوَّلِهِ، لَفْظًا فِي اتِّفَاقِ الْحَرَكَاتِ وَالسَّكَنَاتِ، نَحْوُ: يَضْرِبُ وَيَسْتَخْرِجُ، كَضَارِبٍ وَمُسْتَخْرِجٍ، وَفِي دُخُولِ لَامِ التَّأْكِيدِ فِي أَوَّلِهِمَا، تَقُولُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَيَقُومُ، كَمَا تَقُولُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَقَائِمٌ، وَفِي تَسَاوِيهِمَا فِي عَدَدِ الْحُرُوفِ؛ وَمَعْنًى فِي أَنَّهُ مُشْتَرَكٌ بَيْنَ الْحَالِ وَالِاسْتِقْبَالِ، كَاسْمِ الْفَاعِلِ، وَلِذَلِكَ سَمَّوْهُ مُضَارِعًا.
text.en: The second is the muḍāriʿ: it is a verb that resembles the noun, with one of the letters of atayna at its beginning: in the wording, in the agreement of the vowels and the unvowelled letters, as yaḍribu and yastakhriju, like ḍāribin and mustakhrijin; in the coming of the lām of emphasis at the beginning of both — you say inna Zaydan la-yaqūmu “Zayd is surely standing”, as you say inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun “Zayd is surely standing” —; and in their being equal in the number of letters; and in meaning, in that it is shared between the present and the future, like the active participle. For that reason they named it muḍāriʿ (resembling).

text.original: وَالسِّينُ وَسَوْفَ تُخَصِّصُهُ بِالِاسْتِقْبَالِ، نَحْوُ: سَيَضْرِبُ، وَسَوْفَ يَضْرِبُ، وَاللَّامُ الْمَفْتُوحَةُ بِالْحَالِ، نَحْوُ: لَيَضْرِبُ. وَحُرُوفُ الْمُضَارَعَةِ مَضْمُومَةٌ فِي الرُّبَاعِيِّ، نَحْوُ: يُدَحْرِجُ وَيُخْرِجُ؛ لِأَنَّ أَصْلَهُ يُؤَخْرِجُ، وَمَفْتُوحَةٌ فِيمَا عَدَاهُ، كَيَضْرِبُ وَيَسْتَخْرِجُ.
text.en: The sīn and sawfa make it particular to the future, as sa-yaḍribu and wa-sawfa yaḍribu “he will hit”; and the lām with fatḥa to the present, as la-yaḍribu “he is surely hitting”. The prefixes of the muḍāriʿ have a ḍamma in the quadriliteral, as yudaḥriju “he rolls” and yukhriju “he brings out” — for its original form is yuʾakhriju —, and a fatḥa in what is other than it, as yaḍribu and yastakhriju.

text.original: وَإِنَّمَا أُعْرِبَ، مَعَ أَنَّ أَصْلَ الْفِعْلِ الْبِنَاءُ، لِمُضَارَعَتِهِ الِاسْمَ، وَأَصْلُ الِاسْمِ الْإِعْرَابُ، وَذَلِكَ إِذَا لَمْ يَتَّصِلْ بِهِ نُونُ التَّأْكِيدِ وَلَا نُونُ جَمْعِ الْمُؤَنَّثِ. وَإِعْرَابُهُ ثَلَاثَةُ أَنْوَاعٍ: رَفْعٌ، وَنَصْبٌ، وَجَزْمٌ، نَحْوُ: هُوَ يَضْرِبُ، وَلَنْ يَضْرِبَ، وَلَمْ يَضْرِبْ.
text.en: It is inflected — although the base of the verb is bināʾ — only because of its resemblance (muḍāraʿa) to the noun, and the base of the noun is iʿrāb; this is when neither the nūn of emphasis nor the nūn of the feminine plural is joined to it. Its iʿrāb is of three kinds: rafʿ, naṣb and jazm, as huwa yaḍribu “he hits”, wa-lan yaḍriba “and he will not hit” and wa-lam yaḍrib “and he did not hit”.

lessons.title: The four kinds of the verb's iʿrāb; the muḍāriʿ in rafʿ
body: As the noun had nine kinds of iʿrāb (lessons 5–6), the verb has four. The first: rafʿ by the ḍamma, naṣb by the fatḥa, jazm by the sukūn. It belongs to “the sound singular that is not the woman addressed”: huwa yaḍribu, lan yaḍriba, lam yaḍrib.

The second: rafʿ by the nūn kept, naṣb and jazm by the nūn dropped. It belongs to the dual, the masculine plural and the woman addressed, “sound or not”: humā yafʿalāni, hum yafʿalūna, anti tafʿalīna; lan yafʿalā, lan yafʿalū, lan tafʿalī; lam yafʿalā, lam yafʿalū, lam tafʿalī. The alif, wāw and yāʾ stay: they are the pronouns, the fāʿil; only the nūn, the sign of rafʿ, comes and goes.

The third and fourth belong to the defective verb (nāqiṣ), whose last root letter is weak, when it is not dual, plural or the woman addressed. With yāʾ or wāw, rafʿ is by an implied ḍamma, naṣb by the fatḥa heard, and jazm by dropping the last letter: yarmī, yaghzū; lan yarmiya, lan yaghzuwa; lam yarmi, lam yaghzu. With alif, both rafʿ and naṣb are implied, and jazm drops the alif: yasʿā, lan yasʿā, lam yasʿa.

What puts the muḍāriʿ in rafʿ? “Its governor is abstract, namely its being free of what puts it in naṣb and what puts it in jazm”: huwa yaḍribu, yaghzū, yarmī, yasʿā. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ and the Kūfans; the Baṣrans say instead that it is raised by standing where a noun could stand.

terms.en: the nūn kept for rafʿ, dropped for naṣb and jazm
the defective verb, its last root letter weak

being free of naṣb and jazm: the governor of the muḍāriʿ in rafʿ

tasks.prompt: Give the kind of iʿrāb and its sign: lan tafʿalī; lam yaghzu; huwa yasʿā; lan yarmiya.
tasks.arabic: لَنْ تَفْعَلِي — لَمْ يَغْزُ — هُوَ يَسْعَى — لَنْ يَرْمِيَ
tasks.answer: Lan tafʿalī: the second kind, naṣb by dropping the nūn. Lam yaghzu: the third, jazm by dropping the wāw. Huwa yasʿā: the fourth, rafʿ by an implied ḍamma. Lan yarmiya: the third, naṣb by the fatḥa heard.

tasks.prompt: Why does the yāʾ of tafʿalīna stay in lan tafʿalī, while the nūn goes?
tasks.answer: The yāʾ is the pronoun of the woman addressed, the fāʿil; the nūn is only the sign of rafʿ, kept in rafʿ and dropped in naṣb and jazm.

tasks.prompt: Why is the naṣb of yarmī heard but that of yasʿā not?
tasks.answer: The light fatḥa can be spoken on a yāʾ or a wāw (lan yarmiya, lan yaghzuwa), but an alif carries no vowel at all, so in yasʿā the fatḥa is implied.

tasks.prompt: What puts yaḍribu in rafʿ in huwa yaḍribu, according to the book, and what do the Baṣrans say?
tasks.answer: The book: an abstract governor, its being free of every governor of naṣb and jazm, the view of al-Farrāʾ and the Kūfans. The Baṣrans: its standing in a place where a noun could stand.

text.original: فَصْلٌ فِي أَصْنَافِ إِعْرَابِ الْفِعْلِ، وَهِيَ أَرْبَعَةٌ: الْأَوَّلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الرَّفْعُ بِالضَّمَّةِ، وَالنَّصْبُ بِالْفَتْحَةِ، وَالْجَزْمُ بِالسُّكُونِ، وَيَخْتَصُّ بِالْمُفْرَدِ الصَّحِيحِ غَيْرِ مُخَاطَبَةٍ، تَقُولُ: هُوَ يَضْرِبُ، وَلَنْ يَضْرِبَ، وَلَمْ يَضْرِبْ.
text.en: Section on the kinds of the iʿrāb of the verb. They are four. The first: that rafʿ is by the ḍamma, naṣb by the fatḥa and jazm by the sukūn. It belongs to the sound singular that is not [the feminine] addressed; you say huwa yaḍribu, wa-lan yaḍriba and wa-lam yaḍrib.

text.original: وَالثَّانِي أَنْ يَكُونَ الرَّفْعُ بِثُبُوتِ النُّونِ، وَالنَّصْبُ وَالْجَزْمُ بِحَذْفِهَا، وَيَخْتَصُّ بِالتَّثْنِيَةِ وَجَمْعِ الْمُذَكَّرِ وَالْمُفْرَدَةِ الْمُخَاطَبَةِ، صَحِيحًا كَانَ أَوْ غَيْرَهُ، تَقُولُ: هُمَا يَفْعَلَانِ، وَهُمْ يَفْعَلُونَ، وَأَنْتِ تَفْعَلِينَ، وَلَنْ يَفْعَلَا، وَلَنْ يَفْعَلُوا، وَلَنْ تَفْعَلِي، وَلَمْ يَفْعَلَا، وَلَمْ يَفْعَلُوا، وَلَمْ تَفْعَلِي.
text.en: The second: that rafʿ is by the keeping of the nūn, and naṣb and jazm by its dropping. It belongs to the dual, the masculine plural and the singular feminine addressed, sound or not; you say humā yafʿalāni “they two do”, wa-hum yafʿalūna “and they do” and wa-anti tafʿalīna “and you (f.) do”; wa-lan yafʿalā, wa-lan yafʿalū and wa-lan tafʿalī; and wa-lam yafʿalā, wa-lam yafʿalū and wa-lam tafʿalī.

text.original: وَالثَّالِثُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الرَّفْعُ بِتَقْدِيرِ الضَّمَّةِ، وَالنَّصْبُ بِالْفَتْحَةِ لَفْظًا، وَالْجَزْمُ بِحَذْفِ اللَّامِ، وَيَخْتَصُّ بِالنَّاقِصِ الْيَائِيِّ وَالْوَاوِيِّ غَيْرِ تَثْنِيَةٍ وَجَمْعٍ وَمُخَاطَبَةٍ، تَقُولُ: هُوَ يَرْمِي وَيَغْزُو، وَلَنْ يَرْمِيَ وَلَنْ يَغْزُوَ، وَلَمْ يَرْمِ وَلَمْ يَغْزُ.
text.en: The third: that rafʿ is by an implied ḍamma, naṣb by the fatḥa audibly and jazm by the dropping of the lām [of the root]. It belongs to the defective (nāqiṣ) with yāʾ and with wāw, when it is not dual, plural or [feminine] addressed; you say huwa yarmī “he throws” wa-yaghzū “and he raids”, wa-lan yarmiya wa-lan yaghzuwa and wa-lam yarmi wa-lam yaghzu.

text.original: وَالرَّابِعُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الرَّفْعُ بِتَقْدِيرِ الضَّمَّةِ، وَالنَّصْبُ بِتَقْدِيرِ الْفَتْحَةِ، وَالْجَزْمُ بِحَذْفِ اللَّامِ، وَيَخْتَصُّ بِالنَّاقِصِ الْأَلِفِيِّ غَيْرِ تَثْنِيَةٍ وَجَمْعٍ وَمُخَاطَبَةٍ، نَحْوُ: هُوَ يَسْعَى، وَلَنْ يَسْعَى، وَلَمْ يَسْعَ. فَصْلٌ: الْمَرْفُوعُ عَامِلُهُ مَعْنَوِيٌّ، وَهُوَ تَجَرُّدُهُ عَنِ النَّاصِبِ وَالْجَازِمِ، نَحْوُ: هُوَ يَضْرِبُ، وَيَغْزُو، وَيَرْمِي، وَيَسْعَى.
text.en: The fourth: that rafʿ is by an implied ḍamma, naṣb by an implied fatḥa and jazm by the dropping of the lām. It belongs to the defective with alif, when it is not dual, plural or [feminine] addressed, as huwa yasʿā “he strives”, wa-lan yasʿā and wa-lam yasʿa. Section. The marfūʿ [muḍāriʿ]: its governor is abstract, namely its being free of what puts it in naṣb and what puts it in jazm, as huwa yaḍribu “he hits”, wa-yaghzū, wa-yarmī and wa-yasʿā.

lessons.title: The muḍāriʿ in naṣb: an and its sisters; the implied an
body: The muḍāriʿ is put in naṣb by five particles: an, lan, kay, idhan, and an implied. Urīdu an tuḥsina ilayya, “I want you to do good to me”; anā lan aḍribaka; aslamtu kay adkhula al-jannata; idhan yaghfira Allāhu laka.

An is implied in seven places. After ḥattā: aslamtu ḥattā adkhula al-jannata. After the lām of kay: qāma Zaydun li-yadhhaba. After the lām of denial: mā kāna Allāhu li-yuʿadhdhibahum (Q 8:33). After the fāʾ in answer to six things: a command, aslim fa-taslama; a prohibition, lā taʿṣi fa-tuʿadhdhaba; a question, hal taʿlamu fa-tanjuwa; a negation, mā tazūrunā fa-nukrimaka; a wish, layta lī mālan fa-unfiqahu; an offer, alā tanzilu bi-nā fa-tuṣība khayran.

Then after the wāw in answer to the same six, aslim wa-taslama; after aw meaning “until” or “unless”, la-alzamannaka aw tuʿṭiyanī ḥaqqī; and after the wāw that joins the verb to a plain noun, aʿjabanī qiyāmuka wa-takhruja, where takhruja stands for “your going out”, joined to qiyāmuka. An may be spoken after the lām of kay, aslamtu li-an adkhula al-jannata, and after that wāw, wa-an takhruja; and it must be spoken when the lām of kay meets the lā of negation: li-allā yaʿlama (Q 57:29).

Not every an gives naṣb. After a verb of knowing, an is “the one lightened from the heavy anna”, and the verb after it stays in rafʿ: ʿalimtu an sa-yaqūmu; ʿalima an sa-yakūnu minkum marḍā (Q 73:20). After a verb of supposing both are allowed: naṣb, or the rafʿ of the lightened anna: ẓanantu an sa-yaqūmu. Knowing is certain, and anna is the particle of certainty; supposing lies between.

terms.en: the particles that put the muḍāriʿ in naṣb
an implied, after seven words
the lām of denial, after mā kāna
an lightened from anna, after a verb of knowing

examples.en: an expressed

tasks.answer: Kay, expressed. An implied after the lām of kay. An implied after the fāʾ in answer to a question.

tasks.prompt: Why is takhruja in naṣb in aʿjabanī qiyāmuka wa-takhruja?
tasks.answer: The wāw joins the verb to a plain noun, qiyāmuka; an is implied after it, and an with takhruja stands for the maṣdar khurūjuka, so a noun is joined to a noun.

tasks.prompt: When must an be spoken after the lām of kay?
tasks.answer: When the lām meets the lā of negation: li-allā yaʿlama. Otherwise it may be implied or spoken (li-yadhhaba, li-an adkhula).

tasks.prompt: Why is yakūnu in rafʿ in ʿalima an sa-yakūnu minkum marḍā?
tasks.answer: After a verb of knowing, an is anna lightened, not the an that gives naṣb, so the verb after it stays in rafʿ.

quiz.prompt: How many governors of naṣb does the book give?
quiz.explanation: An, lan, kay, idhan, and an implied.

quiz.prompt: In how many places is an implied?
quiz.explanation: Ḥattā, two lāms, fāʾ, wāw, aw, the joining wāw.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَنْصُوبُ عَامِلُهُ خَمْسَةُ أَحْرُفٍ: أَنْ، وَلَنْ، وَكَيْ، وَإِذَنْ، وَأَنِ الْمُقَدَّرَةُ، نَحْوُ: أُرِيدُ أَنْ تُحْسِنَ إِلَيَّ، وَأَنَا لَنْ أَضْرِبَكَ، وَأَسْلَمْتُ كَيْ أَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ، وَإِذَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكَ.
text.en: Section. The manṣūb [muḍāriʿ]: its governor is five particles: an, lan, kay, idhan and the implied an, as urīdu an tuḥsina ilayya “I want you to do good to me”, wa-anā lan aḍribaka “and I will not hit you”, wa-aslamtu kay adkhula al-jannata “and I became Muslim so that I may enter Paradise” and wa-idhan yaghfira Allāhu laka “and then God will forgive you”.

text.original: وَتُقَدَّرُ أَنْ فِي سَبْعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ: بَعْدَ حَتَّى، نَحْوُ: أَسْلَمْتُ حَتَّى أَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ، وَلَامِ كَيْ، نَحْوُ: قَامَ زَيْدٌ لِيَذْهَبَ، وَلَامِ الْجُحُودِ، نَحْوُ: مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ، وَالْفَاءِ الْوَاقِعَةِ فِي جَوَابِ الْأَمْرِ وَالنَّهْيِ وَالِاسْتِفْهَامِ وَالنَّفْيِ وَالتَّمَنِّي وَالْعَرْضِ، نَحْوُ: أَسْلِمْ فَتَسْلَمَ، وَلَا تَعْصِ فَتُعَذَّبَ، وَهَلْ تَعْلَمُ فَتَنْجُوَ، وَمَا تَزُورُنَا فَنُكْرِمَكَ، وَلَيْتَ لِي مَالًا فَأُنْفِقَهُ، وَأَلَا تَنْزِلُ بِنَا فَتُصِيبَ خَيْرًا.
text.en: An is implied in seven places: after ḥattā, as aslamtu ḥattā adkhula al-jannata “I became Muslim so that I may enter Paradise”; [after] the lām of kay, as qāma Zaydun li-yadhhaba “Zayd stood up to go”; the lām of denial (juḥūd), as mā kāna Allāhu li-yuʿadhdhibahum “God was not one to punish them”; and the fāʾ that stands in the answer to the command, the prohibition, the question, the negation, the wish and the offer, as aslim fa-taslama “become Muslim, and you will be safe”, wa-lā taʿṣi fa-tuʿadhdhaba “and do not disobey, lest you be punished”, wa-hal taʿlamu fa-tanjuwa “and do you know, so that you may be saved?”, wa-mā tazūrunā fa-nukrimaka “and you do not visit us, that we might honour you”, wa-layta lī mālan fa-unfiqahu “and would that I had wealth, that I might spend it” and wa-alā tanzilu bi-nā fa-tuṣība khayran “and will you not stay with us, and get some good?”.

text.original: وَبَعْدَ الْوَاوِ الْوَاقِعَةِ فِي جَوَابِ هَذِهِ الْمَوَاضِعِ كَذَلِكَ، نَحْوُ: أَسْلِمْ وَتَسْلَمَ، إِلَى آخِرِهِ، وَبَعْدَ أَوْ بِمَعْنَى إِلَى أَنْ أَوْ إِلَّا أَنْ، نَحْوُ: لَأَلْزَمَنَّكَ أَوْ تُعْطِيَنِي حَقِّي، وَوَاوِ الْعَطْفِ إِذَا كَانَ الْمَعْطُوفُ عَلَيْهِ اسْمًا صَرِيحًا، نَحْوُ: أَعْجَبَنِي قِيَامُكَ وَتَخْرُجَ.
text.en: [It is implied] after the wāw that stands in the answer of these places likewise, as aslim wa-taslama, to the end; after aw in the meaning of ilā an (until) or illā an (unless), as la-alzamannaka aw tuʿṭiyanī ḥaqqī “I shall surely stick to you until you give me my right”; and [after] the wāw of conjunction when what it is conjoined to is a plain noun, as aʿjabanī qiyāmuka wa-takhruja “your standing and your going out pleased me”.

text.original: وَيَجُوزُ إِظْهَارُ أَنْ مَعَ لَامِ كَيْ، نَحْوُ: أَسْلَمْتُ لِأَنْ أَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ، وَمَعَ وَاوِ الْعَطْفِ، نَحْوُ: أَعْجَبَنِي قِيَامُكَ وَأَنْ تَخْرُجَ، وَيَجِبُ إِظْهَارُهَا فِي لَامِ كَيْ إِذَا اتَّصَلَتْ بِلَا النَّافِيَةِ، نَحْوُ: لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ.
text.en: An may be expressed with the lām of kay, as aslamtu li-an adkhula al-jannata “I became Muslim in order to enter Paradise”, and with the wāw of conjunction, as aʿjabanī qiyāmuka wa-an takhruja; it must be expressed with the lām of kay when it is joined to the negating lā, as li-allā yaʿlama “so that he may not know”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ أَنِ الْوَاقِعَةَ بَعْدَ الْعِلْمِ لَيْسَتْ هِيَ النَّاصِبَةَ لِلْفِعْلِ الْمُضَارِعِ، وَإِنَّمَا هِيَ الْمُخَفَّفَةُ مِنَ الْمُثَقَّلَةِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ أَنْ سَيَقُومُ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضَى. وَأَنِ الْوَاقِعَةُ بَعْدَ الظَّنِّ جَازَ فِيهَا الْوَجْهَانِ: النَّصْبُ بِهَا، وَأَنْ تَجْعَلَهَا كَالْوَاقِعَةِ بَعْدَ الْعِلْمِ، نَحْوُ: ظَنَنْتُ أَنْ سَيَقُومُ.
text.en: Know that the an that stands after [a verb of] knowledge is not the one that puts the muḍāriʿ in naṣb; it is only the one lightened from the heavy [anna], as ʿalimtu an sa-yaqūmu “I knew that he would stand”; God Most High said: ʿalima an sa-yakūnu minkum marḍā “He knows that there will be sick ones among you”. As for the an that stands after [a verb of] supposing, both ways are allowed in it: naṣb by it, and treating it like the one that stands after knowledge, as ẓanantu an sa-yaqūmu “I thought that he would stand”.

lessons.title: The muḍāriʿ in jazm: lam, lammā, and the condition
body: The governors of jazm are lam, lammā, the lām of command, the lā of prohibition, and the words of requital (kalim al-mujāzāt): in, mahmā, idhmā, ḥaythumā, ayna, matā, mā, man, ayyun, annā, and in implied. Lam yaḍrib; lammā yaḍrib; wa-l-yaḍrib; lā taḍrib; in taḍrib aḍrib.

Lam “turns the muḍāriʿ into a negated past”, and so does lammā, “except that in it there is an expectation after it and a lasting before it”: qāma al-amīru wa-lammā yarkab, “the prince has stood and has not yet ridden”: he has not ridden up to now, and he is expected to. The verb may be dropped after lammā only: nadima Zaydun wa-lammā, “Zayd regretted, and not yet”, that is, wa-lammā yanfaʿhu al-nadamu; one does not say nadima Zaydun wa-lam.

The words of requital, “whether particle or noun”, come upon two sentences “to indicate that the first is the cause of the second”: the first is the condition (sharṭ), the second the requital (jazāʾ). If both are muḍāriʿ, both are in jazm in the wording: in tukrimnī ukrimka. If both are past, the governor shows nothing in the wording: in ḍarabta ḍarabtu, both in jazm only in their place.

If only the requital is past, the condition must be in jazm: in taḍribnī ḍarabtuka. If only the condition is past, the requital may be in jazm or not: in jiʾtanī ukrimka, or ukrimuka. The rule is easy to remember: a muḍāriʿ that comes first must show the jazm; one that comes after a past may or may not.

tasks.prompt: How do lam yarkab and lammā yarkab differ?
tasks.answer: Both turn the muḍāriʿ into a negated past. Lammā adds that the not-riding has lasted up to now and that the riding is expected: “has not yet ridden”. Lam only says “did not ride”.

tasks.prompt: Complete what is dropped in nadima Zaydun wa-lammā, and say why wa-lam is not allowed.
tasks.answer: Wa-lammā yanfaʿhu al-nadamu, “and regret has not yet profited him”. The verb may be dropped after lammā only, not after lam.

tasks.prompt: Show where the jazm is seen: in tukrimnī ukrimka; in ḍarabta ḍarabtu; in jiʾtanī ukrimka.
tasks.answer: In tukrimnī ukrimka: in both verbs, both being muḍāriʿ. In ḍarabta ḍarabtu: in neither; both are past and in jazm only in their place. In jiʾtanī ukrimka: in the requital only, which may also be said in rafʿ, ukrimuka, since the condition is past.

tasks.prompt: What do the words of requital indicate about the two sentences?
tasks.answer: That the first sentence, the condition, is the cause of the second, the requital.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْمَجْزُومُ عَامِلُهُ لَمْ، وَلَمَّا، وَلَامُ الْأَمْرِ، وَلَا فِي النَّهْيِ، وَكَلِمُ الْمُجَازَاةِ، وَهِيَ: إِنْ، وَمَهْمَا، وَإِذْمَا، وَحَيْثُمَا، وَأَيْنَ، وَمَتَى، وَمَا، وَمَنْ، وَأَيٌّ، وَأَنَّى، وَإِنِ الْمُقَدَّرَةُ، نَحْوُ: لَمْ يَضْرِبْ، وَلَمَّا يَضْرِبْ، وَلْيَضْرِبْ، وَلَا تَضْرِبْ، وَإِنْ تَضْرِبْ أَضْرِبْ، إِلَى آخِرِهِ.
text.en: Section. The majzūm [muḍāriʿ]: its governors are lam, lammā, the lām of command, lā in the prohibition, and the words of requital (kalim al-mujāzāt), which are in, mahmā, idhmā, ḥaythumā, ayna, matā, mā, man, ayyun and annā, and the implied in, as lam yaḍrib “he did not hit”, wa-lammā yaḍrib “and he has not yet hit”, wa-l-yaḍrib “and let him hit”, wa-lā taḍrib “and do not hit” and wa-in taḍrib aḍrib “and if you hit, I hit”, to the end.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ لَمْ تَقْلِبُ الْمُضَارِعَ مَاضِيًا مَنْفِيًّا، وَلَمَّا كَذَلِكَ، إِلَّا أَنَّ فِيهَا تَوَقُّعًا بَعْدَهُ وَدَوَامًا قَبْلَهُ، نَحْوُ: قَامَ الْأَمِيرُ وَلَمَّا يَرْكَبْ. وَيَجُوزُ حَذْفُ الْفِعْلِ بَعْدَ لَمَّا خَاصَّةً، تَقُولُ: نَدِمَ زَيْدٌ وَلَمَّا، أَيْ وَلَمَّا يَنْفَعْهُ النَّدَمُ، وَلَا تَقُولُ: نَدِمَ زَيْدٌ وَلَمْ.
text.en: Know that lam turns the muḍāriʿ into a negated past, and lammā likewise, except that in it there is an expectation after it and a lasting before it, as qāma al-amīru wa-lammā yarkab “the prince has stood up and has not yet ridden”. The verb may be dropped after lammā only; you say nadima Zaydun wa-lammā “Zayd regretted, and not yet”, that is, wa-lammā yanfaʿhu al-nadamu “and regret has not yet profited him”; and you do not say nadima Zaydun wa-lam.

text.original: وَأَمَّا كَلِمُ الْمُجَازَاةِ، حَرْفًا كَانَتْ أَوِ اسْمًا، فَهِيَ تَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْجُمْلَتَيْنِ لِتَدُلَّ عَلَى أَنَّ الْأُولَى سَبَبٌ لِلثَّانِيَةِ، وَتُسَمَّى الْأُولَى شَرْطًا، وَالثَّانِيَةُ جَزَاءً. ثُمَّ إِنْ كَانَ الشَّرْطُ وَالْجَزَاءُ مُضَارِعَيْنِ يَجِبُ الْجَزْمُ فِيهِمَا لَفْظًا، نَحْوُ: إِنْ تُكْرِمْنِي أُكْرِمْكَ، وَإِنْ كَانَا مَاضِيَيْنِ لَمْ يَعْمَلْ فِيهِمَا لَفْظًا، نَحْوُ: إِنْ ضَرَبْتَ ضَرَبْتُ.
text.en: As for the words of requital, whether particle or noun, they come upon two sentences to indicate that the first is the cause of the second; the first is called the condition (sharṭ) and the second the requital (jazāʾ). Then, if the condition and the requital are both muḍāriʿ, jazm in both is necessary in the wording, as in tukrimnī ukrimka “if you honour me, I honour you”; if both are past, it does not govern them in the wording, as in ḍarabta ḍarabtu “if you hit, I hit”.

text.original: وَإِنْ كَانَ الْجَزَاءُ وَحْدَهُ مَاضِيًا يَجِبُ الْجَزْمُ فِي الشَّرْطِ، نَحْوُ: إِنْ تَضْرِبْنِي ضَرَبْتُكَ، وَإِنْ كَانَ الشَّرْطُ وَحْدَهُ مَاضِيًا جَازَ فِي الْجَزَاءِ الْوَجْهَانِ، نَحْوُ: إِنْ جِئْتَنِي أُكْرِمْكَ.
text.en: If the requital alone is past, jazm is necessary in the condition, as in taḍribnī ḍarabtuka “if you hit me, I hit you”; if the condition alone is past, both ways are allowed in the requital, as in jiʾtanī ukrimka “if you come to me, I honour you”.

lessons.title: The fāʾ in the requital; in implied after a command
body: When the requital is a past verb without qad, the fāʾ is not allowed: in akramtanī akramtuka; wa-man dakhalahu kāna āminan (Q 3:97). When it is a muḍāriʿ, affirmed or negated with lā, both ways are allowed: in taḍribnī aḍribka, or fa-aḍribuka; in tashtimnī lā aḍribka, or fa-lā aḍribuka. With the fāʾ the verb is in rafʿ.

In every other case the fāʾ is necessary, in four kinds of requital. A past with qad: in yasriq fa-qad saraqa akhun lahu min qablu (Q 12:77). A muḍāriʿ negated by anything but lā: fa-lan yuqbala minhu (Q 3:85). A nominal sentence: man jāʾa bi-l-ḥasanati fa-lahu ʿashru amthālihā (Q 6:160). And a sentence of inshāʾ, a command, qul in kuntum tuḥibbūna Allāha fa-ttabiʿūnī (Q 3:31), or a prohibition, fa-in ʿalimtumūhunna muʾminātin fa-lā tarjiʿūhunna ilā al-kuffāri (Q 60:10). Idhā with a nominal sentence may take the fāʾ's place: wa-in tuṣibhum sayyiʾatun … idhā hum yaqnaṭūna (Q 30:36).

In is implied, and the second verb is in jazm, after five kinds of speech: a command, taʿallam tanju, “learn, and you will be saved”; a prohibition, lā takdhib yakun khayran laka; a question, hal tazūrunā nukrimka; a wish, laytaka ʿindī akhdumka; an offer, alā tanzilu bi-nā tuṣib khayran; and, the book adds, after negation in some places.

But only “when it is intended that the first is the cause of the second”: taʿallam tanju means in tataʿallam tanju. This gives a test anyone can use: put in before the first verb. So lā takfur tadkhuli al-nāra is not allowed, “because the causation is impossible”: in lā takfur tadkhuli al-nāra, “if you do not disbelieve, you will enter the Fire”, says nonsense.

tasks.prompt: Must, may or may not the requital take the fāʾ? in akramtanī akramtuka; in tashtimnī lā aḍribka; man jāʾa bi-l-ḥasanati lahu ʿashru amthālihā.
tasks.answer: In akramtanī akramtuka: may not (a past without qad). In tashtimnī lā aḍribka: may (a muḍāriʿ negated with lā; with the fāʾ, fa-lā aḍribuka). Man jāʾa … lahu ʿashru amthālihā: must, fa-lahu, since the requital is a nominal sentence.

tasks.prompt: Why is the fāʾ needed in in yasriq fa-qad saraqa akhun lahu min qablu?
tasks.arabic: إِنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ
tasks.answer: The requital is a past verb with qad, one of the four cases in which the fāʾ is necessary.

tasks.prompt: Give the in that is implied in hal tazūrunā nukrimka, and the iʿrāb of nukrimka.
tasks.answer: “Will you visit us? If you visit us, we will honour you”: the question stands for a condition. Nukrimka is the requital of the implied in, in jazm.

tasks.prompt: Apply the book's test to lā takdhib yakun khayran laka and lā takfur tadkhuli al-nāra.
tasks.answer: Put in before the first: in lā takdhib yakun khayran laka, “if you do not lie, it will be better for you”, makes sense, so the jazm is allowed. In lā takfur tadkhuli al-nāra, “if you do not disbelieve, you will enter the Fire”, is nonsense, so it is not allowed.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ إِذَا كَانَ الْجَزَاءُ مَاضِيًا بِغَيْرِ قَدْ لَمْ يَجُزِ الْفَاءُ فِيهِ، نَحْوُ: إِنْ أَكْرَمْتَنِي أَكْرَمْتُكَ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِنًا. وَإِنْ كَانَ مُضَارِعًا مُثْبَتًا أَوْ مَنْفِيًّا بِلَا جَازَ فِيهِ الْوَجْهَانِ، نَحْوُ: إِنْ تَضْرِبْنِي أَضْرِبْكَ، أَوْ فَأَضْرِبُكَ، وَإِنْ تَشْتِمْنِي لَا أَضْرِبْكَ، أَوْ فَلَا أَضْرِبُكَ.
text.en: Know that when the requital is a past without qad, the fāʾ is not allowed in it, as in akramtanī akramtuka “if you honour me, I honour you”; God Most High said: wa-man dakhalahu kāna āminan “and whoever enters it is safe”. If it is a muḍāriʿ, affirmed or negated with lā, both ways are allowed in it, as in taḍribnī aḍribka “if you hit me, I hit you” or fa-aḍribuka, and wa-in tashtimnī lā aḍribka “and if you insult me, I do not hit you” or fa-lā aḍribuka.

text.original: وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنِ الْجَزَاءُ أَحَدَ الْقِسْمَيْنِ الْمَذْكُورَيْنِ فَيَجِبُ الْفَاءُ فِيهِ، وَذَلِكَ فِي أَرْبَعِ صُوَرٍ: الْأُولَى أَنْ يَكُونَ الْجَزَاءُ مَاضِيًا مَعَ قَدْ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: إِنْ يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ، وَالثَّانِيَةُ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُضَارِعًا مَنْفِيًّا بِغَيْرِ لَا، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ، وَالثَّالِثَةُ أَنْ يَكُونَ جُمْلَةً اسْمِيَّةً، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا.
text.en: If the requital is not one of the two kinds mentioned, the fāʾ is necessary in it, and that is in four cases. The first: that the requital is a past with qad, as in His saying, exalted is He: in yasriq fa-qad saraqa akhun lahu min qablu “if he steals, a brother of his stole before”. The second: that it is a muḍāriʿ negated with other than lā, as in His saying, exalted is He: wa-man yabtaghi ghayra al-islāmi dīnan fa-lan yuqbala minhu “and whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him”. The third: that it is a nominal sentence, as in His saying, exalted is He: man jāʾa bi-al-ḥasanati fa-lahu ʿashru amthālihā “whoever brings a good deed, for him is ten times its like”.

text.original: وَالرَّابِعَةُ أَنْ يَكُونَ جُمْلَةً إِنْشَائِيَّةً، إِمَّا أَمْرًا، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: قُلْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي، وَإِمَّا نَهْيًا، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: فَإِنْ عَلِمْتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤْمِنَاتٍ فَلَا تَرْجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ. وَقَدْ يَقَعُ إِذَا مَعَ الْجُمْلَةِ الِاسْمِيَّةِ مَوْضِعَ الْفَاءِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ.
text.en: The fourth: that it is a sentence of utterance (inshāʾ), either a command, as in His saying, exalted is He: qul in kuntum tuḥibbūna Allāha fa-ittabiʿūnī “say: if you love God, follow me”, or a prohibition, as in His saying, exalted is He: fa-in ʿalimtumūhunna muʾminātin fa-lā tarjiʿūhunna ilā al-kuffāri “and if you know them to be believers, do not send them back to the unbelievers”. Idhā with a nominal sentence may stand in the place of the fāʾ, as in His saying, exalted is He: wa-in tuṣibhum sayyiʾatun bi-mā qaddamat aydīhim idhā hum yaqnaṭūna “and if an evil befalls them for what their hands have sent before, behold, they despair”.

text.original: وَإِنَّمَا تُقَدَّرُ إِنْ بَعْدَ الْأَفْعَالِ الْخَمْسَةِ الَّتِي هِيَ: الْأَمْرُ، نَحْوُ: تَعَلَّمْ تَنْجُ، وَالنَّهْيُ، نَحْوُ: لَا تَكْذِبْ يَكُنْ خَيْرًا لَكَ، وَالِاسْتِفْهَامُ، نَحْوُ: هَلْ تَزُورُنَا نُكْرِمْكَ، وَالتَّمَنِّي، نَحْوُ: لَيْتَكَ عِنْدِي أَخْدُمْكَ، وَالْعَرْضُ، نَحْوُ: أَلَا تَنْزِلُ بِنَا تُصِبْ خَيْرًا، وَبَعْدَ النَّفْيِ فِي بَعْضِ الْمَوَاضِعِ، نَحْوُ: لَا تَفْعَلْ شَرًّا يَكُنْ خَيْرًا لَكَ.
text.en: In is implied only after the five [kinds of] verbs, which are: the command, as taʿallam tanju “learn, [and] you will be saved”; the prohibition, as lā takdhib yakun khayran laka “do not lie, [and] it will be better for you”; the question, as hal tazūrunā nukrimka “will you visit us? [Then] we will honour you”; the wish, as laytaka ʿindī akhdumka “would that you were with me, [and] I would serve you”; and the offer, as alā tanzilu bi-nā tuṣib khayran “will you not stay with us? [Then] you will get some good”; and after negation in some places, as lā tafʿal sharran yakun khayran laka “do no evil, [and] it will be better for you”.

text.original: وَذَلِكَ إِذَا قُصِدَ أَنَّ الْأَوَّلَ سَبَبٌ لِلثَّانِي، كَمَا رَأَيْتَ فِي الْأَمْثِلَةِ؛ فَإِنَّ مَعْنَى قَوْلِنَا: تَعَلَّمْ تَنْجُ، هُوَ: إِنْ تَتَعَلَّمْ تَنْجُ، وَكَذَلِكَ الْبَوَاقِي. فَلِذَلِكَ امْتَنَعَ قَوْلُكَ: لَا تَكْفُرْ تَدْخُلِ النَّارَ؛ لِامْتِنَاعِ السَّبَبِيَّةِ، إِذْ لَا يَصِحُّ أَنْ يُقَالَ: إِنْ لَا تَكْفُرْ تَدْخُلِ النَّارَ.
text.en: That is when it is intended that the first is the cause of the second, as you have seen in the examples; for the meaning of our saying taʿallam tanju is in tataʿallam tanju “if you learn, you will be saved”, and likewise the rest. Therefore your saying lā takfur tadkhuli al-nāra “do not disbelieve, [and] you will enter the Fire” is not allowed, because the causation is impossible, since it cannot rightly be said in lā takfur tadkhuli al-nāra “if you do not disbelieve, you will enter the Fire”.

lessons.title: The imperative; the verb whose doer is not named
lessons.arabic: الْأَمْرُ وَفِعْلُ مَا لَمْ يُسَمَّ فَاعِلُهُ
lessons.transliteration: al-amr wa-fiʿl mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu
body: The imperative is “a form by which the act is sought from the fāʿil addressed”. It is made from the muḍāriʿ by dropping its prefix. If the letter after the prefix has a sukūn, a hamza of joining is put in front: with ḍamma if the third letter has ḍamma, unṣur; with kasra if it has fatḥa or kasra, iʿlam, iḍrib, istakhrij. If that letter is vowelled, no hamza is needed: ʿid, ḥāsib. The imperative of ifʿāl belongs to the second kind: from yukrimu, whose origin is yuʾakrimu, the hamza returns: akrim.

The imperative is “built on the sign of jazm”: on sukūn, iḍrib; on the dropping of the last letter, ughzu, irmi, isʿa; on the dropping of the nūn, iḍribā, iḍribū, iḍribī. Whatever the muḍāriʿ loses in jazm, the imperative lacks.

The verb whose doer is not named is “a verb whose fāʿil has been dropped and the mafʿūl put in its place”; it belongs only to the transitive. Its sign in the past is a ḍamma on the first letter and a kasra before the last, in the verbs with no hamza of joining and no added tāʾ: ḍuriba, duḥrija, ukrima. With an added tāʾ the first and second letters take ḍamma: tufuḍḍila, tuḍūriba. With a hamza of joining the first and third letters take ḍamma: ustukhrija, uqtudira; “the hamza follows the ḍamma” when it is spoken.

In the muḍāriʿ the sign is a ḍamma on the prefix and a fatḥa before the last letter: yuḍrabu, yustakhraju. But in mufāʿala, ifʿāl, tafʿīl, faʿlala and the forms attached to faʿlala, the prefix already has a ḍamma in the active, so the only sign is the fatḥa before the last: yuḥāsabu, yudaḥraju.

In the hollow verb the past is qīla, bīʿa; or with ishmām, a hint of ḍamma in the first letter; or with a wāw, qūla, būʿa. So too ikhtīra and inqīda, but not ustukhīra and uqīma, “because there is no fuʿila in them”. In the muḍāriʿ the middle letter becomes an alif: yuqālu, yubāʿu, “as you have learned in full in taṣrīf”.

terms.en: the imperative, made from the muḍāriʿ, built on the sign of jazm
the hamza of joining, before an unvowelled letter
the passive verb, its doer not named
a hint of ḍamma in the first letter of qīla

no hamza: the letter after the prefix is vowelled

tasks.prompt: Explain the hamza of each imperative: unṣur; iḍrib; ʿid.
tasks.answer: Unṣur: the letter after the prefix has a sukūn and the third letter a ḍamma (yanṣuru), so a hamza of joining with ḍamma. Iḍrib: the same, but the third letter has a kasra (yaḍribu), so a hamza with kasra. ʿId: the letter after the prefix is vowelled, so no hamza.

tasks.prompt: On what is each imperative built? iḍrib; irmi; iḍribū.
tasks.answer: Iḍrib: on sukūn. Irmi: on the dropping of the last letter. Iḍribū: on the dropping of the nūn. Each is built on what would be the sign of jazm in its muḍāriʿ.

tasks.prompt: Give the sign of the passive in ustukhrija and in yuḥāsabu.
tasks.answer: Ustukhrija: a verb with a hamza of joining, so the first and third letters take ḍamma and the letter before the last a kasra. Yuḥāsabu: a muḍāriʿ of mufāʿala, whose prefix has a ḍamma even in the active, so the sign is only the fatḥa before the last letter.

tasks.prompt: Which verbs have no passive, according to the book?
tasks.answer: The intransitive verbs: the passive belongs only to the transitive, since its mafʿūl must take the place of the dropped fāʿil.

text.original: وَالثَّالِثُ الْأَمْرُ، وَهُوَ صِيغَةٌ يُطْلَبُ بِهَا الْفِعْلُ مِنَ الْفَاعِلِ الْمُخَاطَبِ بِأَنْ تَحْذِفَ مِنَ الْمُضَارِعِ حَرْفَ الْمُضَارَعَةِ، ثُمَّ تَنْظُرَ: فَإِنْ كَانَ مَا بَعْدَ حَرْفِ الْمُضَارَعَةِ سَاكِنًا زِدْتَ هَمْزَةَ الْوَصْلِ مَضْمُومَةً إِنِ انْضَمَّ ثَالِثُهُ، نَحْوُ: انْصُرْ، وَمَكْسُورَةً إِنِ انْفَتَحَ أَوِ انْكَسَرَ، كَاعْلَمْ وَاضْرِبْ وَاسْتَخْرِجْ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مُتَحَرِّكًا فَلَا حَاجَةَ إِلَى الْهَمْزَةِ، نَحْوُ: عِدْ وَحَاسِبْ، وَالْأَمْرُ مِنْ بَابِ الْإِفْعَالِ مِنَ الْقِسْمِ الثَّانِي. وَهُوَ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى عَلَامَةِ الْجَزْمِ، كَاضْرِبْ، وَاغْزُ، وَارْمِ، وَاسْعَ، وَاضْرِبَا، وَاضْرِبُوا، وَاضْرِبِي.
text.en: The third is the imperative (amr): it is a form by which the act is sought from the fāʿil addressed, by your dropping the prefix of the muḍāriʿ from the muḍāriʿ; then you look: if what is after the prefix of the muḍāriʿ is unvowelled, you add a hamza of joining (hamzat al-waṣl), with ḍamma if its third letter has a ḍamma, as unṣur “help!”, and with kasra if it has a fatḥa or a kasra, as iʿlam “know!”, iḍrib “hit!” and istakhrij “bring out!”; and if it is vowelled, there is no need of the hamza, as ʿid “promise!” and ḥāsib “call to account!”; and the imperative of the bāb of ifʿāl belongs to the second kind. It is fixed on the sign of jazm, as iḍrib, ughzu “raid!”, irmi “throw!”, isʿa “strive!”, iḍribā “hit! (two)”, iḍribū “hit! (pl.)” and iḍribī “hit! (f.)”.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: فِعْلُ مَا لَمْ يُسَمَّ فَاعِلُهُ، هُوَ فِعْلٌ حُذِفَ فَاعِلُهُ وَأُقِيمَ الْمَفْعُولُ مَقَامَهُ، وَيَخْتَصُّ بِالْمُتَعَدِّي. وَعَلَامَتُهُ فِي الْمَاضِي أَنْ يَكُونَ أَوَّلُهُ مَضْمُومًا فَقَطْ وَمَا قَبْلَ آخِرِهِ مَكْسُورًا فِي الْأَبْوَابِ الَّتِي لَيْسَتْ فِي أَوَائِلِهَا هَمْزَةُ وَصْلٍ وَلَا تَاءٌ زَائِدَةٌ، نَحْوُ: ضُرِبَ، وَدُحْرِجَ، وَأُكْرِمَ.
text.en: Section. The verb whose doer is not named (fiʿl mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu): it is a verb whose fāʿil has been dropped and the mafʿūl put in its place; it belongs to the transitive verb. Its sign in the past is that its first letter only has a ḍamma and the letter before its last a kasra, in the bābs that have at their beginning no hamza of joining and no added tāʾ, as ḍuriba “he was hit”, duḥrija “he was rolled” and ukrima “he was honoured”.

text.original: وَأَنْ يَكُونَ أَوَّلُهُ وَثَانِيهِ مَضْمُومًا وَمَا قَبْلَ آخِرِهِ كَذَلِكَ فِيمَا فِي أَوَّلِهِ تَاءٌ زَائِدَةٌ، نَحْوُ: تُفُضِّلَ وَتُضُورِبَ، وَأَنْ يَكُونَ أَوَّلُهُ وَثَالِثُهُ مَضْمُومًا وَمَا قَبْلَ آخِرِهِ كَذَلِكَ فِيمَا فِي أَوَّلِهِ هَمْزَةُ وَصْلٍ، نَحْوُ: اسْتُخْرِجَ وَاقْتُدِرَ، وَالْهَمْزَةُ تَتْبَعُ الْمَضْمُومَ إِنْ لَمْ تُدْرَجْ.
text.en: And that its first and second letters have a ḍamma, and the letter before its last likewise [a kasra], in what has an added tāʾ at its beginning, as tufuḍḍila and tuḍūriba; and that its first and third letters have a ḍamma, and the letter before its last likewise, in what has a hamza of joining at its beginning, as ustukhrija and uqtudira; the hamza follows the [letter with] ḍamma if it is not passed over in joining.

text.original: وَفِي الْمُضَارِعِ أَنْ يَكُونَ حَرْفُ الْمُضَارَعَةِ مَضْمُومًا وَمَا قَبْلَ آخِرِهِ مَفْتُوحًا، نَحْوُ: يُضْرَبُ وَيُسْتَخْرَجُ، إِلَّا فِي بَابِ الْمُفَاعَلَةِ وَالْإِفْعَالِ وَالتَّفْعِيلِ وَالْفَعْلَلَةِ وَمُلْحَقَاتِهَا الثَّمَانِيَةِ؛ فَإِنَّ الْعَلَامَةَ فِيهَا فَتْحُ مَا قَبْلَ الْآخِرِ، نَحْوُ: يُحَاسَبُ وَيُدَحْرَجُ.
text.en: In the muḍāriʿ [its sign] is that the prefix of the muḍāriʿ has a ḍamma and the letter before its last a fatḥa, as yuḍrabu and yustakhraju, except in the bābs of mufāʿala, ifʿāl, tafʿīl and faʿlala and their eight attached forms; for in them the sign is the fatḥa of the letter before the last, as yuḥāsabu and yudaḥraju.

text.original: وَفِي الْأَجْوَفِ مَاضِيهِ: قِيلَ وَبِيعَ، وَبِالْإِشْمَامِ: قِيلَ وَبِيعَ، وَبِالْوَاوِ: قُولَ وَبُوعَ، وَكَذَلِكَ بَابُ اخْتِيرَ وَانْقِيدَ، دُونَ اسْتُخِيرَ وَأُقِيمَ؛ لِفَقْدِ فُعِلَ فِيهِمَا. وَفِي مُضَارِعِهِ تُقْلَبُ الْعَيْنُ أَلِفًا، نَحْوُ: يُقَالُ وَيُبَاعُ، كَمَا عَرَفْتَ فِي التَّصْرِيفِ مُسْتَقْصًى.
text.en: In the hollow (ajwaf) its past is qīla and bīʿa, and with ishmām (a hint of ḍamma) qīla and bīʿa, and with the wāw qūla and būʿa; likewise the bāb of ikhtīra and inqīda, but not ustukhīra and uqīma, because there is no fuʿila in them. In its muḍāriʿ the ʿayn is turned into an alif, as yuqālu and yubāʿu, as you have learned in full in taṣrīf.

lessons.title: Transitive and intransitive; three objects; the verbs of the heart
body: A verb is transitive when “the understanding of its meaning depends on something connected with it other than the fāʿil”: ḍaraba makes one ask whom. It is intransitive when not: qaʿada, qāma. A transitive verb may take one object, ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran; two, aʿṭā Zaydun ʿAmran dirhaman, where either may be left alone, aʿṭaytu Zaydan or aʿṭaytu dirhaman; or three: aʿlama Allāhu Zaydan ʿAmran fāḍilan, “God made Zayd know ʿAmr to be excellent”, and with it arā, anbaʾa, nabbaʾa, akhbara, khabbara and ḥaddatha.

In these seven the first object behaves like the objects of aʿṭaytu and may stand alone, aʿlama Allāhu Zaydan; but the second and third are like the objects of ʿalimtu and may not be separated: not aʿlamtu Zaydan khayra al-nāsi, but aʿlamtu Zaydan ʿAmran khayra al-nāsi. The reason is that the second and third were in origin a mubtadaʾ and its khabar.

The verbs of the heart are ʿalimtu, ẓanantu, ḥasibtu, khiltu, raʾaytu, wajadtu and zaʿamtu. They come upon the mubtadaʾ and khabar and put both in naṣb as objects: ʿalimtu Zaydan ʿāliman. Their properties: first, neither object may be left alone, so not ʿalimtu Zaydan. Second, their work may be cancelled (ilghāʾ) when they stand in the middle, Zaydun ẓanantu qāʾimun, or at the end, Zaydun qāʾimun ẓanantu.

Third, they are suspended (tuʿallaq) before a question, ʿalimtu a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun; a negation, ʿalimtu mā Zaydun fī al-dāri; or the lām of ibtidāʾ, ʿalimtu la-Zaydun munṭaliqun. The commentators tell the two apart: cancelling is a choice, and the verb gives up its work in wording and meaning; suspending is required, and the verb gives up its work in the wording only, the sentence being still its object in its place.

Fourth, their fāʿil and object may be two pronouns of one person: ʿalimtunī munṭaliqan, “I knew myself departing”, ẓanantuka fāḍilan. And with other meanings they take one object and are not verbs of the heart: ẓanantu for “I suspected”, ʿalimtu for “I recognised”, raʾaytu for “I saw”, wajadtu for “I found the lost camel”.

the verbs of the heart, with two objects from a mubtadaʾ and khabar
cancelling their work, when they come in the middle or at the end
suspending their work before a question, a negation or the lām

tasks.prompt: May one object be left alone? aʿṭaytu Zaydan; ʿalimtu Zaydan; aʿlama Allāhu Zaydan; aʿlamtu Zaydan khayra al-nāsi.
tasks.answer: Aʿṭaytu Zaydan: yes, the objects of aʿṭā may be left alone. ʿAlimtu Zaydan: no, a verb of the heart needs both. Aʿlama Allāhu Zaydan: yes, the first object of aʿlama is like those of aʿṭā. Aʿlamtu Zaydan khayra al-nāsi: no, the second and third are like the objects of ʿalimtu; one must say aʿlamtu Zaydan ʿAmran khayra al-nāsi.

tasks.prompt: Parse Zaydun qāʾimun ẓanantu and ʿalimtu mā Zaydun fī al-dāri.
tasks.arabic: زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ ظَنَنْتُ — عَلِمْتُ مَا زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ
tasks.answer: In the first, ẓanantu comes at the end and its work is cancelled: Zaydun qāʾimun is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in rafʿ. In the second, ʿalimtu is suspended by the negation mā: it does not work on the words, but the sentence mā Zaydun fī al-dāri is its object in its place.

tasks.prompt: How does cancelling differ from suspending, according to the commentators?
tasks.answer: Cancelling is allowed, not required, when the verb comes in the middle or at the end, and the verb loses its work in wording and in meaning. Suspending is required before a question, a negation or the lām, and the verb loses its work only in the wording; the sentence after it is its object in its place.

tasks.prompt: Is raʾaytu a verb of the heart in raʾaytu Zaydan, “I saw Zayd”?
tasks.answer: No. In the sense of abṣartu, “I saw with the eye”, it takes one object only and is not a verb of the heart.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْفِعْلُ إِمَّا مُتَعَدٍّ، وَهُوَ مَا يَتَوَقَّفُ فَهْمُ مَعْنَاهُ عَلَى مُتَعَلِّقٍ غَيْرِ الْفَاعِلِ، كَضَرَبَ، وَإِمَّا لَازِمٌ، وَهُوَ بِخِلَافِهِ، كَقَعَدَ وَقَامَ. وَالْمُتَعَدِّي قَدْ يَكُونُ إِلَى مَفْعُولٍ وَاحِدٍ، كَضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا، وَإِلَى مَفْعُولَيْنِ، كَأَعْطَى زَيْدٌ عَمْرًا دِرْهَمًا، وَيَجُوزُ فِيهِ الِاقْتِصَارُ عَلَى أَحَدِ مَفْعُولَيْهِ، كَأَعْطَيْتُ زَيْدًا، أَوْ دِرْهَمًا، بِخِلَافِ بَابِ عَلِمْتُ.
text.en: Section. The verb is either transitive (mutaʿaddī), which is one the understanding of whose meaning depends on something connected with it other than the fāʿil, as ḍaraba “he hit”, or intransitive (lāzim), which is the opposite, as qaʿada “he sat” and qāma “he stood”. The transitive may be to one mafʿūl, as ḍaraba Zaydun ʿAmran “Zayd hit ʿAmr”, and to two mafʿūls, as aʿṭā Zaydun ʿAmran dirhaman “Zayd gave ʿAmr a dirham” — and in this one of its two mafʿūls may be left alone, as aʿṭaytu Zaydan “I gave Zayd” or dirhaman “a dirham”, unlike the bāb of ʿalimtu —,

text.original: وَإِلَى ثَلَاثَةِ مَفَاعِيلَ، نَحْوُ: أَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ زَيْدًا عَمْرًا فَاضِلًا، وَمِنْهُ: أَرَى، وَأَنْبَأَ، وَنَبَّأَ، وَأَخْبَرَ، وَخَبَّرَ، وَحَدَّثَ. وَهَذِهِ السَّبْعَةُ مَفْعُولُهَا الْأَوَّلُ مَعَ الْأَخِيرَيْنِ كَمَفْعُولَيْ أَعْطَيْتُ فِي جَوَازِ الِاقْتِصَارِ عَلَى أَحَدِهِمَا، تَقُولُ: أَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ زَيْدًا، وَالثَّانِي مَعَ الثَّالِثِ كَمَفْعُولَيْ عَلِمْتُ فِي عَدَمِ جَوَازِ الِاقْتِصَارِ عَلَى أَحَدِهِمَا، فَلَا تَقُولُ: أَعْلَمْتُ زَيْدًا خَيْرَ النَّاسِ، بَلْ تَقُولُ: أَعْلَمْتُ زَيْدًا عَمْرًا خَيْرَ النَّاسِ.
text.en: and to three mafʿūls, as aʿlama Allāhu Zaydan ʿAmran fāḍilan “God made Zayd know ʿAmr to be excellent”; and of this kind are arā, anbaʾa, nabbaʾa, akhbara, khabbara and ḥaddatha. In these seven the first mafʿūl with the last two is like the two mafʿūls of aʿṭaytu, in that one of them may be left alone — you say aʿlama Allāhu Zaydan —, and the second with the third is like the two mafʿūls of ʿalimtu, in that neither may be left alone; so you do not say aʿlamtu Zaydan khayra al-nāsi, but you say aʿlamtu Zaydan ʿAmran khayra al-nāsi “I made Zayd know ʿAmr to be the best of people”.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: أَفْعَالُ الْقُلُوبِ: عَلِمْتُ، وَظَنَنْتُ، وَحَسِبْتُ، وَخِلْتُ، وَرَأَيْتُ، وَوَجَدْتُ، وَزَعَمْتُ، وَهِيَ أَفْعَالٌ تَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ فَتَنْصِبُهُمَا عَلَى الْمَفْعُولِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ زَيْدًا عَالِمًا. وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ لِهَذِهِ الْأَفْعَالِ خَوَاصَّ: مِنْهَا أَنْ لَا يُقْتَصَرَ عَلَى أَحَدِ مَفْعُولَيْهَا، بِخِلَافِ بَابِ أَعْطَيْتُ، فَلَا تَقُولُ: عَلِمْتُ زَيْدًا.
text.en: Section. The verbs of the heart (afʿāl al-qulūb) are ʿalimtu “I knew”, ẓanantu “I thought”, ḥasibtu “I reckoned”, khiltu “I fancied”, raʾaytu “I deemed”, wajadtu “I found” and zaʿamtu “I claimed”. They are verbs that come upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar and put both in naṣb as mafʿūls, as ʿalimtu Zaydan ʿāliman “I knew Zayd to be learned”. Know that these verbs have properties. Among them: that one of their two mafʿūls may not be left alone, unlike the bāb of aʿṭaytu; so you do not say ʿalimtu Zaydan.

text.original: وَمِنْهَا جَوَازُ الْإِلْغَاءِ إِذَا تَوَسَّطَتْ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ ظَنَنْتُ قَائِمٌ، أَوْ تَأَخَّرَتْ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ ظَنَنْتُ. وَمِنْهَا أَنَّهَا تُعَلَّقُ إِذَا وَقَعَتْ قَبْلَ الِاسْتِفْهَامِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ أَزَيْدٌ عِنْدَكَ أَمْ عَمْرٌو، وَقَبْلَ النَّفْيِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ مَا زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ، وَقَبْلَ لَامِ الِابْتِدَاءِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُ لَزَيْدٌ مُنْطَلِقٌ.
text.en: Among them: that cancelling (ilghāʾ) [their governing] is allowed when they stand in the middle, as Zaydun ẓanantu qāʾimun “Zayd, I thought, is standing”, or at the end, as Zaydun qāʾimun ẓanantu “Zayd is standing, I thought”. Among them: that they are suspended (tuʿallaq) when they stand before a question, as ʿalimtu a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun “I knew whether Zayd or ʿAmr is with you”; before a negation, as ʿalimtu mā Zaydun fī al-dāri “I knew that Zayd is not in the house”; and before the lām of ibtidāʾ, as ʿalimtu la-Zaydun munṭaliqun “I knew that Zayd is surely departing”.

text.original: وَمِنْهَا أَنَّهُ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَكُونَ فَاعِلُهَا وَمَفْعُولُهَا ضَمِيرَيْنِ لِشَيْءٍ وَاحِدٍ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتُنِي مُنْطَلِقًا، وَظَنَنْتُكَ فَاضِلًا. وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ قَدْ يَكُونُ ظَنَنْتُ بِمَعْنَى اتَّهَمْتُ، وَعَلِمْتُ بِمَعْنَى عَرَفْتُ، وَرَأَيْتُ بِمَعْنَى أَبْصَرْتُ، وَوَجَدْتُ بِمَعْنَى أَصَبْتُ الضَّالَّةَ، فَتَنْصِبُ مَفْعُولًا وَاحِدًا فَقَطْ، وَلَا تَكُونُ حِينَئِذٍ مِنْ أَفْعَالِ الْقُلُوبِ.
text.en: Among them: that their fāʿil and their mafʿūl may be two pronouns of one thing, as ʿalimtunī munṭaliqan “I knew myself to be departing” and wa-ẓanantuka fāḍilan “and I thought you excellent”. Know that ẓanantu may be in the meaning of ittahamtu “I suspected”, ʿalimtu in the meaning of ʿaraftu “I recognised”, raʾaytu in the meaning of abṣartu “I saw”, and wajadtu in the meaning of aṣabtu al-ḍāllata “I found the lost [animal]”; then they put one mafʿūl only in naṣb, and they are not then among the verbs of the heart.

lessons.title: The incomplete verbs: kāna and its sisters
body: The incomplete verbs are “laid down to settle the fāʿil in a quality other than the quality of their maṣdar”. Kāna Zaydun qāʾiman does not say that Zayd did any “being”; it settles him in standing, in past time. They come upon the nominal sentence “to give its attribution the force of their meaning”, raising the first and putting the second in naṣb (lesson 15).

Kāna is of three kinds. Incomplete, telling that its khabar held of its subject in the past, either lastingly, kāna Allāhu ʿalīman ḥakīman, “God is All-Knowing, Wise”, where the past does not mean that it ended, or for a time, kāna Zaydun shābban, “Zayd was a youth”. Complete, meaning “it took place”: kāna al-qitālu. And additional, which can be dropped without changing the meaning: ʿalā kāna al-musawwamati al-ʿirābi, “above the branded Arabian horses”, “that is, ʿalā al-musawwamati”.

Ṣāra is for passing into a state: ṣāra Zaydun ghaniyyan. Aṣbaḥa, amsā and aḍḥā join the content of the sentence to the morning, the evening and the forenoon: aṣbaḥa Zaydun dhākiran, “Zayd was remembering [God] in the morning”; they also mean ṣāra, aṣbaḥa Zaydun ghaniyyan, “Zayd became rich”; and they may be complete, “entering the morning”. Ẓalla and bāta do the same for the day and the night: ẓalla Zaydun kātiban, “Zayd spent the day writing”; and they too may mean ṣāra.

Mā zāla, mā fatiʾa, mā bariḥa and mā infakka tell that the khabar goes on holding of the subject: mā zāla Zaydun amīran, “Zayd has not ceased to be prince”; “the particle of negation is bound to them”, for the negation of ceasing is lasting. Mā dāma times one thing by the time another lasts: aqūmu mā dāma al-amīru jālisan, “I stand as long as the prince is sitting”. Laysa negates the sentence in the present, “and it is said, absolutely”.

the complete kāna: “it took place”, with no khabar
the additional kāna, dropped without change of meaning
going on: the meaning of mā zāla and its sisters

tasks.prompt: Which kāna is it? kāna Zaydun shābban; kāna al-qitālu; ʿalā kāna al-musawwamati.
tasks.answer: Kāna Zaydun shābban: incomplete, with ism and khabar, for a time in the past. Kāna al-qitālu: complete, “the fighting took place”, with a fāʿil and no khabar. ʿAlā kāna al-musawwamati: additional, since dropping it leaves ʿalā al-musawwamati with the same meaning.

tasks.prompt: Why does kāna Allāhu ʿalīman ḥakīman not mean that God's knowledge has ended?
tasks.answer: Kāna tells that the khabar held of its subject in the past, either lastingly or for a time. Here it is lasting: the past is told without any end to it.

tasks.prompt: Give the two meanings of aṣbaḥa in the book's examples.
tasks.answer: In aṣbaḥa Zaydun dhākiran it joins the content to the morning: Zayd was remembering in the morning. In aṣbaḥa Zaydun ghaniyyan it means ṣāra: Zayd became rich.

tasks.prompt: Why must mā zāla always have its negation?
tasks.answer: Zāla means “ceased”; it is the negation of ceasing that gives the meaning of going on. Without mā, the verb would say the opposite.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْأَفْعَالُ النَّاقِصَةُ هِيَ أَفْعَالٌ وُضِعَتْ لِتَقْرِيرِ الْفَاعِلِ عَلَى صِفَةٍ غَيْرِ صِفَةِ مَصْدَرِهَا، وَهِيَ: كَانَ، وَصَارَ، وَظَلَّ، وَبَاتَ، إِلَى آخِرِهَا. تَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْجُمْلَةِ الِاسْمِيَّةِ لِإِفَادَةِ نِسْبَتِهَا حُكْمَ مَعْنَاهَا، تَرْفَعُ الْأَوَّلَ وَتَنْصِبُ الثَّانِيَ، فَتَقُولُ: كَانَ زَيْدٌ قَائِمًا.
text.en: Section. The incomplete verbs (al-afʿāl al-nāqiṣa) are verbs laid down to settle the fāʿil in a quality other than the quality of their maṣdar. They are kāna, ṣāra, ẓalla, bāta, to the end of them. They come upon the nominal sentence to give its attribution the force of their meaning; they put the first in rafʿ and the second in naṣb; so you say kāna Zaydun qāʾiman “Zayd was standing”.

text.original: وَكَانَ عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ أَقْسَامٍ: نَاقِصَةٌ، وَهِيَ تَدُلُّ عَلَى ثُبُوتِ خَبَرِهَا لِفَاعِلِهَا فِي الْمَاضِي، إِمَّا دَائِمًا، نَحْوُ: كَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا، أَوْ مُنْقَطِعًا، نَحْوُ: كَانَ زَيْدٌ شَابًّا؛ وَتَامَّةٌ بِمَعْنَى ثَبَتَ وَحَصَلَ، نَحْوُ: كَانَ الْقِتَالُ، أَيْ حَصَلَ الْقِتَالُ؛ وَزَائِدَةٌ لَا يَتَغَيَّرُ بِإِسْقَاطِهَا مَعْنَى الْجُمْلَةِ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ، شِعْرٌ: جِيَادُ بَنِي أَبِي بَكْرٍ تَسَامَى * عَلَى كَانَ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ الْعِرَابِ، أَيْ عَلَى الْمُسَوَّمَةِ.
text.en: Kāna is of three kinds. Incomplete (nāqiṣa), which indicates that its khabar holds of its fāʿil in the past, either lastingly, as kāna Allāhu ʿalīman ḥakīman “God is All-Knowing, Wise”, or interrupted, as kāna Zaydun shābban “Zayd was a youth”. Complete (tāmma), in the meaning of thabata and ḥaṣala “it took place”, as kāna al-qitālu “the fighting took place”, that is, ḥaṣala al-qitālu. And additional (zāʾida), by whose dropping the meaning of the sentence does not change, as in the poet's saying, verse: jiyādu banī Abī Bakrin tasāmā / ʿalā kāna al-musawwamati al-ʿirābi “The steeds of the Banū Abī Bakr rise high / above the branded Arabian [horses]”, that is, ʿalā al-musawwamati.

text.original: وَصَارَ لِلِانْتِقَالِ، نَحْوُ: صَارَ زَيْدٌ غَنِيًّا. وَأَصْبَحَ وَأَمْسَى وَأَضْحَى تَدُلُّ عَلَى اقْتِرَانِ مَضْمُونِ الْجُمْلَةِ بِتِلْكَ الْأَوْقَاتِ، نَحْوُ: أَصْبَحَ زَيْدٌ ذَاكِرًا، أَيْ كَانَ ذَاكِرًا فِي وَقْتِ الصُّبْحِ، وَبِمَعْنَى صَارَ، نَحْوُ: أَصْبَحَ زَيْدٌ غَنِيًّا، وَتَامَّةٌ بِمَعْنَى دَخَلَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَالضُّحَى وَالْمَسَاءِ.
text.en: Ṣāra is for passing [into a state], as ṣāra Zaydun ghaniyyan “Zayd became rich”. Aṣbaḥa, amsā and aḍḥā indicate that the content of the sentence is joined with those times, as aṣbaḥa Zaydun dhākiran “Zayd was remembering [God] in the morning”, that is, kāna dhākiran fī waqti al-ṣubḥi “he was remembering at the time of morning”; [they come] in the meaning of ṣāra, as aṣbaḥa Zaydun ghaniyyan “Zayd became rich”; and complete, in the meaning of entering the morning, the forenoon and the evening.

text.original: وَظَلَّ وَبَاتَ يَدُلَّانِ عَلَى اقْتِرَانِ مَضْمُونِ الْجُمْلَةِ بِوَقْتَيْهِمَا، نَحْوُ: ظَلَّ زَيْدٌ كَاتِبًا، وَبِمَعْنَى صَارَ. وَمَا زَالَ، وَمَا فَتِئَ، وَمَا بَرِحَ، وَمَا انْفَكَّ تَدُلُّ عَلَى اسْتِمْرَارِ ثُبُوتِ خَبَرِهَا لِفَاعِلِهَا مُذْ قَبِلَهُ، نَحْوُ: مَا زَالَ زَيْدٌ أَمِيرًا، وَيَلْزَمُهَا حَرْفُ النَّفْيِ.
text.en: Ẓalla and bāta indicate that the content of the sentence is joined with their two times, as ẓalla Zaydun kātiban “Zayd spent the day writing”, and [they come] in the meaning of ṣāra. Mā zāla, mā fatiʾa, mā bariḥa and mā infakka indicate that their khabar goes on holding of their fāʿil since it received it, as mā zāla Zaydun amīran “Zayd has not ceased to be prince”; the particle of negation is bound to them.

text.original: وَمَا دَامَ يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَوْقِيتِ أَمْرٍ بِمُدَّةِ ثُبُوتِ خَبَرِهَا لِفَاعِلِهَا، نَحْوُ: أَقُومُ مَا دَامَ الْأَمِيرُ جَالِسًا. وَلَيْسَ يَدُلُّ عَلَى نَفْيِ مَعْنَى الْجُمْلَةِ حَالًا، وَقِيلَ مُطْلَقًا. وَقَدْ عَرَفْتَ بَقِيَّةَ أَحْكَامِهَا فِي الْقِسْمِ الْأَوَّلِ، فَلَا نُعِيدُهَا.
text.en: Mā dāma indicates the timing of a matter by the period in which its khabar holds of its fāʿil, as aqūmu mā dāma al-amīru jālisan “I stand as long as the prince is sitting”. Laysa indicates the negation of the meaning of the sentence in the present; and it is said, absolutely. You have learned the rest of their rules in the first part, so we do not repeat them.

lessons.title: The verbs of nearness; the verbs of wonder
body: The verbs of nearness indicate “the nearness of the khabar to their fāʿil”, in three kinds. For hope: ʿasā, a rigid verb used only in the past. It works like kāda, but its khabar is a muḍāriʿ with an: ʿasā Zaydun an yaqūma, “perhaps Zayd will stand”. The khabar may come before the ism, ʿasā an yaqūma Zaydun, and an is sometimes dropped, ʿasā Zaydun yaqūmu.

For coming about: kāda, whose khabar is a muḍāriʿ without an, kāda Zaydun yaqūmu, “Zayd was about to stand”, though an sometimes comes in, kāda Zaydun an yaqūma. For taking up and beginning: ṭafiqa, jaʿala, karaba and akhadha, used like kāda: ṭafiqa Zaydun yaktubu, “Zayd began to write”. And awshaka is used like both ʿasā and kāda. Why the an with ʿasā and not with kāda? The commentators answer from the meaning: ʿasā looks to the future, which an gives; kāda tells of something on the point of happening now.

The verbs of wonder are “laid down to express wonder”, in two forms. Mā afʿalahu: mā aḥsana Zaydan, “how beautiful Zayd is!”, “that is, ayyu shayʾin aḥsana Zaydan”, what has made Zayd beautiful?, with a pronoun in aḥsana as its fāʿil. And afʿil bihi: aḥsin bi-Zaydin. They are built only from verbs from which the elative can be built (lesson 46).

For the others one uses a helping verb: mā ashadda istikhrājahu, ashdid bi-istikhrājihi. The two forms are fixed phrases: “no free handling is allowed in them”, no putting a word before or after, and nothing between. Al-Māzinī alone allowed an adverb between: mā aḥsana al-yawma Zaydan.

a rigid verb, used in one form only, as ʿasā
wonder: mā afʿalahu and afʿil bihi
the verbs of beginning: ṭafiqa, jaʿala, karaba, akhadha

tasks.prompt: Correct or explain: ʿasā Zaydun yaqūmu; kāda Zaydun an yaqūma.
tasks.arabic: عَسَى زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ — كَادَ زَيْدٌ أَنْ يَقُومَ
tasks.answer: Both are allowed, but less usual. The khabar of ʿasā is normally a muḍāriʿ with an (ʿasā Zaydun an yaqūma), and an is sometimes dropped. The khabar of kāda is normally without an (kāda Zaydun yaqūmu), and an sometimes comes in.

tasks.prompt: Parse mā aḥsana Zaydan as the book explains it.
tasks.answer: Mā means “what thing”: ayyu shayʾin. Aḥsana is a past verb whose fāʿil is a pronoun hidden in it, going back to mā; Zaydan is its object: “what thing has made Zayd beautiful?”.

tasks.prompt: How does one express wonder at a verb of more than three letters, such as istakhraja?
tasks.answer: Through a helping verb from a bare triliteral, with the maṣdar after it: mā ashadda istikhrājahu, or ashdid bi-istikhrājihi.

tasks.prompt: Is mā aḥsana al-yawma Zaydan allowed?
tasks.answer: Not for most grammarians, since nothing may come between the parts of the form of wonder; al-Māzinī allowed an adverb, as al-yawma, to come between.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: أَفْعَالُ الْمُقَارَبَةِ هِيَ أَفْعَالٌ وُضِعَتْ لِلدَّلَالَةِ عَلَى دُنُوِّ الْخَبَرِ لِفَاعِلِهَا، وَهِيَ ثَلَاثَةُ أَقْسَامٍ: الْأَوَّلُ لِلرَّجَاءِ، وَهُوَ عَسَى، وَهُوَ فِعْلٌ جَامِدٌ لَا يُسْتَعْمَلُ مِنْهُ غَيْرُ الْمَاضِي، وَهُوَ فِي الْعَمَلِ مِثْلُ كَادَ، إِلَّا أَنَّ خَبَرَهُ فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَعَ أَنْ، نَحْوُ: عَسَى زَيْدٌ أَنْ يَقُومَ، وَيَجُوزُ تَقْدِيمُ الْخَبَرِ عَلَى اسْمِهِ، نَحْوُ: عَسَى أَنْ يَقُومَ زَيْدٌ، وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ أَنْ، نَحْوُ: عَسَى زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ.
text.en: Section. The verbs of nearness (afʿāl al-muqāraba) are verbs laid down to indicate the nearness of the khabar to their fāʿil. They are of three kinds. The first is for hope, and it is ʿasā; it is a rigid (jāmid) verb of which nothing but the past is used. In governing it is like kāda, except that its khabar is a muḍāriʿ verb with an, as ʿasā Zaydun an yaqūma “perhaps Zayd will stand”; its khabar may be put before its ism, as ʿasā an yaqūma Zaydun; and an is sometimes dropped, as ʿasā Zaydun yaqūmu.

text.original: وَالثَّانِي لِلْحُصُولِ، وَهُوَ كَادَ، وَخَبَرُهُ مُضَارِعٌ دُونَ أَنْ، نَحْوُ: كَادَ زَيْدٌ يَقُومُ، وَقَدْ تَدْخُلُ أَنْ، نَحْوُ: كَادَ زَيْدٌ أَنْ يَقُومَ. وَالثَّالِثُ لِلْأَخْذِ وَالشُّرُوعِ فِي الْفِعْلِ، وَهُوَ طَفِقَ، وَجَعَلَ، وَكَرَبَ، وَأَخَذَ، وَاسْتِعْمَالُهَا مِثْلُ كَادَ، نَحْوُ: طَفِقَ زَيْدٌ يَكْتُبُ. وَأَوْشَكَ، وَاسْتِعْمَالُهَا مِثْلُ عَسَى وَكَادَ.
text.en: The second is for coming about, and it is kāda; its khabar is a muḍāriʿ without an, as kāda Zaydun yaqūmu “Zayd was about to stand”, and an sometimes comes in, as kāda Zaydun an yaqūma. The third is for taking up and beginning the act: it is ṭafiqa, jaʿala, karaba and akhadha, and their use is like kāda, as ṭafiqa Zaydun yaktubu “Zayd began to write”. And awshaka: its use is like ʿasā and kāda.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: فِعْلَا التَّعَجُّبِ مَا وُضِعَ لِإِنْشَاءِ التَّعَجُّبِ، وَلَهُ صِيغَتَانِ: مَا أَفْعَلَهُ، نَحْوُ: مَا أَحْسَنَ زَيْدًا، أَيْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَحْسَنَ زَيْدًا، وَفِي أَحْسَنَ ضَمِيرٌ، وَهُوَ فَاعِلُهُ؛ وَأَفْعِلْ بِهِ، نَحْوُ: أَحْسِنْ بِزَيْدٍ. وَلَا يُبْنَيَانِ إِلَّا مِمَّا يُبْنَى مِنْهُ أَفْعَلُ التَّفْضِيلِ.
text.en: Section. The two verbs of wonder (fiʿlā al-taʿajjub): what is laid down to express wonder. It has two forms. mā afʿalahu, as mā aḥsana Zaydan “how beautiful Zayd is!”, that is, ayyu shayʾin aḥsana Zaydan “what thing has made Zayd beautiful?”; in aḥsana there is a pronoun, which is its fāʿil. And afʿil bi-hi, as aḥsin bi-Zaydin “how beautiful Zayd is!”. They are built only from that from which the afʿal of tafḍīl is built.

text.original: وَيُتَوَصَّلُ فِي الْمُمْتَنِعِ بِمِثْلِ: مَا أَشَدَّ اسْتِخْرَاجَهُ فِي الْأَوَّلِ، وَأَشْدِدْ بِاسْتِخْرَاجِهِ فِي الثَّانِي، كَمَا عَرَفْتَ فِي اسْمِ التَّفْضِيلِ. وَلَا يَجُوزُ التَّصَرُّفُ فِيهِمَا بِتَقْدِيمٍ وَلَا تَأْخِيرٍ وَلَا فَصْلٍ، وَالْمَازِنِيُّ أَجَازَ الْفَصْلَ بِالظَّرْفِ، نَحْوُ: مَا أَحْسَنَ الْيَوْمَ زَيْدًا.
text.en: In what is impossible one reaches [the meaning] by such [phrases] as mā ashadda istikhrājahu “how strong is his bringing out!” in the first and ashdid bi-istikhrājihi in the second, as you have learned in the elative. No free handling is allowed in them, by putting before or after or by separating; al-Māzinī allowed separating by an adverb, as mā aḥsana al-yawma Zaydan “how beautiful Zayd is today!”.

lessons.title: The verbs of praise and blame
body: The verbs of praise and blame are “laid down to express praise or blame”. Praise has two. Niʿma: its fāʿil is a noun with the lām, niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun, “how excellent a man is Zayd!”, or muḍāf to one with the lām, niʿma ghulāmu al-rajuli Zaydun. Its fāʿil may be a hidden pronoun, and then a tamyīz must explain it, an indefinite in naṣb, niʿma rajulan Zaydun, or mā, fa-niʿimmā hiya (Q 2:271), “that is, niʿma shayʾan hiya”.

Zayd in these sentences “is called the one singled out for praise” (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ). The commentators parse it in two ways: as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the sentence before it, or as the khabar of a dropped mubtadaʾ, “he is Zayd”. Either way niʿma, a rigid past verb, has its own fāʿil, al-rajulu, and Zayd is not that fāʿil.

The second verb of praise is ḥabbadhā: ḥabbadhā Zaydun, “how lovely is Zayd!”. Ḥabba is the verb, its fāʿil is dhā, and Zayd is the one singled out. A tamyīz or a ḥāl may come before or after him: ḥabbadhā rajulan Zaydun, ḥabbadhā Zaydun rajulan; ḥabbadhā rākiban Zaydun, ḥabbadhā Zaydun rākiban.

Blame also has two verbs. Biʾsa: biʾsa al-rajulu ʿAmrun, biʾsa ghulāmu al-rajuli ʿAmrun, biʾsa rajulan ʿAmrun. And sāʾa, “like biʾsa in all the kinds”: sāʾa al-rajulu Zaydun, sāʾa ghulāmu al-rajuli Zaydun, sāʾa rajulan Zaydun. With this the part on the verb ends; the particles come next.

the one singled out for praise, as Zayd
ḥabba with its fāʿil dhā: “how lovely is…”
the tamyīz that explains a hidden fāʿil: niʿma rajulan

tasks.prompt: Name the fāʿil and the one singled out: niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun; niʿma rajulan Zaydun; ḥabbadhā Zaydun.
tasks.arabic: نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ — نِعْمَ رَجُلًا زَيْدٌ — حَبَّذَا زَيْدٌ
tasks.answer: In the first, the fāʿil is al-rajulu and Zaydun is singled out. In the second, the fāʿil is a hidden pronoun, explained by the tamyīz rajulan; Zaydun is singled out. In the third, the fāʿil of ḥabba is dhā, and Zaydun is singled out.

tasks.prompt: Give the two parsings of Zaydun in niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun.
tasks.answer: A mubtadaʾ put last, whose khabar is the sentence niʿma al-rajulu before it; or the khabar of a dropped mubtadaʾ (huwa Zaydun).

tasks.prompt: Unfold fa-niʿimmā hiya as the book does.
tasks.answer: Niʿma shayʾan hiya: niʿma with a hidden fāʿil, explained by mā in the sense of shayʾan, “a thing”; hiya is the one singled out.

tasks.prompt: Put a ḥāl before and after the one singled out with ḥabbadhā, as in the book.
tasks.answer: Ḥabbadhā rākiban Zaydun, and ḥabbadhā Zaydun rākiban, “how lovely is Zayd, riding!”.
