options: how excellent a thing it is!

text.original: فَصْلٌ: أَفْعَالُ الْمَدْحِ وَالذَّمِّ، مَا وُضِعَ لِإِنْشَاءِ مَدْحٍ أَوْ ذَمٍّ. أَمَّا الْمَدْحُ فَلَهُ فِعْلَانِ: نِعْمَ، وَفَاعِلُهُ اسْمٌ مُعَرَّفٌ بِاللَّامِ، نَحْوُ: نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ، أَوْ مُضَافٌ إِلَى الْمُعَرَّفِ بِاللَّامِ، نَحْوُ: نِعْمَ غُلَامُ الرَّجُلِ زَيْدٌ، وَقَدْ يَكُونُ فَاعِلُهُ مُضْمَرًا، وَيَجِبُ تَمْيِيزُهُ بِنَكِرَةٍ مَنْصُوبَةٍ، نَحْوُ: نِعْمَ رَجُلًا زَيْدٌ، أَوْ بِمَا، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ، أَيْ نِعْمَ شَيْئًا هِيَ. وَزَيْدٌ يُسَمَّى الْمَخْصُوصَ بِالْمَدْحِ.
text.en: Section. The verbs of praise and blame: what is laid down to express praise or blame. Praise has two verbs. niʿma: its fāʿil is a noun defined by the lām, as niʿma al-rajulu Zaydun “how excellent a man is Zayd!”, or muḍāf to one defined by the lām, as niʿma ghulāmu al-rajuli Zaydun “how excellent the man's servant is Zayd!”; its fāʿil may be a pronoun, and then it must be specified by an indefinite in naṣb, as niʿma rajulan Zaydun “how excellent a man is Zayd!”, or by mā, as in His saying, exalted is He: fa-niʿimmā hiya “how excellent it is!”, that is, niʿma shayʾan hiya “how excellent a thing it is!”. Zayd is called the one singled out for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ).

text.original: وَحَبَّذَا، نَحْوُ: حَبَّذَا زَيْدٌ؛ فَحَبَّ فِعْلُ الْمَدْحِ، وَفَاعِلُهُ ذَا، وَالْمَخْصُوصُ بِالْمَدْحِ زَيْدٌ. وَيَجُوزُ أَنْ يَقَعَ قَبْلَ الْمَخْصُوصِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ تَمْيِيزٌ، نَحْوُ: حَبَّذَا رَجُلًا زَيْدٌ، وَحَبَّذَا زَيْدٌ رَجُلًا، أَوْ حَالٌ، نَحْوُ: حَبَّذَا رَاكِبًا زَيْدٌ، وَحَبَّذَا زَيْدٌ رَاكِبًا.
text.en: And ḥabbadhā, as ḥabbadhā Zaydun “how lovely is Zayd!”: ḥabba is the verb of praise, its fāʿil is dhā and the one singled out for praise is Zayd. Before the one singled out or after it there may stand a tamyīz, as ḥabbadhā rajulan Zaydun and wa-ḥabbadhā Zaydun rajulan “how lovely a man is Zayd!”, or a ḥāl, as ḥabbadhā rākiban Zaydun and wa-ḥabbadhā Zaydun rākiban “how lovely is Zayd riding!”.

text.original: وَأَمَّا الذَّمُّ فَلَهُ فِعْلَانِ أَيْضًا: بِئْسَ، نَحْوُ: بِئْسَ الرَّجُلُ عَمْرٌو، وَبِئْسَ غُلَامُ الرَّجُلِ عَمْرٌو، وَبِئْسَ رَجُلًا عَمْرٌو؛ وَسَاءَ، نَحْوُ: سَاءَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ، وَسَاءَ غُلَامُ الرَّجُلِ زَيْدٌ، وَسَاءَ رَجُلًا زَيْدٌ. وَسَاءَ مِثْلُ بِئْسَ فِي سَائِرِ الْأَقْسَامِ.
text.en: Blame too has two verbs: biʾsa, as biʾsa al-rajulu ʿAmrun “how bad a man is ʿAmr!”, wa-biʾsa ghulāmu al-rajuli ʿAmrun and wa-biʾsa rajulan ʿAmrun; and sāʾa, as sāʾa al-rajulu Zaydun “how bad a man is Zayd!”, wa-sāʾa ghulāmu al-rajuli Zaydun and wa-sāʾa rajulan Zaydun. Sāʾa is like biʾsa in all the kinds.

lessons.title: The seventeen kinds of particle; the particles of jarr; min
body: The third part is on the particle, defined in lesson 3. Its kinds are seventeen: the particles of jarr; those resembling the verb; of ʿaṭf; of calling attention; of the vocative; of answer (ījāb); the additional; the two of explanation; of the maṣdar; of urging; the particle of expectation; the two of question; of condition; the particle of rebuke; the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; the tanwīn; and the two nūns of emphasis. Many were met already in the parts on the noun and the verb; here each is taken by itself.

The particles of jarr are “laid down to carry the verb, or what resembles it, or the meaning of the verb, through to what follows them”: a verb, marartu bi-Zaydin; a participle, anā mārrun bi-Zaydin; the meaning of a verb, hādhā fī al-dāri abūka, “that is, ushīru ilayhi fīhā”, I point to him in it. That is why every particle of jarr with its noun must be attached to something with a verb's meaning.

They are nineteen. Min is for the beginning of an extent, “and its sign is that the end can rightly be set over against it”: sirtu mina al-baṣrati ilā al-kūfati. It is for making clear, when alladhī could take its place: fa-jtanibū al-rijsa mina al-awthāni (Q 22:30), “shun the filth that is the idols”. It is for the part, when baʿḍ, “some”, could take its place: akhadhtu mina al-darāhimi. And it is additional when dropping it spoils nothing: mā jāʾanī min aḥadin, “not anyone came to me”.

Min is not added in affirmative speech, “against the Kūfans”; their example qad kāna min maṭarin, “there has been some rain”, the book says, “is interpreted” otherwise. Each meaning of min comes with a test, and the student should use them: try ilā against it, alladhī or baʿḍ in its place, or drop it, and see which one fits.

tasks.prompt: Find the meaning of min by the book's tests: sirtu mina al-baṣrati; akhadhtu mina al-darāhimi; mā jāʾanī min aḥadin.
tasks.answer: Sirtu mina al-baṣrati: the beginning of the extent, since an end can be set against it (ilā al-kūfati). Akhadhtu mina al-darāhimi: the part, since baʿḍ could replace it (“some of the dirhams”). Mā jāʾanī min aḥadin: additional, since mā jāʾanī aḥadun means the same.

tasks.prompt: In hādhā fī al-dāri abūka, what does fī carry through, and to what?
tasks.answer: The meaning of a verb in hādhā, “I point to him”, through to al-dāri: ushīru ilayhi fīhā, “I point to him in the house”.

tasks.prompt: Why is min in fa-jtanibū al-rijsa mina al-awthāni for making clear and not for the part?
tasks.answer: Alladhī can take its place: “the filth which is the idols”. It tells what the filth is; it does not tell the believers to shun only some of the idols.

tasks.prompt: Do the Kūfans and the book agree on min in affirmative speech?
tasks.answer: No. The Kūfans allow min to be additional in affirmative speech, as qad kāna min maṭarin; the book does not, and interprets such examples otherwise.

quiz.prompt: How many kinds of particle does the book count?
quiz.explanation: From the particles of jarr to the nūns of emphasis.

text.original: وَقَدْ مَضَى تَعْرِيفُهُ، وَأَقْسَامُهُ سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ: حُرُوفُ الْجَرِّ، وَالْحُرُوفُ الْمُشَبَّهَةُ بِالْفِعْلِ، وَحُرُوفُ الْعَطْفِ، وَحُرُوفُ التَّنْبِيهِ، وَحُرُوفُ النِّدَاءِ، وَحُرُوفُ الْإِيجَابِ، وَحُرُوفُ الزِّيَادَةِ، وَحَرْفَا التَّفْسِيرِ، وَحُرُوفُ الْمَصْدَرِ، وَحُرُوفُ التَّحْضِيضِ، وَحَرْفُ التَّوَقُّعِ، وَحَرْفَا الِاسْتِفْهَامِ، وَحُرُوفُ الشَّرْطِ، وَحَرْفُ الرَّدْعِ، وَتَاءُ التَّأْنِيثِ السَّاكِنَةُ، وَالتَّنْوِينُ، وَنُونَا التَّأْكِيدِ.
text.en: Its definition has passed. Its kinds are seventeen: the particles of jarr; the particles resembling the verb; the particles of conjunction; the particles of calling attention; the particles of the vocative; the particles of affirmation (ījāb); the additional particles; the two particles of explanation; the particles of the maṣdar; the particles of urging (taḥḍīḍ); the particle of expectation; the two particles of question; the particles of condition; the particle of rebuke (radʿ); the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; the tanwīn; and the two nūns of emphasis.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: حُرُوفُ الْجَرِّ حُرُوفٌ وُضِعَتْ لِإِفْضَاءِ الْفِعْلِ أَوْ شِبْهِهِ أَوْ مَعْنَى الْفِعْلِ إِلَى مَا يَلِيهِ، نَحْوُ: مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ، وَأَنَا مَارٌّ بِزَيْدٍ، وَهَذَا فِي الدَّارِ أَبُوكَ، أَيْ أُشِيرُ إِلَيْهِ فِيهَا. وَهِيَ تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ حَرْفًا: مِنْ، وَهِيَ لِابْتِدَاءِ الْغَايَةِ، وَعَلَامَتُهُ أَنْ يَصِحَّ فِي مُقَابَلَتِهِ الِانْتِهَاءُ، كَمَا تَقُولُ: سِرْتُ مِنَ الْبَصْرَةِ إِلَى الْكُوفَةِ.
text.en: Section. The particles of jarr are particles laid down to carry the verb, or what resembles it, or the meaning of the verb, through to what follows them, as marartu bi-Zaydin “I passed by Zayd”, wa-anā mārrun bi-Zaydin “and I am passing by Zayd” and wa-hādhā fī al-dāri abūka “and this, in the house, is your father”, that is, ushīru ilayhi fīhā “I point to him in it”. They are nineteen particles. min: it is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and its sign is that the end can rightly be set over against it, as you say sirtu mina al-baṣrati ilā al-kūfati “I travelled from Baṣra to Kūfa”;

text.original: وَلِلتَّبْيِينِ، وَعَلَامَتُهُ أَنْ يَصِحَّ وَضْعُ لَفْظِ الَّذِي مَكَانَهُ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثَانِ، وَلِلتَّبْعِيضِ، وَعَلَامَتُهُ أَنْ يَصِحَّ وَضْعُ لَفْظِ بَعْضٍ مَكَانَهُ، نَحْوُ: أَخَذْتُ مِنَ الدَّرَاهِمِ، وَزَائِدَةً، وَعَلَامَتُهُ أَنْ لَا يَخْتَلَّ الْمَعْنَى بِإِسْقَاطِهَا، نَحْوُ: مَا جَاءَنِي مِنْ أَحَدٍ. وَلَا تُزَادُ مِنْ فِي الْكَلَامِ الْمُوجَبِ، خِلَافًا لِلْكُوفِيِّينَ، وَأَمَّا قَوْلُهُمْ: قَدْ كَانَ مِنْ مَطَرٍ، وَشِبْهُهُ، فَمُتَأَوَّلٌ.
text.en: for making clear (tabyīn), and its sign is that the word alladhī can rightly be put in its place, as in His saying, exalted is He: fa-ijtanibū al-rijsa mina al-awthāni “so shun the filth of idols”; for the part (tabʿīḍ), and its sign is that the word baʿḍ (some) can rightly be put in its place, as akhadhtu mina al-darāhimi “I took some of the dirhams”; and additional, and its sign is that the meaning is not spoiled by dropping it, as mā jāʾanī min aḥadin “not anyone came to me”. Min is not added in affirmative speech, against the Kūfans; as for their saying qad kāna min maṭarin “there has been some rain” and the like, it is interpreted [otherwise].

lessons.title: Ilā, ḥattā, fī and the bāʾ
body: Ilā is for the end of the extent, and rarely means maʿa, “with”: fa-ghsilū wujūhakum wa-aydiyakum ilā al-marāfiqi (Q 5:6), the hands with the elbows. Ḥattā is like ilā, nimtu al-bāriḥata ḥattā al-ṣabāḥi, “I slept last night until the morning”, and often means maʿa: qadima al-ḥājju ḥattā al-mushāti, “the pilgrims came, even those on foot”. It comes only on an explicit noun, so ḥattāhu is not said, “against al-Mubarrad”, and the poet's ḥattāka is irregular.
Fī is for containing: Zaydun fī al-dāri, al-māʾu fī al-kūzi; and rarely for ʿalā, “on”: wa-la-uṣallibannakum fī judhūʿi al-nakhli (Q 20:71), on the trunks of the palms, held as fast as if in them.

The bāʾ is first for sticking (ilṣāq): marartu bi-Zaydin, “that is, my passing stuck to a place near which Zayd is”, not to Zayd himself. Then for seeking help, katabtu bi-l-qalami; for the cause, innakum ẓalamtum anfusakum bi-ttikhādhikumu al-ʿijla (Q 2:54); for company, kharaja Zaydun bi-ʿashīratihi; for exchange, biʿtu hādhā bi-dhāka; for making a verb transitive, dhahabtu bi-Zaydin, “I took Zayd away”; and for place, jalastu bi-l-masjidi.

The bāʾ is also additional: by rule in the khabar of a negation, mā Zaydun bi-qāʾimin, and of a question, hal Zaydun bi-qāʾimin; and by hearing in a marfūʿ, bi-ḥasbika dirhamun, “that is, ḥasbuka”, kafā bi-Allāhi shahīdan, “that is, kafā Allāhu”, and in a manṣūb, alqā bi-yadihi, “that is, yadahu”. The additional bāʾ adds strength, not meaning, and the word after it keeps its own place in iʿrāb.

terms.en: the end of the extent: ilā and ḥattā
containing: the meaning of fī
sticking: the first meaning of the bāʾ
making a verb transitive: dhahabtu bi-Zaydin

examples.en: ḥattā meaning “with, even”
fī meaning “on” (Q 20:71)
the bāʾ of seeking help

tasks.prompt: Give the meaning of the bāʾ in each: katabtu bi-l-qalami; biʿtu hādhā bi-dhāka; kharaja Zaydun bi-ʿashīratihi; mā Zaydun bi-qāʾimin.
tasks.answer: Bi-l-qalami: seeking help. Bi-dhāka: exchange. Bi-ʿashīratihi: company. Bi-qāʾimin: additional, by rule, in the khabar of a negation.

tasks.prompt: Why is ḥattāhu not said, and what does the book make of the poet's ḥattāka?
tasks.answer: Ḥattā comes only upon an explicit noun, not a pronoun; al-Mubarrad allowed it, but the book does not. The poet's ḥattāka is heard, so it is called irregular, not a model.

tasks.prompt: Parse Allāhi in kafā bi-Allāhi shahīdan.
tasks.answer: The bāʾ is additional, by hearing. Allāhi is in jarr in its wording but is the fāʿil of kafā in its place: kafā Allāhu. Shahīdan is a tamyīz (or ḥāl).

tasks.prompt: What does marartu bi-Zaydin mean exactly, according to the book?
tasks.answer: The bāʾ is for sticking: “my passing stuck to a place near which Zayd is”; the passing touched the place by Zayd, not Zayd himself.

text.original: وَإِلَى، وَهِيَ لِانْتِهَاءِ الْغَايَةِ، كَمَا مَرَّ، وَبِمَعْنَى مَعَ قَلِيلًا، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ. وَحَتَّى، وَهِيَ مِثْلُ إِلَى، نَحْوُ: نِمْتُ الْبَارِحَةَ حَتَّى الصَّبَاحِ، وَبِمَعْنَى مَعَ كَثِيرًا، نَحْوُ: قَدِمَ الْحَاجُّ حَتَّى الْمُشَاةِ، وَلَا تَدْخُلُ إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّاهِرِ، فَلَا يُقَالُ: حَتَّاهُ، خِلَافًا لِلْمُبَرِّدِ، وَقَوْلُ الشَّاعِرِ، شِعْرٌ: فَلَا وَاللَّهِ لَا يَبْقَى أُنَاسٌ * فَتًى حَتَّاكَ يَا ابْنَ أَبِي زِيَادِ، شَاذٌّ.
text.en: ilā: it is for the end of the extent, as has passed, and in the meaning of maʿa “with”, rarely, as in His saying, exalted is He: fa-ighsilū wujūhakum wa-aydiyakum ilā al-marāfiqi “then wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows”. ḥattā: it is like ilā, as nimtu al-bāriḥata ḥattā al-ṣabāḥi “I slept last night until the morning”, and in the meaning of maʿa, often, as qadima al-ḥājju ḥattā al-mushāti “the pilgrims arrived, even those on foot”; it comes only upon an explicit noun, so one does not say ḥattāhu, against al-Mubarrad; and the poet's saying, verse: fa-lā wa-Allāhi lā yabqā unāsun / fatan ḥattāka yā ibna Abī Ziyādi “No, by God, people will not let a young man remain, up to you, O son of Abū Ziyād”, is irregular.

text.original: وَفِي، وَهِيَ لِلظَّرْفِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ، وَالْمَاءُ فِي الْكُوزِ، وَبِمَعْنَى عَلَى قَلِيلًا، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ. وَالْبَاءُ، وَهِيَ لِلْإِلْصَاقِ، نَحْوُ: مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ، أَيِ الْتَصَقَ مُرُورِي بِمَوْضِعٍ يَقْرُبُ مِنْهُ زَيْدٌ، وَلِلِاسْتِعَانَةِ، نَحْوُ: كَتَبْتُ بِالْقَلَمِ.
text.en: fī: it is for containing (ẓarfiyya), as Zaydun fī al-dāri “Zayd is in the house” and wa-al-māʾu fī al-kūzi “and the water is in the jug”, and in the meaning of ʿalā “on”, rarely, as His saying, exalted is He: wa-la-uṣallibannakum fī judhūʿi al-nakhli “and I shall crucify you on the trunks of palm trees”. The bāʾ: it is for sticking (ilṣāq), as marartu bi-Zaydin “I passed by Zayd”, that is, my passing stuck to a place near which Zayd is; and for seeking help (istiʿāna), as katabtu bi-al-qalami “I wrote with the pen”;

text.original: وَقَدْ يَكُونُ لِلتَّعْلِيلِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ، وَلِلْمُصَاحَبَةِ، نَحْوُ: خَرَجَ زَيْدٌ بِعَشِيرَتِهِ، وَلِلْمُقَابَلَةِ، نَحْوُ: بِعْتُ هَذَا بِذَاكَ، وَلِلتَّعْدِيَةِ، نَحْوُ: ذَهَبْتُ بِزَيْدٍ، وَلِلظَّرْفِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: جَلَسْتُ بِالْمَسْجِدِ.
text.en: it may be for the cause (taʿlīl), as in His saying, exalted is He: innakum ẓalamtum anfusakum bi-ittikhādhikumu al-ʿijla “you have wronged yourselves by your taking the calf”; for accompaniment, as kharaja Zaydun bi-ʿashīratihi “Zayd went out with his clan”; for exchange, as biʿtu hādhā bi-dhāka “I sold this for that”; for making transitive (taʿdiya), as dhahabtu bi-Zaydin “I took Zayd away”; and for place, as jalastu bi-al-masjidi “I sat in the mosque”.

text.original: وَزَائِدَةً قِيَاسًا فِي خَبَرِ النَّفْيِ، نَحْوُ: مَا زَيْدٌ بِقَائِمٍ، وَفِي الِاسْتِفْهَامِ، نَحْوُ: هَلْ زَيْدٌ بِقَائِمٍ، وَسَمَاعًا فِي الْمَرْفُوعِ، نَحْوُ: بِحَسْبِكَ دِرْهَمٌ، أَيْ حَسْبُكَ، وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا، أَيْ كَفَى اللَّهُ، وَفِي الْمَنْصُوبِ، نَحْوُ: أَلْقَى بِيَدِهِ، أَيْ يَدَهُ.
text.en: [It comes] additional, by rule, in the khabar of the negation, as mā Zaydun bi-qāʾimin “Zayd is not standing at all”, and in the question, as hal Zaydun bi-qāʾimin “is Zayd standing?”; and by hearing in the marfūʿ, as bi-ḥasbika dirhamun “a dirham is enough for you”, that is, ḥasbuka, and kafā bi-Allāhi shahīdan “God suffices as witness”, that is, kafā Allāhu; and in the manṣūb, as alqā bi-yadihi “he threw his hand”, that is, yadahu.

lessons.title: The lām; rubba
body: The lām is for belonging (ikhtiṣāṣ): al-jullu li-l-farasi, “the saddle-cloth is for the horse”, al-mālu li-Zaydin. For the cause: ḍarabtuhu li-l-taʾdībi. Additional: radifa lakum (Q 27:72), “that is, radifakum”. In the meaning of ʿan, “about”, with verbs of saying: wa-qāla alladhīna kafarū lilladhīna āmanū law kāna khayran mā sabaqūnā ilayhi (Q 46:11), said of the believers, not to them, since they speak of them in the third person; “and in this there is room for consideration”. And in an oath of wonder, like the wāw: li-Allāhi yabqā ʿalā al-ayyāmi dhū ḥiyadin, “by God, there remains, despite the days, one with knotted horns”, in a verse of al-Hudhalī.

Rubba is for fewness, “as the declarative kam is for multitude” (lesson 34). It claims the head of speech, and comes only on an indefinite that is qualified, rubba rajulin karīmin laqītuhu, “seldom have I met a noble man”; or on a vague pronoun, “always singular and masculine”, explained by an indefinite in naṣb: rubbahu rajulan, rubbahu rajulayni, rubbahu rijālan, rubbahu imraʾatan. The Kūfans make the pronoun agree: rubbahumā rajulayni, rubbahum rijālan, rubbahā imraʾatan.

With the mā that stops it (mā al-kāffa), rubba no longer governs and may come upon either sentence: rubbamā qāma Zaydun, rubbamā Zaydun qāʾimun. Rubba must have a past verb, “because fewness is realised in it”: one can only say that something has seldom been.

That verb is mostly dropped. To one who asks hal laqīta man akramaka, “have you met one who honoured you?”, you answer rubba rajulin akramanī, that is, rubba rajulin akramanī laqītuhu. The book parses it with care: akramanī is the adjective of rajulin, and laqītuhu, the dropped verb, is what rubba is attached to. A beginner who takes akramanī for that verb has missed the qualified indefinite.

tasks.prompt: Give the meaning of the lām: al-mālu li-Zaydin; ḍarabtuhu li-l-taʾdībi; radifa lakum.
tasks.answer: Al-mālu li-Zaydin: belonging. Ḍarabtuhu li-l-taʾdībi: the cause. Radifa lakum: additional, as radifakum.

tasks.prompt: Why does the lām in lilladhīna āmanū (Q 46:11) mean “about” and not “to”?
tasks.arabic: وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْ كَانَ خَيْرًا مَا سَبَقُونَا إِلَيْهِ
tasks.answer: What they say is in the third person: “they would not have gone before us to it”. So they are speaking of the believers, not to them; the lām with a verb of saying is in the meaning of ʿan. The book adds that this is open to consideration.

tasks.prompt: Say “seldom a woman” with rubba and a pronoun, as the book does and as the Kūfans do.
tasks.answer: The book: rubbahu imraʾatan, the pronoun always singular and masculine. The Kūfans: rubbahā imraʾatan, the pronoun agreeing with the tamyīz.

tasks.prompt: Parse rubba rajulin akramanī, said in answer to hal laqīta man akramaka.
tasks.answer: Rubba: the particle of fewness. Rajulin: in jarr by rubba, an indefinite. Akramanī: a sentence that is its adjective. The verb rubba is attached to, laqītuhu, is dropped: rubba rajulin akramanī laqītuhu.

text.original: وَاللَّامُ، وَهِيَ لِلِاخْتِصَاصِ، نَحْوُ: الْجُلُّ لِلْفَرَسِ، وَالْمَالُ لِزَيْدٍ، وَلِلتَّعْلِيلِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبْتُهُ لِلتَّأْدِيبِ، وَزَائِدَةً، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: رَدِفَ لَكُمْ، أَيْ رَدِفَكُمْ، وَبِمَعْنَى عَنْ إِذَا اسْتُعْمِلَ مَعَ الْقَوْلِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْ كَانَ خَيْرًا مَا سَبَقُونَا إِلَيْهِ، وَفِيهِ نَظَرٌ، وَبِمَعْنَى الْوَاوِ فِي الْقَسَمِ لِلتَّعَجُّبِ، كَقَوْلِ الْهُذَلِيِّ، شِعْرٌ: لِلَّهِ يَبْقَى عَلَى الْأَيَّامِ ذُو حِيَدٍ * بِمُشْمَخِرٍّ بِهِ الظَّيَّانُ وَالْآسُ.
text.en: The lām: it is for belonging (ikhtiṣāṣ), as al-jullu li-al-farasi “the saddle-cloth is for the horse” and wa-al-mālu li-Zaydin “and the wealth is Zayd's”; for the cause, as ḍarabtuhu li-al-taʾdībi “I hit him for correction”; additional, as in His saying, exalted is He: radifa lakum “has come close behind you”, that is, radifakum; in the meaning of ʿan when it is used with saying, as in His saying, exalted is He: wa-qāla alladhīna kafarū lilladhīna āmanū law kāna khayran mā sabaqūnā ilayhi “and those who disbelieve say of those who believe: if it were good, they would not have gone before us to it”, and in this there is [room for] consideration; and in the meaning of the wāw in the oath, for wonder, as in the saying of al-Hudhalī, verse: li-Allāhi yabqā ʿalā al-ayyāmi dhū ḥiyadin / bi-mushmakhirrin bihi al-ẓayyānu wa-al-āsu “By God, there remains, despite the days, one with knotted horns / on a towering peak where the jasmine and the myrtle grow”.

text.original: وَرُبَّ، وَهِيَ لِلتَّقْلِيلِ، كَمَا أَنَّ كَمِ الْخَبَرِيَّةَ لِلتَّكْثِيرِ، وَتَسْتَحِقُّ صَدْرَ الْكَلَامِ، وَلَا تَدْخُلُ إِلَّا عَلَى نَكِرَةٍ مَوْصُوفَةٍ، نَحْوُ: رُبَّ رَجُلٍ كَرِيمٍ لَقِيتُهُ، أَوْ مُضْمَرٍ مُبْهَمٍ مُفْرَدٍ مُذَكَّرٍ أَبَدًا، مُمَيَّزٍ بِنَكِرَةٍ مَنْصُوبَةٍ، نَحْوُ: رُبَّهُ رَجُلًا، وَرُبَّهُ رَجُلَيْنِ، وَرُبَّهُ رِجَالًا، وَرُبَّهُ امْرَأَةً، وَكَذَلِكَ الْبَوَاقِي. وَعِنْدَ الْكُوفِيِّينَ يَجِبُ الْمُطَابَقَةُ، نَحْوُ: رُبَّهُمَا رَجُلَيْنِ، وَرُبَّهُمْ رِجَالًا، وَرُبَّهَا امْرَأَةً.
text.en: rubba: it is for fewness (taqlīl), as the declarative kam is for multitude; it has the right to the head of speech, and comes only upon an indefinite that is qualified, as rubba rajulin karīmin laqītuhu “seldom have I met a noble man”, or upon a vague pronoun, always singular and masculine, specified by an indefinite in naṣb, as rubbahu rajulan “seldom a man”, wa-rubbahu rajulayni, wa-rubbahu rijālan and wa-rubbahu imraʾatan, and likewise the rest. With the Kūfans agreement is necessary, as rubbahumā rajulayni, wa-rubbahum rijālan and wa-rubbahā imraʾatan.

text.original: وَقَدْ تَلْحَقُهَا مَا الْكَافَّةُ فَتَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْجُمْلَتَيْنِ، نَحْوُ: رُبَّمَا قَامَ زَيْدٌ، وَرُبَّمَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ. وَلَا بُدَّ لَهَا مِنْ فِعْلٍ مَاضٍ؛ لِأَنَّ التَّقْلِيلَ يَتَحَقَّقُ فِيهِ، وَيُحْذَفُ ذَلِكَ الْفِعْلُ غَالِبًا، كَقَوْلِكَ: رُبَّ رَجُلٍ أَكْرَمَنِي، فِي جَوَابِ مَنْ قَالَ: هَلْ لَقِيتَ مَنْ أَكْرَمَكَ؟ أَيْ رُبَّ رَجُلٍ أَكْرَمَنِي لَقِيتُهُ؛ فَأَكْرَمَنِي صِفَةُ الرَّجُلِ، وَلَقِيتُهُ فِعْلُهَا، وَهُوَ مَحْذُوفٌ.
text.en: The mā that stops [governing] (mā al-kāffa) may be joined to it, and then it comes upon both [kinds of] sentence, as rubbamā qāma Zaydun “seldom has Zayd stood” and wa-rubbamā Zaydun qāʾimun. It must have a past verb, because fewness is realised in it; and that verb is mostly dropped, as your saying rubba rajulin akramanī “seldom a man who honoured me” in answer to one who says hal laqīta man akramaka “have you met one who honoured you?”, that is, rubba rajulin akramanī laqītuhu “seldom have I met a man who honoured me”: akramanī is the adjective of the man, and laqītuhu is its verb, which is dropped.

lessons.title: The wāw of rubba; the particles of the oath and its answer
body: The wāw of rubba is the wāw with which speech opens, in the sense of rubba: wa-baldatin laysa bihā anīsu, illā al-yaʿāfīru wa-illā al-ʿīsu, “and many a land with no companion but young gazelles and white camels”. Baldatin is in jarr after it, as after rubba itself.

The particles of the oath are three. The wāw comes only on an explicit noun: wa-Allāhi, wa-l-raḥmāni, la-aḍribanna; one does not say wa-ka. The tāʾ comes only on the name Allāh: ta-Allāhi; not ta-l-raḥmāni, and ta-rabbi al-kaʿbati is irregular. The bāʾ comes on an explicit noun and on a pronoun: bi-Allāhi, bi-l-raḥmāni, bika. The commentators explain the narrowing: the bāʾ is the origin and is free; the wāw stands for it and keeps to explicit nouns; the tāʾ stands for the wāw and keeps to one name.

An oath must have an answer, the sentence sworn upon (al-muqsam ʿalayhi). An affirmative answer takes the lām, in a nominal or a verbal sentence, wa-Allāhi la-Zaydun qāʾimun, wa-Allāhi la-afʿalanna kadhā; or inna in a nominal one, wa-Allāhi inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun. A negative answer takes mā or lā: wa-Allāhi mā Zaydun bi-qāʾimin; wa-Allāhi lā yaqūmu Zaydun.

The negation may be dropped when nothing is confused: ta-Allāhi taftaʾu tadhkuru Yūsufa (Q 12:85), “that is, lā taftaʾu”, you will not cease remembering Yūsuf; an affirmative answer would have needed the lām and the nūn of emphasis, so their absence shows the negation. And the whole answer may be dropped when what comes before shows it, Zaydun qāʾimun wa-Allāhi, or when the oath stands in the middle, Zaydun wa-Allāhi qāʾimun.

the particles of the oath: the bāʾ, the wāw, the tāʾ

tasks.prompt: Which oath particle is allowed? wa-ka; bika; ta-l-raḥmāni; ta-Allāhi.
tasks.answer: Wa-ka: not allowed (the wāw takes only explicit nouns). Bika: allowed (the bāʾ takes pronouns too). Ta-l-raḥmāni: not allowed (the tāʾ is for Allāh alone). Ta-Allāhi: allowed.

tasks.prompt: Put the oath wa-Allāhi before Zaydun qāʾimun, affirmative and negative.
tasks.answer: Affirmative: wa-Allāhi la-Zaydun qāʾimun, or wa-Allāhi inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun. Negative: wa-Allāhi mā Zaydun bi-qāʾimin (or with lā in a verbal sentence).

tasks.prompt: How does one know that taftaʾu in Q 12:85 is negated?
tasks.answer: An affirmative answer of an oath must have the lām (and with a muḍāriʿ the nūn of emphasis). Taftaʾu has neither, so the answer is negative, with lā dropped: lā taftaʾu. Nothing is confused, so the dropping is allowed.

tasks.prompt: Why has Zaydun wa-Allāhi qāʾimun no separate answer?
tasks.answer: The oath stands in the middle of the sentence, and the sentence itself shows what is sworn; so the answer is dropped.

text.original: وَوَاوُ رُبَّ، وَهِيَ الْوَاوُ الَّتِي يُبْتَدَأُ بِهَا فِي أَوَّلِ الْكَلَامِ، كَقَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ، شِعْرٌ: وَبَلْدَةٍ لَيْسَ بِهَا أَنِيسُ * إِلَّا الْيَعَافِيرُ وَإِلَّا الْعِيسُ. وَوَاوُ الْقَسَمِ، وَهِيَ تَخْتَصُّ بِالظَّاهِرِ، نَحْوُ: وَاللَّهِ، وَالرَّحْمَنِ، لَأَضْرِبَنَّ، فَلَا يُقَالُ: وَكَ. وَتَاءُ الْقَسَمِ، وَهِيَ تَخْتَصُّ بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ، فَلَا يُقَالُ: تَالرَّحْمَنِ، وَقَوْلُهُمْ: تَرَبِّ الْكَعْبَةِ، شَاذٌّ. وَبَاءُ الْقَسَمِ، وَهِيَ تَدْخُلُ عَلَى الظَّاهِرِ وَالْمُضْمَرِ، نَحْوُ: بِاللَّهِ، وَبِالرَّحْمَنِ، وَبِكَ.
text.en: The wāw of rubba is the wāw with which one begins at the start of speech, as in the poet's saying, verse: wa-baldatin laysa bi-hā anīsu / illā al-yaʿāfīru wa-illā al-ʿīsu “And [many] a land with no companion in it / but the young gazelles and the white camels”. The wāw of the oath belongs to the explicit noun, as wa-Allāhi and wa-al-raḥmāni “by God, by the Merciful”, la-aḍribanna “I shall surely hit”; so one does not say wa-ka. The tāʾ of the oath belongs to Allāh alone, so one does not say ta-al-raḥmāni; and their saying ta-rabbi al-kaʿbati “by the Lord of the Kaʿba” is irregular. The bāʾ of the oath comes upon the explicit noun and the pronoun, as bi-Allāhi, wa-bi-al-raḥmāni and wa-bi-ka.

text.original: وَلَا بُدَّ لِلْقَسَمِ مِنَ الْجَوَابِ، وَهِيَ جُمْلَةٌ تُسَمَّى الْمُقْسَمَ عَلَيْهَا؛ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ مُثْبَتَةً يَجِبُ دُخُولُ اللَّامِ فِي الِاسْمِيَّةِ وَالْفِعْلِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: وَاللَّهِ لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، وَوَاللَّهِ لَأَفْعَلَنَّ كَذَا، وَإِنَّ فِي الِاسْمِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَقَائِمٌ، وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مَنْفِيَّةً وَجَبَ دُخُولُ مَا وَلَا، نَحْوُ: وَاللَّهِ مَا زَيْدٌ بِقَائِمٍ، وَوَاللَّهِ لَا يَقُومُ زَيْدٌ.
text.en: The oath must have an answer, which is a sentence called the thing sworn upon (al-muqsam ʿalayhā). If it is affirmative, the lām must come in, in the nominal and in the verbal [sentence], as wa-Allāhi la-Zaydun qāʾimun “by God, Zayd is surely standing” and wa-wa-Allāhi la-afʿalanna kadhā “and by God, I shall surely do such-and-such”, and inna in the nominal, as wa-Allāhi inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun “by God, Zayd is surely standing”. If it is negative, mā and lā must come in, as wa-Allāhi mā Zaydun bi-qāʾimin “by God, Zayd is not standing” and wa-wa-Allāhi lā yaqūmu Zaydun “and by God, Zayd will not stand”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ قَدْ يُحْذَفُ حَرْفُ النَّفْيِ لِزَوَالِ اللَّبْسِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: تَاللَّهِ تَفْتَأُ تَذْكُرُ يُوسُفَ، أَيْ لَا تَفْتَأُ. وَقَدْ يُحْذَفُ جَوَابُ الْقَسَمِ إِنْ تَقَدَّمَ مَا يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ وَاللَّهِ، أَوْ تَوَسَّطَ الْقَسَمُ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ وَاللَّهِ قَائِمٌ.
text.en: Know that the particle of negation may be dropped when there is no confusion, as in His saying, exalted is He: ta-Allāhi taftaʾu tadhkuru Yūsufa “by God, you will not cease remembering Yūsuf”, that is, lā taftaʾu. The answer of the oath may be dropped if what indicates it comes before, as Zaydun qāʾimun wa-Allāhi “Zayd is standing, by God”, or if the oath stands in the middle, as Zaydun wa-Allāhi qāʾimun “Zayd, by God, is standing”.

lessons.title: ʿAn, ʿalā, the kāf, mudh; the six that resemble the verb
lessons.arabic: عَنْ وَعَلَى وَالْكَافُ، وَالْحُرُوفُ الْمُشَبَّهَةُ بِالْفِعْلِ
lessons.transliteration: ʿan wa-ʿalā wa-l-kāf, wa-l-ḥurūf al-mushabbaha bi-l-fiʿl
body: ʿAn is for passing beyond (mujāwaza): ramaytu al-sahma ʿani al-qawsi ilā al-ṣaydi, “I shot the arrow from the bow at the game”; the arrow passes beyond the bow. ʿAlā is for being above (istiʿlāʾ): Zaydun ʿalā al-saṭḥi, “Zayd is on the roof”. Both may be nouns when min comes upon them: jalastu min ʿan yamīnihi, “I sat at his right side”; nazaltu min ʿalā al-farasi, “I got down from upon the horse”. The commentators explain: a particle of jarr comes only upon a noun, so here ʿan means “side” and ʿalā means “above”.

The kāf is for likening: Zaydun ka-ʿAmrin, “Zayd is like ʿAmr”. It is additional in laysa ka-mithlihi shayʾun (Q 42:11), “there is nothing like Him”. It may also be a noun, as in the verse yaḍḥakna ʿan ka-al-baradi al-munhammi, “they laugh, showing [teeth] like melting hail”: ʿan is a particle of jarr, so what it comes upon is a noun, and the kāf here means “the like of”.

Mudh and mundhu are for time. Either for the beginning in the past, as you say in Shaʿbān mā raʾaytuhu mudh Rajabin, “I have not seen him since Rajab”; or for containing in the present, mā raʾaytuhu mudh shahrinā, wa-mundhu yawminā, that is, fī shahrinā, wa-fī yawminā, “in this month of ours, in this day of ours”. As nouns they were met among the built adverbs (lesson 36); here they are particles of jarr.

Khalā, ʿadā and ḥāshā are for exception, with what follows them in jarr: jāʾanī al-qawmu khalā Zaydin, wa-ʿadā ʿAmrin, wa-ḥāshā Bakrin, “the people came to me, save Zayd, ʿAmr and Bakr”. This closes the particles of jarr.

A new section opens: the particles that resemble the verb are six, inna, anna, kaʾanna, lākinna, layta and laʿalla. They come upon the nominal sentence, put its ism in naṣb and its khabar in rafʿ, “as you have learned” (lessons 15 and 23): inna Zaydan qāʾimun. The commentators give the resemblance: like the past verb they have three letters or more and are built on the fatḥa, and their meanings are those of verbs (I emphasise, I liken, I correct, I wish, I hope).
The mā that stops (mā al-kāffa) may be joined to them and stop them from governing; then they may come upon verbs: innamā qāma Zaydun, “only Zayd stood”.

being above: the meaning of ʿalā
the additional kāf, as in laysa ka-mithlihi shayʾun
the six particles that resemble the verb: inna and its sisters
the mā that stops inna and its sisters from governing

tasks.prompt: Is ʿan a particle or a noun here? (a) ramaytu al-sahma ʿani al-qawsi; (b) jalastu min ʿan yamīnihi.
tasks.answer: (a) A particle of jarr, for passing beyond: the arrow passes beyond the bow. (b) A noun: min, a particle of jarr, has come upon it, and it means “side”: “I sat at the side of his right”.

tasks.prompt: Name the use of the kāf in each: Zaydun ka-ʿAmrin; laysa ka-mithlihi shayʾun; yaḍḥakna ʿan ka-al-baradi al-munhammi.
tasks.answer: Zaydun ka-ʿAmrin: for likening. Laysa ka-mithlihi shayʾun: additional. Yaḍḥakna ʿan ka-al-baradi: a noun meaning “the like of”, since ʿan, a particle of jarr, has come upon it.

tasks.prompt: It is Shaʿbān. Say that you have not seen him since Rajab, and that you have not seen him this day of ours; name the use of mudh or mundhu in each.
tasks.answer: Mā raʾaytuhu mudh Rajabin: for the beginning in the past. Mā raʾaytuhu mundhu yawminā, that is, fī yawminā: for containing in the present.

tasks.prompt: What changes when mā is joined to inna in innamā qāma Zaydun?
tasks.answer: The mā stops inna from governing (mā al-kāffa). Inna no longer needs an ism in naṣb and a khabar in rafʿ, so it may come upon a verb: innamā qāma Zaydun, “only Zayd stood”.

text.original: وَعَنْ لِلْمُجَاوَزَةِ، نَحْوُ: رَمَيْتُ السَّهْمَ عَنِ الْقَوْسِ إِلَى الصَّيْدِ. وَعَلَى لِلِاسْتِعْلَاءِ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ عَلَى السَّطْحِ. وَقَدْ يَكُونُ عَنْ وَعَلَى اسْمَيْنِ إِذَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ، كَمَا تَقُولُ: جَلَسْتُ مِنْ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ، وَنَزَلْتُ مِنْ عَلَى الْفَرَسِ. وَالْكَافُ لِلتَّشْبِيهِ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ كَعَمْرٍو، وَزَائِدَةً، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ، وَقَدْ تَكُونُ اسْمًا، كَقَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ: يَضْحَكْنَ عَنْ كَالْبَرَدِ الْمُنْهَمِّ.
text.en: ʿan is for passing beyond (mujāwaza), as ramaytu al-sahma ʿani al-qawsi ilā al-ṣaydi “I shot the arrow from the bow at the game”. ʿalā is for being above (istiʿlāʾ), as Zaydun ʿalā al-saṭḥi “Zayd is on the roof”. ʿAn and ʿalā may be nouns when min comes upon them, as you say jalastu min ʿan yamīnihi “I sat at his right side” and wa-nazaltu min ʿalā al-farasi “and I got down from upon the horse”. The kāf is for likening, as Zaydun ka-ʿAmrin “Zayd is like ʿAmr”; additional, as in His saying, exalted is He: laysa ka-mithlihi shayʾun “there is nothing like Him”; and it may be a noun, as in the poet's saying: yaḍḥakna ʿan ka-al-baradi al-munhammi “they laugh [showing teeth] like melting hail”.

text.original: وَمُذْ وَمُنْذُ لِلزَّمَانِ، إِمَّا لِلِابْتِدَاءِ فِي الْمَاضِي، كَمَا تَقُولُ فِي شَعْبَانَ: مَا رَأَيْتُهُ مُذْ رَجَبٍ، أَوْ لِلظَّرْفِيَّةِ فِي الْحَاضِرِ، نَحْوُ: مَا رَأَيْتُهُ مُذْ شَهْرِنَا، وَمُنْذُ يَوْمِنَا، أَيْ فِي شَهْرِنَا وَفِي يَوْمِنَا. وَخَلَا وَعَدَا وَحَاشَا لِلِاسْتِثْنَاءِ، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي الْقَوْمُ خَلَا زَيْدٍ، وَعَدَا عَمْرٍو، وَحَاشَا بَكْرٍ.
text.en: mudh and mundhu are for time: either for the beginning in the past, as you say in Shaʿbān mā raʾaytuhu mudh Rajabin “I have not seen him since Rajab”; or for containing in the present, as mā raʾaytuhu mudh shahrinā “I have not seen him this month of ours” and wa-mundhu yawminā “and this day of ours”, that is, fī shahrinā and wa-fī yawminā. khalā, ʿadā and ḥāshā are for exception, as jāʾanī al-qawmu khalā Zaydin “the people came to me, save Zayd”, wa-ʿadā ʿAmrin and wa-ḥāshā Bakrin.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: الْحُرُوفُ الْمُشَبَّهَةُ بِالْفِعْلِ سِتَّةٌ: إِنَّ، وَأَنَّ، وَكَأَنَّ، وَلَكِنَّ، وَلَيْتَ، وَلَعَلَّ. هَذِهِ الْحُرُوفُ تَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْجُمْلَةِ الِاسْمِيَّةِ، تَنْصِبُ الِاسْمَ وَتَرْفَعُ الْخَبَرَ، كَمَا عَرَفْتَ، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ. وَقَدْ تَلْحَقُهَا مَا الْكَافَّةُ فَتَكُفُّهَا عَنِ الْعَمَلِ، وَحِينَئِذٍ تَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْأَفْعَالِ، تَقُولُ: إِنَّمَا قَامَ زَيْدٌ.
text.en: Section. The particles resembling the verb are six: inna, anna, kaʾanna, lākinna, layta and laʿalla. These particles come upon the nominal sentence; they put the ism in naṣb and the khabar in rafʿ, as you have learned, as inna Zaydan qāʾimun “Zayd is indeed standing”. The mā that stops [governing] may be joined to them and stop them from governing, and then they come upon verbs; you say innamā qāma Zaydun “only Zayd stood”.

lessons.title: Inna and anna: kasra or fatḥa; lightening
body: Inna with kasra does not change the meaning of the sentence; it emphasises it. Anna with fatḥa, together with what follows it, has the rule of a single word: anna and its sentence stand where a single noun would stand. From this the book draws the places of each.

The kasra is necessary at the beginning of speech, inna Zaydan qāʾimun; after saying, yaqūlu innahā baqaratun (Q 2:68), “He says: it is a cow”; after the relative, mā raʾaytu alladhī innahu fī al-masjidi, “I did not see the one who is in the mosque”; and when the lām is in its khabar, inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun. Speech opens with a sentence, what is said is a sentence, and the ṣila of a relative is a sentence, so there the emphasising inna stands.

The fatḥa is necessary wherever a single word is wanted: as fāʿil, balaghanī anna Zaydan qāʾimun, “it has reached me that Zayd is standing”; as mafʿūl, karihtu annaka qāʾimun; as mubtadaʾ, ʿindī annaka qāʾimun; as muḍāf ilayhi, ʿajibtu min ṭūli anna Bakran qāʾimun; as majrūr, ʿajibtu min anna Bakran qāʾimun; and after law and lawlā: law annaka ʿindanā la-akramtuka, lawlā annahu ḥāḍirun la-ghāba Zaydun.

A noun conjoined to the ism of inna with kasra may be in naṣb, after its wording, or in rafʿ, after its place: inna Zaydan qāʾimun wa-ʿAmran, or wa-ʿAmrun. Its place is the rafʿ of the mubtadaʾ that inna came upon.

Inna may be lightened to in, and then the lām is bound to its khabar: wa-in kullan lammā la-yuwaffiyannahum (Q 11:111); then its governing may be cancelled: wa-in kullun lammā jamīʿun ladaynā muḥḍarūna (Q 36:32). Lightened, it may come upon the verbs that come upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar: wa-in kunta min qablihi la-mina al-ghāfilīna (Q 12:3), wa-in naẓunnuka la-mina al-kādhibīna (Q 26:186). The commentators call this lām the lām that tells apart (al-lām al-fāriqa): it shows that in is the lightened inna and not the negating in.

Anna may be lightened to an. Then it must govern an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), which is its ism, and the sentence after it is its khabar, nominal, balaghanī an Zaydun qāʾimun, or verbal, balaghanī an qad qāma Zaydun. Before a verb, the sīn, sawfa, qad or a particle of negation must come: ʿalima an sa-yakūnu minkum marḍā (Q 73:20), “He knows that there will be sick ones among you”.

terms.en: inna with kasra: it emphasises the sentence and leaves its meaning
anna with fatḥa: with its sentence it has the rule of a single word
conjoining on the place: wa-ʿAmrun in rafʿ after the ism of inna
the lightened inna, with the lām bound to its khabar
the pronoun of the matter: the implied ism of the lightened an

tasks.prompt: Kasra or fatḥa? (a) qultu: _nna Zaydan qāʾimun; (b) balaghanī _nna Zaydan qāʾimun; (c) _nna Zaydan la-qāʾimun; (d) law _nnaka ʿindanā la-akramtuka.
tasks.answer: (a) Inna: after saying. (b) Anna: with its sentence it stands as the fāʿil of balaghanī. (c) Inna: the lām is in its khabar. (d) Annaka: after law.

tasks.prompt: Parse the conjoined noun in inna Zaydan qāʾimun wa-ʿAmran, and in inna Zaydan qāʾimun wa-ʿAmrun.
tasks.answer: Wa-ʿAmran is conjoined on the wording of the ism of inna, Zaydan, in naṣb. Wa-ʿAmrun is conjoined on its place, the rafʿ of the mubtadaʾ that inna came upon. The book allows both.

tasks.prompt: In wa-in kunta min qablihi la-mina al-ghāfilīna, what shows that in is the lightened inna and not a negation?
tasks.arabic: وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
tasks.answer: The lām on the khabar, la-mina al-ghāfilīna: the lightened inna binds the lām to its khabar (the commentators call it the lām that tells apart). Here in has come upon kāna, one of the verbs that come upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar.

tasks.prompt: In balaghanī an qad qāma Zaydun, what is the ism of an, and what is its khabar? Why is qad there?
tasks.answer: Its ism is the pronoun of the matter, hidden and implied; its khabar is the sentence qad qāma Zaydun. Before a verb, the lightened an must be followed by the sīn, sawfa, qad or a negation; here it is qad.

quiz.prompt: After a verb of saying the hamza takes…

quiz.explanation: “That Zayd is standing has reached me”: the doer of balagha.

quiz.prompt: After law and lawlā the hamza takes…

The ism of the lightened an is…

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ إِنَّ الْمَكْسُورَةَ الْهَمْزَةِ لَا تُغَيِّرُ مَعْنَى الْجُمْلَةِ، بَلْ تُؤَكِّدُهَا، وَأَنَّ الْمَفْتُوحَةَ الْهَمْزَةِ مَعَ مَا بَعْدَهَا فِي حُكْمِ الْمُفْرَدِ؛ وَلِذَلِكَ يَجِبُ الْكَسْرُ إِذَا كَانَ فِي ابْتِدَاءِ الْكَلَامِ، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، وَبَعْدَ الْقَوْلِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ، وَبَعْدَ الْمَوْصُولِ، نَحْوُ: مَا رَأَيْتُ الَّذِي إِنَّهُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ، وَإِذَا كَانَ فِي خَبَرِهَا اللَّامُ، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَقَائِمٌ.
text.en: Know that inna with kasra on the hamza does not change the meaning of the sentence but emphasises it, while anna with fatḥa on the hamza, with what comes after it, has the rule of a single word. Therefore the kasra is necessary when it is at the beginning of speech, as inna Zaydan qāʾimun; after saying, as in His saying, exalted is He: yaqūlu innahā baqaratun “He says: it is a cow”; after the relative, as mā raʾaytu alladhī innahu fī al-masjidi “I did not see the one who is in the mosque”; and when the lām is in its khabar, as inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun “Zayd is surely standing”.

text.original: وَيَجِبُ الْفَتْحُ حَيْثُ يَقَعُ فَاعِلًا، نَحْوُ: بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ، وَحَيْثُ يَقَعُ مَفْعُولًا، نَحْوُ: كَرِهْتُ أَنَّكَ قَائِمٌ، وَحَيْثُ يَقَعُ مُبْتَدَأً، نَحْوُ: عِنْدِي أَنَّكَ قَائِمٌ، وَحَيْثُ يَقَعُ مُضَافًا إِلَيْهِ، نَحْوُ: عَجِبْتُ مِنْ طُولِ أَنَّ بَكْرًا قَائِمٌ، وَحَيْثُ يَقَعُ مَجْرُورًا، نَحْوُ: عَجِبْتُ مِنْ أَنَّ بَكْرًا قَائِمٌ، وَبَعْدَ لَوْ، نَحْوُ: لَوْ أَنَّكَ عِنْدَنَا لَأَكْرَمْتُكَ، وَبَعْدَ لَوْلَا، نَحْوُ: لَوْلَا أَنَّهُ حَاضِرٌ لَغَابَ زَيْدٌ.
text.en: The fatḥa is necessary where it stands as fāʿil, as balaghanī anna Zaydan qāʾimun “it has reached me that Zayd is standing”; where it stands as mafʿūl, as karihtu annaka qāʾimun “I disliked that you are standing”; where it stands as mubtadaʾ, as ʿindī annaka qāʾimun “with me [it is known] that you are standing”; where it stands as muḍāf ilayhi, as ʿajibtu min ṭūli anna Bakran qāʾimun “I wondered at how long Bakr is standing”; where it stands as majrūr, as ʿajibtu min anna Bakran qāʾimun “I wondered that Bakr is standing”; after law, as law annaka ʿindanā la-akramtuka “if you were with us, I would honour you”; and after lawlā, as lawlā annahu ḥāḍirun la-ghāba Zaydun “were it not that he is present, Zayd would have been absent”.

text.original: وَيَجُوزُ الْعَطْفُ عَلَى اسْمِ إِنَّ الْمَكْسُورَةِ بِالرَّفْعِ وَالنَّصْبِ بِاعْتِبَارِ الْمَحَلِّ وَاللَّفْظِ، مِثْلُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ وَعَمْرٌو، وَعَمْرًا. وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ إِنَّ الْمَكْسُورَةَ يَجُوزُ دُخُولُ اللَّامِ عَلَى خَبَرِهَا، وَقَدْ تُخَفَّفُ فَيَلْزَمُهَا اللَّامُ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَإِنْ كُلًّا لَمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ، وَحِينَئِذٍ يَجُوزُ إِلْغَاؤُهَا، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ. وَيَجُوزُ دُخُولُهَا عَلَى الْأَفْعَالِ الدَّاخِلَةِ عَلَى الْمُبْتَدَإِ وَالْخَبَرِ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ، وَإِنْ نَظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ.
text.en: Conjunction on the ism of inna with kasra is allowed with rafʿ and with naṣb, in regard to the place and to the wording, as inna Zaydan qāʾimun wa-ʿAmrun “Zayd is indeed standing, and ʿAmr”, and wa-ʿAmran. Know that the lām may come into the khabar of inna with kasra; it may be lightened, and then the lām is bound to it, as in His saying, exalted is He: wa-in kullan lammā la-yuwaffiyannahum “and indeed to each of them He will surely pay in full”; and then its cancelling is allowed, as in His saying, exalted is He: wa-in kullun lammā jamīʿun ladaynā muḥḍarūna “and indeed all of them will be brought before Us together”. It may come upon the verbs that come upon the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, as His saying, exalted is He: wa-in kunta min qablihi la-mina al-ghāfilīna “and before it you were indeed among the unaware” and wa-in naẓunnuka la-mina al-kādhibīna “and indeed we think you one of the liars”.

text.original: وَكَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الْمَفْتُوحَةُ قَدْ تُخَفَّفُ، فَحِينَئِذٍ يَجِبُ عَمَلُهَا فِي ضَمِيرِ شَأْنٍ مُقَدَّرٍ، فَتَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْجُمْلَةِ، اسْمِيَّةً كَانَتْ، نَحْوُ: بَلَغَنِي أَنْ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، أَوْ فِعْلِيَّةً، نَحْوُ: بَلَغَنِي أَنْ قَدْ قَامَ زَيْدٌ، وَيَجِبُ دُخُولُ السِّينِ أَوْ سَوْفَ أَوْ قَدْ أَوْ حَرْفِ النَّفْيِ عَلَى الْفِعْلِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: عَلِمَ أَنْ سَيَكُونُ مِنْكُمْ مَرْضَى، وَضَمِيرُ الشَّأْنِ الْمُسْتَتِرُ اسْمُ أَنْ، وَالْجُمْلَةُ خَبَرُهَا.
text.en: Likewise anna with fatḥa may be lightened; then it must govern an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and it comes upon the sentence, whether nominal, as balaghanī an Zaydun qāʾimun “it has reached me that Zayd is standing”, or verbal, as balaghanī an qad qāma Zaydun “it has reached me that Zayd has stood”; and the sīn, sawfa, qad or a particle of negation must come upon the verb, as in His saying, exalted is He: ʿalima an sa-yakūnu minkum marḍā “He knows that there will be sick ones among you”. The hidden pronoun of the matter is the ism of an, and the sentence is its khabar.

lessons.title: Kaʾanna, lākinna, layta and laʿalla
body: Kaʾanna is for likening: kaʾanna Zaydan al-asadu, “Zayd is as if the lion”. It is compounded of the kāf of likening and inna with kasra; its underlying form is inna Zaydan ka-al-asadi. The kāf was brought before inna, and so the hamza took the fatḥa, just as the hamza has the fatḥa after a particle of jarr (lesson 62). Lightened, it is cancelled: kaʾan Zaydun asadun, with both nouns in rafʿ.

Lākinna is for correcting a wrong impression (istidrāk). It stands between two utterances that differ in meaning: ghāba Zaydun lākinna Bakran ḥāḍirun, “Zayd was absent, but Bakr is present”. The wāw may come with it: qāma Zaydun wa-lākinna ʿAmran qāʿidun. Lightened, it is cancelled: mashā Zaydun lākin Bakrun ʿindanā.

Layta is for wishing (tamannī): layta Zaydan ʿindanā, “would that Zayd were with us”. Al-Farrāʾ, the Kūfan, allowed layta Zaydan qāʾiman, with both nouns in naṣb, taking layta in the meaning of the verb atamannā, “I wish”.

Laʿalla is for hoping (tarajjī), as in the verse uḥibbu al-ṣāliḥīna wa-lastu minhum, laʿalla Allāha yarzuqunī ṣalāḥā, “I love the righteous, though I am not of them; perhaps God will grant me righteousness”. Jarr by it is irregular: laʿalla Zaydin qāʾimun. The commentators separate the two: one may wish for what cannot be, but one hopes only for what may be.
Laʿalla has dialect forms: ʿalla, ʿanna, anna, laʾanna and laʿanna. According to al-Mubarrad its origin is ʿalla, to which the lām was added, and the others are branches.

terms.en: likening: the meaning of kaʾanna
correcting a wrong impression: the meaning of lākinna
wishing: the meaning of layta
hoping: the meaning of laʿalla
cancelling: a lightened particle no longer governs

examples.en: kaʾanna for likening
kaʾan lightened and cancelled
lākinna between two utterances that differ
layta for wishing
laʿalla for hoping

tasks.prompt: Give the underlying form of kaʾanna Zaydan al-asadu, and say why its hamza has a fatḥa.
tasks.answer: Inna Zaydan ka-al-asadi. The kāf of likening was brought before inna and joined to it; since the kāf comes before it, the hamza takes the fatḥa.

tasks.prompt: Parse both nouns in kaʾan Zaydun asadun.
tasks.answer: Kaʾan is lightened and cancelled, so it governs nothing. Zaydun is the mubtadaʾ in rafʿ; asadun is its khabar in rafʿ.

tasks.prompt: Why is lākinna in place in ghāba Zaydun lākinna Bakran ḥāḍirun, and why would it not be in place between “Zayd was absent” and “Bakr was absent”?
tasks.answer: Lākinna stands between two utterances that differ in meaning: absence and presence. Two utterances that agree, absent and absent, leave no wrong impression to correct, so lākinna has no place between them.

tasks.prompt: Who allowed layta Zaydan qāʾiman, and how is it explained? What is the usual form?
tasks.answer: Al-Farrāʾ allowed it, taking layta in the meaning of atamannā, “I wish”, so both nouns are in naṣb. The usual form puts the khabar in rafʿ: layta Zaydan qāʾimun.

tasks.prompt: Name the dialect forms of laʿalla, and the origin according to al-Mubarrad.
tasks.answer: ʿAlla, ʿanna, anna, laʾanna and laʿanna. Al-Mubarrad held that the origin is ʿalla, with the lām added, and that the others are branches.

quiz.prompt: Kaʾanna is compounded of…
options: the kāf and the lightened an
the kāf of likening and inna
quiz.explanation: Its underlying form is inna Zaydan ka-al-asadi.

quiz.prompt: The lightened kaʾan…
options: binds the lām to its khabar
governs a pronoun of the matter
quiz.explanation: Kaʾan Zaydun asadun, both nouns in rafʿ.

quiz.prompt: Lākinna stands between two utterances…
With lākinna the wāw is…
Layta is for…
quiz.explanation: Layta Zaydan ʿindanā, “would that Zayd were with us”.

quiz.prompt: Who allowed layta Zaydan qāʾiman?
quiz.explanation: He took layta in the meaning of atamannā, “I wish”.

quiz.prompt: Laʿalla Zaydin qāʾimun, with jarr, is…
quiz.explanation: The book says jarr by laʿalla is irregular (shādhdh).

text.original: وَكَأَنَّ لِلتَّشْبِيهِ، نَحْوُ: كَأَنَّ زَيْدًا الْأَسَدُ، وَهُوَ مُرَكَّبٌ مِنْ كَافِ التَّشْبِيهِ وَإِنَّ الْمَكْسُورَةِ، وَإِنَّمَا فُتِحَتْ لِتَقَدُّمِ الْكَافِ عَلَيْهَا، تَقْدِيرُهُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا كَالْأَسَدِ. وَقَدْ تُخَفَّفُ فَتُلْغَى، نَحْوُ: كَأَنْ زَيْدٌ أَسَدٌ.
text.en: Kaʾanna is for likening, as kaʾanna Zaydan al-asadu “Zayd is as if the lion”. It is compounded of the kāf of likening and inna with kasra; it was given a fatḥa only because the kāf comes before it; its underlying form is inna Zaydan ka-al-asadi “Zayd is like the lion”. It may be lightened and then cancelled, as kaʾan Zaydun asadun “Zayd is as if a lion”.

text.original: وَلَكِنَّ لِلِاسْتِدْرَاكِ، وَيَتَوَسَّطُ بَيْنَ كَلَامَيْنِ مُتَغَايِرَيْنِ فِي الْمَعْنَى، نَحْوُ: غَابَ زَيْدٌ لَكِنَّ بَكْرًا حَاضِرٌ، وَيَجُوزُ مَعَهَا الْوَاوُ، نَحْوُ: قَامَ زَيْدٌ وَلَكِنَّ عَمْرًا قَاعِدٌ، وَقَدْ تُخَفَّفُ فَتُلْغَى، نَحْوُ: مَشَى زَيْدٌ لَكِنْ بَكْرٌ عِنْدَنَا. وَلَيْتَ لِلتَّمَنِّي، نَحْوُ: لَيْتَ زَيْدًا عِنْدَنَا، وَأَجَازَ الْفَرَّاءُ: لَيْتَ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا، بِمَعْنَى أَتَمَنَّى.
text.en: Lākinna is for correcting [a wrong impression] (istidrāk); it stands between two utterances differing in meaning, as ghāba Zaydun lākinna Bakran ḥāḍirun “Zayd was absent, but Bakr is present”; the wāw is allowed with it, as qāma Zaydun wa-lākinna ʿAmran qāʿidun “Zayd stood, but ʿAmr is sitting”; it may be lightened and then cancelled, as mashā Zaydun lākin Bakrun ʿindanā “Zayd walked, but Bakr is with us”. Layta is for wishing, as layta Zaydan ʿindanā “would that Zayd were with us”; al-Farrāʾ allowed layta Zaydan qāʾiman, in the meaning of atamannā “I wish”.

text.original: وَلَعَلَّ لِلتَّرَجِّي، كَقَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ، شِعْرٌ: أُحِبُّ الصَّالِحِينَ وَلَسْتُ مِنْهُمْ * لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُنِي صَلَاحَا. وَشَذَّ الْجَرُّ بِهَا، نَحْوُ: لَعَلَّ زَيْدٍ قَائِمٌ. وَفِي لَعَلَّ لُغَاتٌ: عَلَّ، وَعَنَّ، وَأَنَّ، وَلَأَنَّ، وَلَعَنَّ، وَعِنْدَ الْمُبَرِّدِ أَصْلُهَا عَلَّ، زِيدَتْ فِيهِ اللَّامُ، وَالْبَوَاقِي فُرُوعٌ.
text.en: Laʿalla is for hoping, as in the poet's saying, verse: uḥibbu al-ṣāliḥīna wa-lastu minhum / laʿalla Allāha yarzuqunī ṣalāḥā “I love the righteous, though I am not of them; / perhaps God will grant me righteousness”. Jarr by it is irregular, as laʿalla Zaydin qāʾimun. In laʿalla there are dialect forms: ʿalla, ʿanna, anna, laʾanna and laʿanna; according to al-Mubarrad its origin is ʿalla, to which the lām was added, and the others are branches.

lessons.title: The particles of conjunction: the four of joining; immā and aw
body: The particles of conjunction are ten: the wāw, the fāʾ, thumma, ḥattā, immā, aw, am, lā, bal and lākin. The book sorts them by what they do with the judgement: four join, three give it to one of two things left vague, and three give it to one of two things determined (lesson 65).

The first four are for joining. The wāw joins absolutely, with no order: jāʾanī Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun, whether Zayd came first or ʿAmr. The fāʾ is for order without delay: qāma Zaydun fa-ʿAmrun, Zayd first and ʿAmr straight after. Thumma is for order with delay: dakhala Zaydun thumma ʿAmrun, Zayd first, and time between them.

Ḥattā is like thumma in order and delay, except that its delay is shorter. What it conjoins must be part of what it is conjoined to, and it shows strength in the conjoined, māta al-nāsu ḥattā al-anbiyāʾu, “the people died, even the prophets”, or weakness, qadima al-ḥājju ḥattā al-mushātu, “the pilgrims arrived, even those on foot”. The prophets are among the people, and those on foot among the pilgrims.
Immā, aw and am are for the judgement holding of one of two things, vaguely, not determined: marartu bi-rajulin awi imraʾatin, “I passed by a man or a woman”.

Immā is a particle of conjunction only when another immā comes before it: al-ʿadadu immā zawjun wa-immā fardun, “a number is either even or odd”; it is the second immā that conjoins. Immā may also come before aw: Zaydun immā kātibun aw ummiyyun, “Zayd is either one who writes or unlettered”.

terms.en: the ten particles of conjunction
joining absolutely, with no order: the wāw
order without delay: the fāʾ
order with delay: thumma, and ḥattā with a shorter delay
one of two things, left vague: immā, aw and am

examples.en: the wāw: joining with no order
the fāʾ: order without delay
ḥattā: the conjoined is part of the first, with strength
immā after another immā
immā before aw

tasks.prompt: Join Zayd and ʿAmr in jāʾa with the right particle: (a) the order is not stated; (b) Zayd came first and ʿAmr straight after; (c) Zayd came first and ʿAmr a long while later.
tasks.answer: (a) The wāw: jāʾa Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun. (b) The fāʾ: jāʾa Zaydun fa-ʿAmrun. (c) Thumma: jāʾa Zaydun thumma ʿAmrun.

tasks.prompt: Why is māta al-nāsu ḥattā al-anbiyāʾu sound, and what does ḥattā show in it?
tasks.answer: What ḥattā conjoins must be part of what it is conjoined to, and the prophets are part of the people. It shows strength in the conjoined: even they died.

tasks.prompt: In al-ʿadadu immā zawjun wa-immā fardun, which immā is the particle of conjunction?
tasks.answer: The second: immā is a particle of conjunction only when another immā comes before it.

tasks.prompt: Compare marartu bi-rajulin wa-imraʾatin with marartu bi-rajulin awi imraʾatin.
tasks.answer: With the wāw the passing holds of both, the man and the woman. With aw it holds of one of the two, left vague, not determined.

quiz.prompt: How many particles of conjunction does the book count?
quiz.explanation: The wāw, the fāʾ, thumma, ḥattā, immā, aw, am, lā, bal and lākin.

quiz.prompt: The wāw joins…
quiz.explanation: Jāʾanī Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun, whoever came first.

quiz.prompt: Qāma Zaydun fa-ʿAmrun means that ʿAmr stood…
quiz.explanation: The fāʾ is for order without delay.

quiz.prompt: Thumma is for…
What ḥattā conjoins must be…
options: part of what it is conjoined to
quiz.explanation: Māta al-nāsu ḥattā al-anbiyāʾu: the prophets are among the people.

quiz.prompt: Qadima al-ḥājju ḥattā al-mushātu shows…
quiz.explanation: Even those on foot, the weakest, arrived.

quiz.prompt: Immā is a particle of conjunction when…

text.original: فَصْلٌ: حُرُوفُ الْعَطْفِ عَشَرَةٌ: الْوَاوُ، وَالْفَاءُ، وَثُمَّ، وَحَتَّى، وَإِمَّا، وَأَوْ، وَأَمْ، وَلَا، وَبَلْ، وَلَكِنْ. فَالْأَرْبَعَةُ الْأُوَلُ لِلْجَمْعِ؛ فَالْوَاوُ لِلْجَمْعِ مُطْلَقًا، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ وَعَمْرٌو، سَوَاءٌ كَانَ زَيْدٌ مُتَقَدِّمًا فِي الْمَجِيءِ أَوْ عَمْرٌو. وَالْفَاءُ لِلتَّرْتِيبِ بِلَا مُهْلَةٍ، نَحْوُ: قَامَ زَيْدٌ فَعَمْرٌو، إِذَا كَانَ زَيْدٌ مُتَقَدِّمًا وَعَمْرٌو مُتَأَخِّرًا بِلَا مُهْلَةٍ.
text.en: Section. The particles of conjunction are ten: the wāw, the fāʾ, thumma, ḥattā, immā, aw, am, lā, bal and lākin. The first four are for joining. The wāw is for joining absolutely, as jāʾanī Zaydun wa-ʿAmrun “Zayd and ʿAmr came to me”, whether Zayd came first or ʿAmr. The fāʾ is for order without delay, as qāma Zaydun fa-ʿAmrun “Zayd stood, then ʿAmr”, when Zayd was first and ʿAmr after, without delay.

text.original: وَثُمَّ لِلتَّرْتِيبِ بِمُهْلَةٍ، نَحْوُ: دَخَلَ زَيْدٌ ثُمَّ عَمْرٌو، إِذَا كَانَ زَيْدٌ مُتَقَدِّمًا وَبَيْنَهُمَا مُهْلَةٌ. وَحَتَّى كَثُمَّ فِي التَّرْتِيبِ وَالْمُهْلَةِ، إِلَّا أَنَّ مُهْلَتَهَا أَقَلُّ مِنْ مُهْلَةِ ثُمَّ، وَيُشْتَرَطُ أَنْ يَكُونَ مَعْطُوفُهَا دَاخِلًا فِي الْمَعْطُوفِ عَلَيْهِ، وَهِيَ تُفِيدُ قُوَّةً فِي الْمَعْطُوفِ، نَحْوُ: مَاتَ النَّاسُ حَتَّى الْأَنْبِيَاءُ، أَوْ ضَعْفًا، نَحْوُ: قَدِمَ الْحَاجُّ حَتَّى الْمُشَاةُ.
text.en: Thumma is for order with delay, as dakhala Zaydun thumma ʿAmrun “Zayd entered, then [later] ʿAmr”, when Zayd was first and between them there was a delay. Ḥattā is like thumma in order and delay, except that its delay is less than the delay of thumma; it is a condition that what it conjoins is included in what it is conjoined to, and it shows strength in the conjoined word, as māta al-nāsu ḥattā al-anbiyāʾu “the people died, even the prophets”, or weakness, as qadima al-ḥājju ḥattā al-mushātu “the pilgrims arrived, even those on foot”.

text.original: وَإِمَّا وَأَوْ وَأَمْ، هَذِهِ الثَّلَاثَةُ لِثُبُوتِ الْحُكْمِ لِأَحَدِ الْأَمْرَيْنِ مُبْهَمًا لَا بِعَيْنِهِ، نَحْوُ: مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ أَوِ امْرَأَةٍ. وَإِمَّا إِنَّمَا تَكُونُ حَرْفَ الْعَطْفِ إِذَا تَقَدَّمَتْهَا إِمَّا أُخْرَى، نَحْوُ: الْعَدَدُ إِمَّا زَوْجٌ وَإِمَّا فَرْدٌ، وَيَجُوزُ أَنْ تَتَقَدَّمَ إِمَّا عَلَى أَوْ، نَحْوُ: زَيْدٌ إِمَّا كَاتِبٌ أَوْ أُمِّيٌّ.
text.en: Immā, aw and am: these three are for the judgement holding of one of two things, vaguely, not determined, as marartu bi-rajulin awi imraʾatin “I passed by a man or a woman”. Immā is a particle of conjunction only when another immā comes before it, as al-ʿadadu immā zawjun wa-immā fardun “a number is either even or odd”; immā may come before aw, as Zaydun immā kātibun aw ummiyyun “Zayd is either one who writes or unlettered”.

lessons.title: Am, connected and disconnected; lā, bal and lākin
body: Am is of two kinds. The connected am (muttaṣila) asks to determine one of two things: the one asking knows that one of them holds, vaguely, and asks which. With aw and immā the one asking does not know that either of them holds at all.

The connected am has three conditions. First, a hamza stands before it: a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun, “is Zayd with you, or ʿAmr?”. Second, what follows am is like what follows the hamza: a noun after the hamza and a noun after am, as there; a verb after each, a-qāma Zaydun am qaʿada, “did Zayd stand, or sit?”. So one does not say a-raʾayta Zaydan am ʿAmran, with a verb after the hamza and a noun after am.

Third, one of the two equal things is certain, and the question is only about which it is. So the answer to am must be by determining, not by yes or no: to a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun one answers by naming one of them. A question with aw or immā is answered by yes or no.

The disconnected am (munqaṭiʿa) is in the meaning of bal with the hamza. You see a figure from afar and say innahā la-ibilun, “they are surely camels”, as one certain; then doubt comes to you that it is a sheep, and you say am hiya shātun, turning away from the first report and beginning anew with a question: bal a-hiya shātun, “rather, is it a sheep?”. It is used in the report, as here, and in the question: a-ʿindaka Zaydun am ʿAmrun, where you asked first whether Zayd is with him, then turned away from that question and took up asking about ʿAmr.

Lā, bal and lākin give the judgement to one of two things, determined. Lā denies of the second what held of the first: jāʾanī Zaydun lā ʿAmrun. Bal is for turning away from the first and affirming of the second: jāʾanī Zaydun bal ʿAmrun, meaning bal jāʾanī ʿAmrun. After a negation the book reads it so: mā jāʾa Bakrun bal Khālidun, meaning bal mā jāʾa Khālidun.

Lākin is for correcting a wrong impression, and a negation must come with it, before it, mā jāʾanī Zaydun lākin ʿAmrun jāʾa, “Zayd did not come to me, but ʿAmr came”, or after it, qāma Bakrun lākin Khālidun lam yaqum, “Bakr stood, but Khālid did not stand”.

terms.en: the connected am: asks which of two things, one of which is known to hold
the disconnected am: in the meaning of bal with the hamza
determining: the answer to the connected am
turning away from the first: the meaning of bal
one of two things, determined: lā, bal and lākin

examples.en: the connected am, with the hamza before it
a verb after the hamza and a verb after am
the disconnected am: bal a-hiya shātun
lā: denied of the second
bal: turning away from the first

tasks.prompt: Connected or disconnected? (a) a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun, asked by one who knows that one of them is with you; (b) innahā la-ibilun, then am hiya shātun.
tasks.answer: (a) Connected: a hamza stands before it, a noun follows each, and one of the two is known to be with you; the question asks which. (b) Disconnected: it means bal a-hiya shātun, turning away from the first report to a new question.

tasks.prompt: Why does the book reject a-raʾayta Zaydan am ʿAmran?
tasks.answer: After the hamza comes a verb, raʾayta, but after am comes a noun, ʿAmran. The connected am needs the same kind after both: a noun after each, as in a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun, or a verb after each, as in a-qāma Zaydun am qaʿada.

tasks.prompt: How is a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun answered, and how a question with aw?
tasks.answer: The question with am is answered by determining, naming Zayd or ʿAmr: the asker already knows that one of them is with you. A question with aw or immā is answered by yes or no, since the asker does not know whether either is.

tasks.prompt: Give the meaning of jāʾanī Zaydun bal ʿAmrun, and of mā jāʾa Bakrun bal Khālidun, as the book gives them.
tasks.answer: Jāʾanī Zaydun bal ʿAmrun means bal jāʾanī ʿAmrun: turning away from Zayd and affirming the coming of ʿAmr. Mā jāʾa Bakrun bal Khālidun the book reads as bal mā jāʾa Khālidun.

tasks.prompt: Lākin needs a negation. Where is it in mā jāʾanī Zaydun lākin ʿAmrun jāʾa, and in qāma Bakrun lākin Khālidun lam yaqum?
tasks.answer: In the first the negation, mā, comes before lākin. In the second it comes after it: lam yaqum.

quiz.prompt: One who asks with the connected am…
options: does not know that either holds
knows that one of the two holds
quiz.explanation: He asks only which one: a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun.

quiz.prompt: Before the connected am there must be…
A-raʾayta Zaydan am ʿAmran is rejected because…
options: a verb follows the hamza but a noun follows am
quiz.explanation: What follows am must be like what follows the hamza.

quiz.prompt: The connected am is answered by…
quiz.explanation: Aw and immā are the ones answered by yes or no.

quiz.prompt: The disconnected am is in the meaning of…
quiz.explanation: Am hiya shātun means bal a-hiya shātun.

quiz.prompt: In jāʾanī Zaydun lā ʿAmrun, lā…
options: denies of ʿAmr what held of Zayd
quiz.explanation: Lā is for denying of the second what held of the first.

quiz.prompt: Lākin as a particle of conjunction needs…
options: a negation before or after it
quiz.explanation: Mā jāʾanī Zaydun lākin ʿAmrun jāʾa; qāma Bakrun lākin Khālidun lam yaqum.

text.original: وَأَمْ عَلَى قِسْمَيْنِ: مُتَّصِلَةٌ، وَهِيَ مَا يُسْأَلُ بِهَا عَنْ تَعْيِينِ أَحَدِ الْأَمْرَيْنِ، وَالسَّائِلُ بِهَا يَعْلَمُ ثُبُوتَ أَحَدِهِمَا مُبْهَمًا، بِخِلَافِ أَوْ وَإِمَّا؛ فَإِنَّ السَّائِلَ بِهِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ ثُبُوتَ أَحَدِهِمَا أَصْلًا. وَتُسْتَعْمَلُ بِثَلَاثَةِ شَرَائِطَ: الْأَوَّلُ أَنْ يَقَعَ قَبْلَهَا هَمْزَةٌ، نَحْوُ: أَزَيْدٌ عِنْدَكَ أَمْ عَمْرٌو.
text.en: Am is of two kinds. Connected (muttaṣila), which is that by which one asks to determine one of two things, the one asking with it knowing that one of the two holds, vaguely — unlike aw and immā, for one who asks with them does not know that either of them holds at all. It is used under three conditions. The first: that a hamza stands before it, as a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun “is Zayd with you, or ʿAmr?”.

text.original: وَالثَّانِي أَنْ يَلِيَهَا لَفْظٌ مِثْلُ مَا يَلِي الْهَمْزَةَ، أَعْنِي إِنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ الْهَمْزَةِ اسْمٌ فَكَذَلِكَ بَعْدَ أَمْ، كَمَا مَرَّ، وَإِنْ كَانَ بَعْدَ الْهَمْزَةِ فِعْلٌ فَكَذَلِكَ بَعْدَهَا، نَحْوُ: أَقَامَ زَيْدٌ أَمْ قَعَدَ، فَلَا يُقَالُ: أَرَأَيْتَ زَيْدًا أَمْ عَمْرًا.
text.en: The second: that the word that follows it is like the word that follows the hamza; I mean, if after the hamza there is a noun, so too after am, as has passed; and if after the hamza there is a verb, so too after it, as a-qāma Zaydun am qaʿada “did Zayd stand, or sit?”; so one does not say a-raʾayta Zaydan am ʿAmran.

text.original: وَالثَّالِثُ أَنْ يَكُونَ أَحَدُ الْأَمْرَيْنِ الْمُسْتَوِيَيْنِ مُحَقَّقًا، وَإِنَّمَا يَكُونُ الِاسْتِفْهَامُ عَنِ التَّعْيِينِ؛ فَلِذَلِكَ يَجِبُ أَنْ يَكُونَ جَوَابُ أَمْ بِالتَّعْيِينِ دُونَ نَعَمْ أَوْ لَا، فَإِذَا قِيلَ: أَزَيْدٌ عِنْدَكَ أَمْ عَمْرٌو، فَجَوَابُهُ بِتَعْيِينِ أَحَدِهِمَا، أَمَّا إِذَا سُئِلَ بِأَوْ وَإِمَّا فَجَوَابُهُ بِنَعَمْ أَوْ لَا.
text.en: The third: that one of the two equal things is certain, and the question is only about determining it; therefore the answer to am must be by determining, not by yes or no: when it is said a-Zaydun ʿindaka am ʿAmrun, its answer is by determining one of them; but when one asks with aw and immā, the answer is by yes or no.

text.original: وَمُنْقَطِعَةٌ، وَهِيَ مَا تَكُونُ بِمَعْنَى بَلْ مَعَ الْهَمْزَةِ، كَمَا رَأَيْتَ شَبَحًا مِنْ بَعِيدٍ قُلْتَ: إِنَّهَا لَإِبِلٌ، عَلَى سَبِيلِ الْقَطْعِ، ثُمَّ حَصَلَ لَكَ الشَّكُّ أَنَّهَا شَاةٌ، فَقُلْتَ: أَمْ هِيَ شَاةٌ، تَقْصِدُ الْإِعْرَاضَ عَنِ الْإِخْبَارِ الْأَوَّلِ، وَالِاسْتِئْنَافَ بِسُؤَالٍ آخَرَ، مَعْنَاهُ: بَلْ أَهِيَ شَاةٌ.
text.en: And disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), which is in the meaning of bal with the hamza: as when you see a figure from afar and say innahā la-ibilun “they are surely camels”, by way of certainty, then doubt comes to you that it is a sheep, and you say am hiya shātun “or is it a sheep?”, intending to turn away from the first report and to begin anew with another question; its meaning is bal a-hiya shātun “rather, is it a sheep?”.

text.original: وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ أَمِ الْمُنْقَطِعَةَ لَا تُسْتَعْمَلُ إِلَّا فِي الْخَبَرِ، كَمَا مَرَّ، وَفِي الِاسْتِفْهَامِ، نَحْوُ: أَعِنْدَكَ زَيْدٌ أَمْ عَمْرٌو، سَأَلْتَ أَوَّلًا عَنْ حُصُولِ زَيْدٍ عِنْدَهُ، ثُمَّ أَضْرَبْتَ عَنِ السُّؤَالِ الْأَوَّلِ، وَأَخَذْتَ فِي السُّؤَالِ عَنْ حُصُولِ عَمْرٍو.
text.en: Know that the disconnected am is used only in the report, as has passed, and in the question, as a-ʿindaka Zaydun am ʿAmrun “is Zayd with you? Or ʿAmr?”: you asked first about Zayd's being with him, then turned away from the first question and took up asking about ʿAmr's being [with him].

text.original: وَلَا وَبَلْ وَلَكِنْ جَمِيعُهَا لِثُبُوتِ الْحُكْمِ لِأَحَدِ الْأَمْرَيْنِ مُعَيَّنًا. أَمَّا لَا فَلِنَفْيِ مَا وَجَبَ لِلْأَوَّلِ عَنِ الثَّانِي، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ لَا عَمْرٌو. وَبَلْ لِلْإِضْرَابِ عَنِ الْأَوَّلِ وَالْإِثْبَاتِ لِلثَّانِي، نَحْوُ: جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ بَلْ عَمْرٌو، وَمَعْنَاهُ: بَلْ جَاءَنِي عَمْرٌو، وَمَا جَاءَ بَكْرٌ بَلْ خَالِدٌ، مَعْنَاهُ: بَلْ مَا جَاءَ خَالِدٌ. وَلَكِنْ لِلِاسْتِدْرَاكِ، وَيَلْزَمُهَا النَّفْيُ قَبْلَهَا، نَحْوُ: مَا جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ لَكِنْ عَمْرٌو جَاءَ، أَوْ بَعْدَهَا، نَحْوُ: قَامَ بَكْرٌ لَكِنْ خَالِدٌ لَمْ يَقُمْ.
text.en: Lā, bal and lākin: all of them are for the judgement holding of one of two things, determined. Lā is for denying of the second what held of the first, as jāʾanī Zaydun lā ʿAmrun “Zayd came to me, not ʿAmr”. Bal is for turning away from the first and affirming of the second, as jāʾanī Zaydun bal ʿAmrun “Zayd came to me — no, ʿAmr”, meaning bal jāʾanī ʿAmrun “rather, ʿAmr came to me”; and mā jāʾa Bakrun bal Khālidun “Bakr did not come — no, Khālid”, meaning bal mā jāʾa Khālidun “rather, Khālid did not come”. Lākin is for correcting [a wrong impression], and a negation must be before it, as mā jāʾanī Zaydun lākin ʿAmrun jāʾa “Zayd did not come to me, but ʿAmr came”, or after it, as qāma Bakrun lākin Khālidun lam yaqum “Bakr stood, but Khālid did not stand”.

lessons.title: Calling attention, the vocative, and affirmation
body: The particles of calling attention (tanbīh) are three: alā, amā and hā. They are laid down to alert the one addressed, lest anything of the speech escape him. Alā and amā come only upon a sentence: nominal, alā innahum humu al-mufsidūna (Q 2:12), “truly, it is they who are the corrupters”, and in the verse amā wa-alladhī abkā wa-aḍḥaka…; or verbal, alā lā tafʿal, amā lā taḍrib.
Hā comes upon the nominal sentence, hā Zaydun qāʾimun, “lo, Zayd is standing”, and upon the single word: hādhā, hāʾulāʾi, the hā at the head of the demonstratives (lesson 32).

The particles of the vocative are five: yā, ayā, hayā, ay and the hamza with fatḥa. Ay and the hamza are for the near, ayā and hayā for the far, and yā for both and for the middle. The rules of the munādā have come before (lesson 18).

The particles of affirmation (ījāb) are six: naʿam, balā, ī, ajal, jayri and inna. Naʿam confirms what was said before, affirmative or negative: to jāʾa Zaydun? you say naʿam, and to amā jāʾa Zaydun?, “has Zayd not come?”, you say naʿam, confirming that he has not.

Balā is only for affirming what has been denied, in a question, a-lastu bi-rabbikum qālū balā (Q 7:172), “Am I not your Lord? They said: yes indeed”, or in a report: to lam yaqum Zaydun you say balā, that is, qad qāma. The commentators draw the lesson from the verse: naʿam there would have confirmed the denial. Ī is for affirming after a question and is bound to the oath: hal kāna kadhā? ī wa-Allāhi. Ajal, jayri and inna confirm a report: to jāʾa Zaydun you say ajal, jayri or inna, “I believe you in this report”.

terms.en: the particles of calling attention: alā, amā, hā
the five particles of the vocative
the six particles of affirmation
confirms what was said before, affirmative or negative
affirms only what has been denied

examples.en: alā upon a nominal sentence (Q 2:12)
hā upon a nominal sentence
balā after a denial in a question (Q 7:172)
ī with the oath bound to it

tasks.prompt: Which particles of the vocative may call (a) one near you, (b) one far away, (c) one at a middle distance?
tasks.answer: (a) Ay or the hamza, and also yā. (b) Ayā or hayā, and also yā. (c) Yā.

tasks.prompt: Someone says lam yaqum Zaydun, and you know that he did stand. Answer with one particle, and say what it means.
tasks.answer: Balā, that is, qad qāma, “yes, he has stood”: balā affirms what has been denied. Naʿam would confirm the denial.

tasks.prompt: Why does the verse have balā, and not naʿam, after a-lastu bi-rabbikum?
tasks.answer: The question is negative: “am I not your Lord?”. Naʿam confirms what came before, so it would confirm the negation. Balā affirms what was denied: “yes, You are our Lord”.

tasks.prompt: Answer hal kāna kadhā? in the affirmative with ī, and confirm the report jāʾa Zaydun in three ways.
tasks.answer: Ī wa-Allāhi: ī comes after a question, and the oath is bound to it. To confirm the report: ajal, or jayri, or inna.

tasks.prompt: Where may hā stand that alā and amā may not?
tasks.answer: Upon a single word, as in hādhā and hāʾulāʾi. Alā and amā come only upon a sentence, nominal or verbal.

quiz.prompt: Alā and amā come upon…
quiz.explanation: Alā innahum humu al-mufsidūna; alā lā tafʿal.

quiz.prompt: Hā may come upon…
options: a nominal sentence or a single word

quiz.prompt: Ayā and hayā are for calling…
quiz.explanation: Ay and the hamza are for the near; yā for all three.

quiz.prompt: Which particle of the vocative serves the near, the far and the middle?
quiz.explanation: The book: yā is for both and for the middle.

quiz.prompt: Naʿam…
options: confirms what came before, affirmative or negative
quiz.explanation: Amā jāʾa Zaydun? Naʿam: he has not come.

quiz.prompt: To lam yaqum Zaydun the answer balā means…
Which particle of affirmation is bound to an oath?

text.original: فَصْلٌ: حُرُوفُ التَّنْبِيهِ ثَلَاثَةٌ: أَلَا، وَأَمَا، وَهَا؛ وُضِعَتْ لِتَنْبِيهِ الْمُخَاطَبِ لِئَلَّا يَفُوتَهُ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ. فَأَلَا وَأَمَا لَا تَدْخُلَانِ إِلَّا عَلَى الْجُمْلَةِ، اسْمِيَّةً كَانَتْ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْمُفْسِدُونَ، وَقَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ، شِعْرٌ: أَمَا وَالَّذِي أَبْكَى وَأَضْحَكَ وَالَّذِي * أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا وَالَّذِي أَمْرُهُ الْأَمْرُ، أَوْ فِعْلِيَّةً، نَحْوُ: أَلَا لَا تَفْعَلْ، وَأَمَا لَا تَضْرِبْ. وَالثَّالِثُ تَدْخُلُ عَلَى الْجُمْلَةِ الِاسْمِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: هَا زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ، وَالْمُفْرَدِ، نَحْوُ: هَذَا، وَهَؤُلَاءِ.
text.en: Section. The particles of calling attention (tanbīh) are three: alā, amā and hā; they are laid down to alert the one addressed, lest anything of the speech escape him. Alā and amā come only upon a sentence, whether nominal, as in His saying, exalted is He: alā innahum humu al-mufsidūna “truly, it is they who are the corrupters”, and in the poet's saying, verse: amā wa-alladhī abkā wa-aḍḥaka wa-alladhī / amāta wa-aḥyā wa-alladhī amruhu al-amru “Lo, by Him who made weep and made laugh, and who / made die and gave life, and whose command is the command”; or verbal, as alā lā tafʿal “lo, do not do [it]” and wa-amā lā taḍrib “and lo, do not hit”. The third comes upon the nominal sentence, as hā Zaydun qāʾimun “lo, Zayd is standing”, and upon the single word, as hādhā and wa-hāʾulāʾi.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: حُرُوفُ النِّدَاءِ خَمْسَةٌ: يَا، وَأَيَا، وَهَيَا، وَأَيْ، وَالْهَمْزَةُ الْمَفْتُوحَةُ. فَأَيْ وَالْهَمْزَةُ لِلْقَرِيبِ، وَأَيَا وَهَيَا لِلْبَعِيدِ، وَيَا لَهُمَا وَلِلْمُتَوَسِّطِ، وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ أَحْكَامُ الْمُنَادَى.
text.en: Section. The particles of the vocative are five: yā, ayā, hayā, ay and the hamza with fatḥa. Ay and the hamza are for the near, ayā and hayā for the far, and yā for both and for the middle; the rules of the munādā have come before.

text.original: فَصْلٌ: حُرُوفُ الْإِيجَابِ سِتَّةٌ: نَعَمْ، وَبَلَى، وَإِي، وَأَجَلْ، وَجَيْرِ، وَإِنَّ. أَمَّا نَعَمْ فَلِتَقْرِيرِ كَلَامٍ سَابِقٍ، مُثْبَتًا كَانَ أَوْ مَنْفِيًّا، نَحْوُ: جَاءَ زَيْدٌ؟ قُلْتَ: نَعَمْ، وَأَمَا جَاءَ زَيْدٌ؟ قُلْتَ: نَعَمْ. وَبَلَى تَخْتَصُّ بِإِيجَابِ مَا نُفِيَ، اسْتِفْهَامًا، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا بَلَى، وَخَبَرًا، كَمَا يُقَالُ: لَمْ يَقُمْ زَيْدٌ، قُلْتَ: بَلَى، أَيْ قَدْ قَامَ.
text.en: Section. The particles of affirmation are six: naʿam, balā, ī, ajal, jayri and inna. Naʿam is for confirming a preceding utterance, whether affirmative or negative, as [one asks] jāʾa Zaydun “has Zayd come?”, and you say naʿam “yes”; and amā jāʾa Zaydun “has Zayd not come?”, and you say naʿam. Balā belongs to affirming what has been denied, in a question, as in His saying, exalted is He: a-lastu bi-rabbikum qālū balā “Am I not your Lord? They said: yes indeed”, and in a report, as when it is said lam yaqum Zaydun “Zayd did not stand”, and you say balā “yes, he did”, that is, qad qāma “he has stood”.

text.original: وَإِي لِلْإِثْبَاتِ بَعْدَ الِاسْتِفْهَامِ، وَيَلْزَمُهَا الْقَسَمُ، كَمَا إِذَا قِيلَ: هَلْ كَانَ كَذَا؟ قُلْتَ: إِي وَاللَّهِ. وَأَجَلْ وَجَيْرِ وَإِنَّ لِتَصْدِيقِ الْخَبَرِ، كَمَا إِذَا قِيلَ: جَاءَ زَيْدٌ، قُلْتَ: أَجَلْ، أَوْ جَيْرِ، أَوْ إِنَّ، أَيْ أُصَدِّقُكَ فِي هَذَا الْخَبَرِ.
text.en: Ī is for affirming after a question, and the oath is bound to it, as when it is said hal kāna kadhā “was it so?”, and you say ī wa-Allāhi “yes, by God”. Ajal, jayri and inna are for confirming a report, as when it is said jāʾa Zaydun “Zayd has come”, and you say ajal, or jayri, or inna, that is, uṣaddiquka fī hādhā al-khabari “I believe you in this report”.

lessons.title: The additional particles; explanation; the maṣdar
body: The additional particles are seven: in, an, mā, lā, min, the bāʾ and the lām. In is added with the negating mā, mā in Zaydun qāʾimun; with the mā of the maṣdar, intaẓir mā in yajlisu al-amīru, “wait as long as the prince sits”; and with lammā, lammā in jalasta jalastu. An is added with lammā, fa-lammā an jāʾa al-bashīru (Q 12:96), and between law and an oath put before it: wa-Allāhi an law qumta qumtu.

Mā is added with the conditional idhā, matā, ayy, annā, ayna and in: idhā mā ṣumta ṣumtu, “when you fast, I fast”, and likewise the rest; and after some particles of jarr: fa-bi-mā raḥmatin mina Allāhi (Q 3:159), ʿammā qalīlin la-yuṣbiḥunna nādimīna (Q 23:40), mimmā khaṭīʾātihim ughriqū (Q 71:25), and Zaydun ṣadīqī ka-mā anna ʿAmran akhī.

Lā is added with the wāw after a negation, mā jāʾanī Zaydun wa-lā ʿAmrun; after the an of the maṣdar, mā manaʿaka an lā tasjuda (Q 7:12), “what prevented you from prostrating?”; and before the oath, lā uqsimu bi-hādhā al-baladi (Q 90:1), in the meaning of uqsimu, “I swear”. Min, the bāʾ and the lām were met among the particles of jarr (lessons 57–59), “so we do not repeat them”.

The two particles of explanation (tafsīr) are ay and an. Ay: wa-isʾali al-qaryata (Q 12:82), ay ahla al-qaryati, “that is, the people of the town”, as if you explained the town by its people. With an only a verb in the meaning of saying is explained: wa-nādaynāhu an yā Ibrāhīmu (Q 37:104), “We called to him: O Ibrāhīm”, calling being a kind of saying. One does not say qultu lahu ani uktub, for there the word of saying itself is mentioned, not its meaning.

The particles of the maṣdar are three: mā, an and anna. Mā and an are for the verbal sentence: wa-ḍāqat ʿalayhimu al-arḍu bi-mā raḥubat (Q 9:118), that is, bi-ruḥbihā, “for all its breadth”; the verse yasurru al-marʾa mā dhahaba al-layālī, “it pleases a man that the nights go by”; and fa-mā kāna jawāba qawmihi illā an qālū (Q 27:56), that is, qawluhum, “their saying”. Anna is for the nominal sentence: ʿalimtu annaka qāʾimun, that is, qiyāmaka, “your standing”.

terms.en: the seven additional particles
the two particles of explanation: ay and an
mā, an and anna, which turn what follows into a maṣdar
the mā of the maṣdar: bi-mā raḥubat, that is, bi-ruḥbihā
the explaining an, after a verb in the meaning of saying

examples.en: an added with lammā (Q 12:96)
mā added after a particle of jarr (Q 3:159)
lā added before the oath (Q 90:1)
an explaining a verb in the meaning of saying (Q 37:104)
anna of the maṣdar: qiyāmaka
